Roll thin, cut into strips or diamond shapes
Twist into decorative shapes
Deep fry until golden
Dust with powdered sugar

recipes.name: Khur-le
recipes.description: Sweet buckwheat pancake — a simple treat from Bumthang, where buckwheat grows at high altitude.
instructions: Mix buckwheat flour with water and sugar to thin batter
Add cardamom
Fry in butter like a thick pancake
Fold or roll and serve warm

recipes.name: Suja
recipes.description: Salty, buttery tea — Bhutan's most important daily drink.
ingredients: 2 tbsp yak butter or regular butter
instructions: Boil water with tea leaves 5 min
Strain into churn or blender
Add butter, milk, and salt
Churn or blend until frothy
Serve hot

recipes.name: Ara
recipes.description: Traditional Bhutanese fermented rice wine.
instructions: Cook rice, cool to warm
Crumble yeast cake over rice, mix
Pack into container, seal loosely
Ferment 7-14 days
Strain liquid
Serve warm or at room temperature

recipes.name: Suja
recipes.description: Salted yak butter tea — the essential Bhutanese drink at every altitude. Warming, fatty, sustaining for mountain life.
instructions: Brew strong black tea
Add to churning vessel (or blender)
Add yak butter and salt
Churn until emulsified and frothy
Serve in wooden cups, refilling constantly

recipes.name: Salteñas
recipes.description: Bolivia's beloved morning pastry — juicy, spiced meat in golden dough.
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, sugar, annatto-infused oil, egg, water
Filling: 300g beef (diced small), 2 potatoes (diced), 1 cup peas, 1 onion, hardboiled egg, olives, cumin, aji pepper, gelatin broth
instructions: Make dough with annatto oil for golden color, chill
Cook filling: sauté beef, onions, add potatoes, peas, spices
Add gelatin broth so filling sets when cold
Chill filling until firm
Fill dough circles, crimp edges into decorative ridge
Bake at 220°C 25 min until golden

recipes.name: Api con Pastel
recipes.full_name: Api con Pastel (Purple Corn Drink with Pastry)
recipes.description: Hot purple corn drink paired with fried cheese pastries.
instructions: Boil purple corn in water with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel 30 min
Strain, sweeten to taste
Make pastry dough, fill with cheese
Fry pastries until golden
Serve hot api alongside cheese pastels

recipes.name: Api con Pastel
recipes.full_name: Api con Pastel (Purple Corn Drink with Pastry)
recipes.description: Hot purple corn drink with fried cheese pastries — the classic Bolivian street breakfast, especially in La Paz's cold mornings.
ingredients: Api: 2 cups purple corn flour, cinnamon, cloves, orange peel, sugar, water
Pastel: flour, cheese filling, oil for frying
instructions: For api: simmer purple corn flour with water, cinnamon, cloves, orange peel
Stir until thick and fragrant
Sweeten with sugar
For pastel: make simple dough, fill with cheese
Fry pastels until golden
Serve hot api alongside warm pastels

recipes.name: Pique Macho
recipes.description: A towering platter of beef, sausage, fries, and peppers.
instructions: Fry potato cubes until golden
Sear beef cubes in hot oil
Fry hot dog slices
Layer on platter: fries, beef, hot dogs
Top with tomato, onion, locoto peppers, egg slices
Season with cumin and salt

recipes.name: Sopa de Maní
recipes.description: Creamy peanut soup with beef — a Cochabamba specialty.
instructions: Brown beef ribs, cover with water, simmer 30 min
Blend peanuts to smooth paste
Add peanut paste to broth
Add potatoes, carrots, onion, garlic, spices
Simmer until vegetables tender
Serve topped with crispy fried pasta noodles

recipes.name: Sopa de Maní
recipes.description: Creamy peanut soup — Bolivia's most beloved soup, rich and deeply nutty. Served across the country for almuerzo (lunch).
instructions: Brown meat, set aside
Sauté onion and tomato, add cumin
Add water, return meat, simmer 20 min
Add potatoes, cook 10 min
Add ground peanuts dissolved in broth — stir to prevent lumps
Add pasta, cook 8 min
Garnish with parsley and fried potato strips

recipes.name: Silpancho
recipes.description: A layered plate of rice, potatoes, breaded beef, and a fried egg.
instructions: Pound beef very thin, bread and fry
Fry potato slices
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Layer on plate: rice, fried potatoes, breaded beef, fried egg
Top with fresh salsa of tomato, onion, locoto, parsley

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Poshista2 assumed (based on copyright claims).

recipes.name: Fricasé
recipes.description: A hearty, spicy pork and hominy stew.
instructions: Brown pork pieces
Blend onions, garlic, aji paste
Add to pork with cumin, oregano, water
Simmer with hominy 60 min
Add chuño, cook 30 more min
Serve with bread

recipes.name: Pique a lo Macho
recipes.description: A macho pile of seared beef, hot dogs, peppers, and fried potatoes — Cochabamba's famous feast dish, always shared.
instructions: Fry potatoes into thick chips, set aside
Sear beef slices quickly over high heat
Add hot dogs, onion, tomato, locotos
Toss together with cumin and salt
Pile on top of fried potatoes
Garnish with hard-boiled egg quarters
Serve on a big shared plate

recipes.name: Anticuchos
recipes.description: Char-grilled beef heart skewers — Andean street food.
instructions: Trim and cube beef heart
Marinate in aji panca, cumin, garlic, vinegar 2+ hours
Thread onto skewers
Grill over high heat, basting with marinade
Serve with boiled potatoes and aji sauce

recipes.name: Tucumanas
recipes.description: Bolivian fried empanadas from Sucre — crunchier and richer than their baked cousins, always with llajwa.
ingredients: Filling: chicken or beef, potato, peas, hard-boiled egg, olive, cumin, ají
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Prepare filling: cook seasoned meat with potato, peas, cumin
Roll dough circles, fill with meat mixture, egg slice, olive
Fold into half-moon, seal edges tightly
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve with llajwa (tomato-locoto salsa)

recipes.name: Salteñas
recipes.description: Bolivia's morning obsession — a sweet-dough empanada with a juicy, soupy filling held together by gelatin that melts when baked. You eat it by biting a corner and sipping the broth first. Called 'South America's soup dumpling,' salteña-eating technique videos are viral content gold.
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, sugar, ají amarillo powder (for color), butter, egg, warm water
Filling: beef or chicken (diced small), potatoes (diced), peas, hard-boiled egg (chopped)
Jigote sauce: ají amarillo paste, onion, cumin, gelatin, beef broth
instructions: Make jigote: cook onion, ají paste, cumin, add broth and gelatin, fold in meat and vegetables
Refrigerate filling until set — the gelatin is essential, it melts into juicy broth when baked
Make dough with flour, sugar, ají powder, butter, egg — it must be slightly sweet
Roll out, cut circles, fill generously
Crimp the seal into a rope pattern along the top — this must hold or juice leaks
Bake at 220°C for 20-25 min until golden with a sweet, slightly charred crust
Eat immediately — bite corner, sip the broth, then eat
The broth-inside-pastry concept is what makes these viral — South America's soup dumpling

recipes.name: Tawa-Tawas
recipes.description: Crispy fried dough spirals drizzled with honey.
instructions: Mix dough with flour, eggs, butter, sugar, zest, anise
Rest 20 min
Roll thin, cut into strips
Shape into spirals
Deep fry until golden
Drizzle with honey or cane syrup

recipes.name: Tawa-Tawas
recipes.description: Spiral-shaped fried dough scented with anise and cinnamon — sold at Bolivian festivals and street corners.
instructions: Mix flour, egg, sugar, anise, cinnamon, orange zest
Knead into smooth dough
Roll into long ropes, coil into spiral shapes
Deep fry until golden
Drizzle with honey or cane syrup

recipes.name: Api Morado
recipes.description: Hot, thick purple corn drink — a La Paz morning ritual.
instructions: Boil purple corn with cinnamon, cloves, orange peel
Simmer 30 min until thick and purple
Strain
Sweeten to taste
Serve hot, sprinkle with ground cinnamon

recipes.name: Chicha
recipes.description: Ancient Andean fermented corn beer.
instructions: Soak and sprout corn 3 days
Grind sprouted corn
Boil in water to make sweet wort
Cool, let ferment naturally 3-7 days
Strain
Serve in clay cups

recipes.name: Mocochinchi
recipes.description: Cinnamon-spiced dried peach drink — Bolivia's refreshing street beverage, sold from carts in every city plaza.
instructions: Boil dried peaches with cinnamon and cloves
Simmer 15 min until peaches are plump
Sweeten with sugar
Cool and refrigerate
Serve cold with a rehydrated peach in each glass

recipes.name: Ćevapi with Somun
recipes.description: Grilled minced meat sausages in flatbread — Bosnia's most famous dish.
instructions: Mix meat with grated onion, garlic, baking soda, salt, pepper
Knead well, rest 2 hours in fridge
Shape into small finger-sized sausages
Grill over charcoal until done
Serve in split somun with raw onion and kajmak

recipes.name: Burek
recipes.description: Flaky spiral phyllo pie filled with spiced meat.
ingredients: For filling: 500g ground beef, 2 onions, salt, pepper
instructions: Sauté meat with onions until cooked
Roll phyllo thin, spread filling in strip
Roll into long coil, spiral into baking pan
Brush with oil
Bake at 180°C 45 min until flaky and golden
Serve with yogurt

recipes.name: Somun sa Kajmakom
recipes.description: Warm Bosnian flatbread stuffed with kajmak cream — the simplest and best breakfast in Sarajevo's baščaršija.
instructions: Warm somun bread
Split open while hot
Spread generous layer of kajmak inside
Eat immediately — the warmth melts the kajmak

recipes.name: Ćevapi for Breakfast
recipes.description: Yes, Bosnians eat ćevapi for breakfast — and it went viral when food creators showed the 9am meat-finger-in-bread ritual. The queues at Željo or Petica in Sarajevo start at dawn. The most Instagrammed food in the Balkans.
instructions: Grill ćevapi over charcoal until charred and juicy
Split somun bread
Tuck ćevapi inside
Pile raw diced onion on top
Add a generous scoop of kajmak
Serve with ajvar on the side
This is breakfast, lunch, and dinner — the meal that put Sarajevo on every food list

recipes.name: Begova Čorba
recipes.description: A creamy, velvety chicken soup from Ottoman Bosnian tradition.
instructions: Boil chicken with vegetables until tender
Remove chicken, strain broth
Shred chicken
Make roux with butter and flour
Add sour cream and egg yolks
Stir into broth, add chicken
Heat gently, don't boil
Garnish with parsley

recipes.name: Bosanski Lonac
recipes.description: A slow-baked layered meat and vegetable pot — never stirred.
instructions: Layer meat and vegetables alternately in clay pot
Season each layer with garlic, peppercorns, bay leaf
Add vinegar and water to just cover
Cover tightly, bake at 160°C for 2 hours
Do not stir — layers develop flavor
Serve from the pot

recipes.name: Klepe
recipes.description: Bosnian meat dumplings in garlic yogurt with paprika butter — Bosnia's version of manti, a legacy of Ottoman cuisine.
ingredients: Filling: 300g ground beef, 1 onion (finely diced), salt, pepper
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Mix filling: raw beef with finely diced onion, salt, pepper
Roll dough thin, cut squares
Place filling on each, fold into triangles, press edges
Boil in salted water until they float, then 3 more min
Serve in bowl with garlic yogurt
Drizzle paprika-infused melted butter over top

recipes.name: Klepe
recipes.description: Meat-filled dumplings topped with garlic yogurt and paprika butter.
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, 1 egg, water, salt
Filling: 400g ground beef, 1 onion, salt, pepper
Topping: garlic yogurt sauce, paprika butter
instructions: Make dough, rest 20 min
Mix beef with onion and seasoning
Roll dough thin, cut squares
Fill and fold into triangles, press edges
Boil in salted water 15 min
Top with garlic yogurt and paprika-infused butter

recipes.name: Japrak
recipes.description: Bosnian-style stuffed grape leaves with paprika-spiced filling.
instructions: Blanch grape leaves
Mix beef, rice, onion, paprika, salt, pepper
Place filling on each leaf, roll tightly
Pack into pot seam-down
Add water and lemon juice to cover
Simmer 60 min
Serve with sour cream

recipes.name: Bosanski Lonac
recipes.description: A sealed layered pot of meat and vegetables — never stirred, slow-cooked for hours. Bosnia's defining one-pot dish, ancient and unchanged.
instructions: Layer in heavy pot: onion, meat, vegetables, meat, vegetables
Tuck in garlic, peppercorns, bay leaf
Add vinegar and enough water to barely cover
Seal pot tightly (traditional: dough seal around lid)
Cook on very low heat for 2+ hours — do not open or stir
The layers stay distinct, the broth concentrates
Serve from the pot at the table

recipes.name: Pita Zeljanica
recipes.description: Flaky phyllo pie filled with spinach and cheese.
instructions: Wilt spinach, squeeze dry, chop
Mix with feta, eggs, onion
Layer phyllo in pan with oil
Spread filling between layers
Bake at 180°C 40 min until golden and flaky

recipes.name: Ćevapi with Somun
recipes.description: Bosnia's most famous food — small grilled meat fingers in flatbread with onion and cream. Sarajevo's ćevabdžinicas have served them for centuries.
instructions: Mix meat with grated onion, baking soda, salt, pepper
Refrigerate 2 hours or overnight
Shape into small finger-sized links
Grill over charcoal, turning once
Serve 10 pieces in split somun with raw diced onion and kajmak

recipes.name: Tufahije
recipes.description: Whole apples poached in syrup and filled with walnuts.
ingredients: Syrup: 2 cups sugar, water, lemon juice
instructions: Make syrup, poach apples until tender
Fill centers with walnut-sugar mixture
Place in serving dish, pour syrup over
Top with whipped cream

recipes.name: Tufahije
recipes.description: Apples poached in syrup and stuffed with walnuts — an Ottoman-era Bosnian dessert served at every kafana.
ingredients: Walnut filling: walnuts, sugar, lemon zest
instructions: Core apples, keeping bottom intact
Poach in sugar syrup until tender but holding shape
Fill centers with ground walnut mixture
Return to syrup, simmer 5 more min
Serve in syrup bowls topped with whipped cream

recipes.name: Bosanska Kafa
recipes.description: Bosnian coffee — a ritual with its own etiquette.
instructions: Heat water in džezva (cezve)
When bubbles form, remove, add coffee
Return to heat, let foam rise
Remove before boiling over
Let grounds settle
Pour into fildžan cups, serve with sugar and rahat lokum

recipes.name: Šljivovica
recipes.description: Traditional plum brandy — the king of Balkan spirits.
instructions: Pit and crush plums
Let ferment naturally 3-4 weeks
Distill twice over copper still
Age in oak barrels 2+ years
Serve as digestif

recipes.name: Bosanska Kafa
recipes.description: Not Turkish coffee — Bosnian coffee. The ritual matters: the džezva, the foam, the sugar cube bitten between sips. A daily act of hospitality.
instructions: Heat water in džezva (copper pot) until it begins to rise
Remove, add coffee, stir once
Return to heat, let foam rise — do not boil
Remove when foam crests
Pour slowly into fildžan cups, foam first
Serve with sugar cube and rahat lokum on the side

recipes.name: Bogobe
recipes.description: Traditional sorghum porridge — Botswana's daily breakfast.
instructions: Boil water with salt
Slowly stir in sorghum flour
Reduce heat, stir 15 min
Cook until thick and smooth
Serve with milk and sugar or honey

recipes.name: Fat Cakes
recipes.description: Puffy fried dough balls — beloved across Botswana.
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt
Add warm water to form soft dough
Rise 1 hour until doubled
Shape into balls
Deep fry until golden brown
Serve warm with butter or jam

recipes.name: Magwinya
recipes.description: Puffy golden fried dough — sold at every bus stop and market in Botswana. Eaten plain, with butter, or filled with mince.
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar, salt
Add warm water to form soft, slightly sticky dough
Cover, rest 30 min
Shape into balls
Deep fry in hot oil until golden and puffy
Drain on paper — they should be light inside

recipes.name: Seswaa
recipes.description: Botswana's national dish — slow-cooked, pounded beef.
instructions: Place beef in pot with onion
Cover with water
Simmer on low heat 3 hours until very tender
Remove bones
Pound and shred meat with fork
Season with salt and pepper
Serve with bogobe or pap

recipes.name: Morogo
recipes.description: Cooked wild greens — an essential side dish.
instructions: Wash greens thoroughly
Sauté onion in oil
Add tomatoes, cook 5 min
Add greens, cover and cook 10 min
Season with salt and pepper
Serve alongside seswaa and pap

recipes.name: Dikgobe
recipes.description: Beans and samp simmered together — Botswana's everyday comfort food. Simple, filling, nourishing.
instructions: Cook soaked samp in plenty of water, 45 min until almost tender
Add soaked beans
Continue cooking until both are soft and creamy
Season with salt
The starch makes the broth thick and silky
Serve as main dish or side

recipes.name: Seswaa
recipes.description: Botswana's national dish — slow-boiled beef pounded into tender shreds, served with pap. The simplicity is the point: just meat, water, salt, and time. Went viral when food explorers showed the communal cooking and pounding tradition at Batswana celebrations.
ingredients: 1kg beef (bone-in, fatty cuts preferred — brisket, shin)
instructions: Place beef and bones in large pot
Cover with water — just enough, not too much
Bring to boil, then reduce to low simmer
Cook 3-4 hours until meat falls off the bone
Remove bones
Shred and pound meat with a wooden spoon or fork until it's a soft, fibrous mass
Season with salt only — no other spices, this is about pure beef flavor
Serve with pap (stiff maize porridge) and a side of morogo (wild greens)
This is Botswana's celebration dish — weddings, funerals, national holidays all center on seswaa

recipes.name: Dikgobe
recipes.description: Hearty stew of beans and corn, eaten with every meal.
instructions: Cook samp and beans together until tender, about 60 min
Sauté onion in oil
Add to beans and corn
Season with salt and pepper
Cook until thick and creamy

recipes.name: Grilled T-Bone with Chakalaka
recipes.description: Grilled steak with spicy vegetable-bean relish.
ingredients: For chakalaka: 1 can baked beans, 2 carrots (grated), 1 onion, 1 pepper, 2 tomatoes, curry powder, chili
instructions: Season steaks with salt and pepper
Grill over hot coals to desired doneness
Make chakalaka: sauté onion, carrots, pepper
Add tomatoes, curry powder, chili
Add baked beans, simmer 10 min
Serve steak with chakalaka and pap

recipes.name: Serobe
recipes.description: Slow-cooked offal stew — traditional Tswana dish served at celebrations and weddings. Nothing is wasted.
instructions: Clean tripe and intestines very thoroughly
Boil in salted water for 60-90 min until very tender
Add onion
Continue simmering until the broth is rich
Season well
Serve with pap — the broth is the best part

recipes.name: Vetkoek
recipes.description: Golden fried bread filled with savory mince or sweet jam.
instructions: Mix dough ingredients, knead
Rise 1 hour
Shape into balls, flatten slightly
Deep fry until golden on both sides
Split open and fill with mince or jam

recipes.name: Biltong
recipes.description: Air-dried spiced beef — a Southern African tradition. Botswana's version uses plenty of coriander and cracked pepper.
instructions: Slice beef into thick strips along the grain
Mix salt, pepper, coriander, sugar
Dip strips in vinegar briefly
Coat with spice mixture
Hang in cool, dry, ventilated area
Dry 3-5 days until firm but still slightly soft inside
Slice thin to serve

recipes.name: Malva Pudding
recipes.description: Warm, spongy pudding drenched in creamy sauce.
ingredients: Sauce: 1 cup cream, 1/2 cup butter, 1/2 cup sugar, vanilla
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, egg, jam
Dissolve baking soda in milk with vinegar
Combine, add melted butter
Bake at 180°C 45 min
Make sauce: heat cream, butter, sugar
Pour hot sauce over hot pudding

recipes.name: Mosutlhwane
recipes.description: Wild melon cooked into a sweet, thick preserve — harvested from the Kalahari, a taste of Botswana's desert landscape.
instructions: Simmer melon cubes in water until very soft
Mash lightly
Sweeten with sugar, add cinnamon
Cook until thick and jammy
Serve warm or cold

recipes.name: Ginger Beer
recipes.description: Spicy, fizzy homemade ginger beer.
instructions: Grate ginger, steep in hot water
Add sugar and cream of tartar
Cool, add pinch of yeast
Bottle and ferment 2 days
Strain and serve cold

recipes.name: Chibuku
recipes.description: Traditional sorghum beer with a thick, porridge-like texture.
instructions: Mix sorghum flour with water, cook to porridge
Cool, add malt
Let ferment 2-3 days in warm place
Stir daily
Strain and serve when mildly alcoholic

recipes.name: Ginger Beer
recipes.description: Fiery homemade ginger beer — refreshing in Botswana's heat. Every family has their own balance of ginger to sugar.
instructions: Grate ginger, steep in hot water 30 min
Strain, pressing out all liquid
Add sugar and lemon juice, stir until dissolved
Top up with cold water
Add pinch of yeast if you want natural fizz
Refrigerate overnight, strain again
Serve ice cold

recipes.name: Pão de Queijo
recipes.description: Chewy, cheesy, gluten-free rolls from Minas Gerais — the tapioca starch makes them uniquely puffy and stretchy inside. Found at every bakery and gas station in Brazil.
instructions: Heat milk with oil and salt until just boiling
Pour over tapioca starch, stir vigorously — it will form a sticky mass
Cool enough to handle, then knead in eggs one at a time
Fold in cheese
Roll into small balls — they should be slightly sticky
Bake at 200°C for 18-20 min until puffed, golden, and cracked on top
Eat immediately — they deflate as they cool

recipes.name: Café da Manhã
recipes.description: Brazilian breakfast is a spread: crusty rolls, strong milky coffee, fresh papaya, ham, cheese, and always a slice of cake. It's simpler than it sounds and more satisfying than it should be.
ingredients: Cake (bolo de cenoura or bolo de fubá)
instructions: Slice and toast pão francês
Butter and fill with ham and cheese
Slice papaya
Cut a generous slice of cake — yes, cake for breakfast
Make café com leite: equal parts strong filtered coffee and hot milk
Arrange everything on the table — breakfast is leisurely

recipes.name: Tapioca Crepe
recipes.description: Northeastern Brazilian crêpe made from tapioca starch — naturally gluten-free, chewy, and filled with anything from cheese to condensed milk. It becomes transparent as it cooks.
ingredients: 1 cup hydrated tapioca starch (goma de tapioca)
Filling: queijo coalho, coconut, condensed milk, or butter and cheese
instructions: Heat non-stick pan — no oil needed
Sprinkle tapioca starch evenly in a thin layer through a sieve
Cook 1-2 min until it forms a solid white disk
Add filling to one half, fold over
Cook 1 more min until cheese melts
Serve immediately

recipes.name: Feijoada Completa
recipes.description: Brazil's national dish — a magnificent slow-cooked black bean stew with every cut of pork imaginable. Always Saturday lunch, always communal.
ingredients: Assorted pork: ribs, sausage (linguiça), carne seca (jerky), pig ear, pig tail, bacon
Accompaniments: white rice, farofa, couve (collard greens), orange slices, vinagrete (tomato-onion salsa)
instructions: Cook soaked beans with bay leaves until almost tender, 1.5 hours
In separate pots, cook the tougher cuts (ears, tails) until soft
Sauté onion and garlic in lard, add to beans
Add all meats to the bean pot gradually — sausage and bacon last
Add halved orange — it cuts the richness
Simmer everything together 30+ min until thick and rich
Make accompaniments: sauté shredded collard greens in garlic; toast farofa (cassava flour) in butter; dice tomato-onion vinagrete
Serve beans and meats in the center, surrounded by bowls of rice, collard greens, farofa, orange slices, and vinagrete
This is a Saturday ritual — never rushed

recipes.name: Moqueca Baiana
recipes.description: Bahian fish stew cooked in a clay pot — African-influenced, vivid orange from dendê oil, never stirred so the layers stay beautiful. The clay pot matters.
instructions: Marinate fish in lime and salt 15 min
In a clay pot (panela de barro), layer: onion, tomato, pepper, fish
Pour coconut milk and dendê oil over — do NOT stir
Cover and cook 25-30 min on medium — the layers meld without stirring
The dendê oil floats to the top, creating a vibrant orange layer
Scatter with cilantro and malagueta pepper
Bring the clay pot to the table
Serve with white rice and pirão (fish gravy thickened with cassava flour)

recipes.name: Churrasco
recipes.description: Brazilian churrasco is about fire, salt, and good meat — especially picanha, the prized fat-capped cut that defined Brazilian BBQ worldwide.
ingredients: Vinagrete (diced tomato, onion, pepper, vinegar, oil)
instructions: Cut picanha into thick C-shaped pieces, following the fat cap curve
Season with coarse salt only — nothing else touches picanha
Skewer in the C-shape, fat side out
Grill over charcoal, rotating the skewer slowly
Carve thin slices off the outside as each layer cooks — this is the rodízio method
Season and grill flank steak, sausage, and chicken hearts on separate skewers
Serve sliced at the table with farofa and vinagrete

recipes.name: Acarajé
recipes.description: Afro-Brazilian bean fritters fried in palm oil and stuffed with shrimp — sold by baianas (women in white traditional dress) on the streets of Salvador. UNESCO-recognized cultural heritage.
ingredients: Filling: vatapá (shrimp-peanut-coconut cream), caruru (okra stew), dried shrimp, vinagrete, hot pepper
instructions: Blend peeled black-eyed peas with onion and salt to a thick paste
Beat vigorously — the airy texture is crucial, it should be lighter than hummus
Heat dendê oil to 180°C in a deep pan
Drop rounded spoonfuls into the oil
Fry until deep golden and crispy, 5-6 min
Split open like a sandwich
Fill with vatapá, caruru, dried shrimp, vinagrete, and pepper sauce

recipes.name: Frango à Passarinho
recipes.description: Bar-style crispy chicken bites — named 'little bird' for the small bone-in pieces. Found at every boteco (neighborhood bar) in Brazil.
ingredients: 1kg chicken (cut into very small bone-in pieces)
instructions: Cut chicken into small pieces — bone-in bites, not boneless
Marinate in garlic, lime, and salt for 1+ hour
Fry in hot oil until deeply golden and crispy
Toss with extra fried garlic chips
Serve with lime wedges

recipes.name: Vatapá
recipes.description: Rich Bahian shrimp cream thickened with bread, peanuts, and cashews — West African roots in Brazilian cuisine.
instructions: Soak dried shrimp, grind half, leave half whole
Blend soaked bread with coconut milk until smooth
Sauté onion, garlic, ginger in dendê oil
Add ground peanuts and cashews
Add coconut-bread mixture, cook until thick
Add shrimp, season with pepper
Simmer until creamy and golden
Serve with white rice or as filling for acarajé

recipes.name: Coxinha
recipes.description: Teardrop-shaped chicken croquettes — Brazil's most popular snack food. The shape mimics a chicken drumstick, and the dough-to-filling ratio is fiercely debated.
ingredients: Filling: shredded chicken, cream cheese, onion, parsley
instructions: Heat broth and butter to boiling, add flour all at once
Stir vigorously until dough pulls from the pan in a smooth ball
Cool dough until handleable
Flatten a piece in your palm, add chicken filling
Wrap dough around filling, shape into a teardrop — this shape is essential, it represents a chicken drumstick
Dip in egg wash, roll in fine breadcrumbs
Deep fry at 180°C until deep golden
The outside should shatter, the inside should be creamy

recipes.name: Pastel
recipes.description: Paper-thin crispy fried pastry with endless filling options — the Saturday morning feira (market) tradition. Best eaten standing up at the market stall.
ingredients: Wrapper: flour, cachaça, oil, salt, warm water (or store-bought)
Fillings: ground beef with olives, hearts of palm with cheese, or shrimp
instructions: Mix dough (the cachaça makes it extra crispy), rest 30 min
Roll very thin, cut rectangles
Fill one side, fold, seal edges with fork
Deep fry until blistered and golden — the wrapper should puff up
Serve immediately with hot sauce

recipes.name: Pão de Queijo Recheado
recipes.full_name: Pão de Queijo Recheado (Stuffed Cheese Bread)
recipes.description: Stuffed pão de queijo — the TikTok-viral version with molten cream cheese or guava paste inside the already-chewy cheese bread. The cheese pull videos broke the internet.
ingredients: Pão de queijo dough: tapioca starch, milk, oil, eggs, queijo minas or Parmesan
Filling: requeijão (Brazilian cream cheese), guava paste, or Catupiry cheese
instructions: Make pão de queijo dough: heat milk and oil, pour over tapioca starch, mix, add eggs and cheese
Shape into balls, press a hole, fill with requeijão or guava paste
Close dough around filling
Bake at 180°C for 20 min until puffed and golden
When you bite in, the filling oozes out — the requeijão version is the viral one

recipes.name: Picanha na Brasa
recipes.description: The cut that made Brazilian steakhouses famous worldwide — top sirloin cap with the fat left on. The viral C-fold skewer technique and the fat-basting have made it the most searched steak on YouTube.
ingredients: 1kg picanha (top sirloin cap, fat cap on)
instructions: Do NOT trim the fat cap — this is essential
Cut into thick steaks with the grain, keeping the C-shaped curve and fat
Season only with coarse salt — nothing else
Fold each steak into a C-shape on a skewer, fat side out
Grill over high heat, fat side first, until the fat renders and chars
Flip, cook to medium-rare inside
Slice thin against the grain at the table
The fat bastes the meat as it cooks — this is why picanha is the world's most viral steak cut

recipes.name: Brigadeiro
recipes.description: Brazil's most beloved sweet — invented in the 1940s for a political campaign. Every birthday party, every celebration, every Tuesday when you're sad. The name means 'brigadier.'
instructions: Combine condensed milk, cocoa, and butter in non-stick pan
Cook on medium heat, stirring constantly
Scrape the bottom — it burns easily
Cook until mixture pulls away from the pan as one mass, 12-15 min
Transfer to buttered plate, cool until handleable
Butter your hands, roll into small balls
Roll in chocolate sprinkles
Place in small paper cups

recipes.name: Pudim de Leite
recipes.description: Condensed milk flan — denser and sweeter than French crème caramel. The recipe is on every can of Leite Moça condensed milk in Brazil.
ingredients: Custard: 1 can condensed milk, 1 can whole milk (use the condensed milk can to measure), 3 eggs
instructions: Melt sugar in flan mold until deep amber caramel, swirl to coat
Blend condensed milk, whole milk, and eggs — that's it, just three ingredients
Pour through strainer into caramelized mold
Cover tightly with foil
Bake in water bath at 160°C for 60 min
Cool, refrigerate overnight
Unmold — the caramel sauce cascades over the custard

recipes.name: Bolo de Rolo
recipes.description: A cake with dozens of paper-thin layers spiraling around guava paste — Pernambuco's pride. Cross-section photos went viral for the hypnotic spiral pattern. Each layer is individually baked and rolled.
ingredients: Batter: 250g butter, 250g sugar, 6 egg yolks, 6 egg whites (whipped), 250g flour
Filling: guava paste (goiabada) melted with a little water into thick paste
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, add yolks
Fold in whipped whites alternately with flour
Spread paper-thin layer of batter on baking sheet
Bake at 200°C for just 3-4 min — barely set
Spread thin layer of guava paste
Roll tightly while still warm
Repeat with another layer, rolling around the first roll
Keep layering and rolling — a proper bolo de rolo has 10+ paper-thin layers
Slice to reveal the dramatic spiral of dozens of thin layers

recipes.name: Caipirinha
recipes.description: Brazil's national cocktail — cachaça (sugarcane spirit), lime, and sugar. Simple, potent, and dangerously easy to drink. Never made with vodka.
instructions: Cut lime into 8 wedges, removing white pith from center
Place in rocks glass with sugar
Muddle firmly — press and twist to extract juice and oils, don't pulverize
Add cachaça
Fill with crushed ice
Stir vigorously — the dilution is part of the drink
Serve in the same glass you muddled in

recipes.name: Guaraná Antartica
recipes.description: Made from guaraná berries from the Amazon — sweet, fruity, and uniquely Brazilian. The national soft drink.
instructions: Serve ice cold
Brazil's most popular soft drink — outsells Coca-Cola in the country

recipes.name: Açaí na Tigela
recipes.description: Originally a post-surf fuel in Pará state, now a worldwide phenomenon. Real açaí is deep purple and barely sweet — the hyper-sweetened version abroad is a different thing.
ingredients: Splash of guaraná syrup or apple juice
Toppings: granola, sliced banana, honey, guaraná powder
instructions: Blend frozen açaí pulp with banana and a splash of liquid — it should be thick, like soft serve
Pour into a bowl
Top with granola, sliced banana, and a drizzle of honey
Eat with a spoon — it's too thick for a straw

recipes.name: Feijoada
recipes.description: Brazilian national lunch - hearty black bean stew with pork and sausage. Evolved from plantation cuisine
instructions: Soak beans overnight
In large pot, heat oil, sauté onion and garlic
Add pork, brown on all sides
Add beans, bay leaves and water to cover by 2 inches
Bring to boil, reduce heat, simmer 3 hours
Add sausage in last 30 minutes
Serve with rice, sautéed collard greens and orange slices on side
tips: Long cooking time essential for tender meat and creamy beans. Tastes better the next day
recipes.fun_fact: Feijoada is Brazilian national lunch, evolved from plantation cuisine as slave food. Now beloved dish across all social classes

recipes.name: Brazilian Feijoada
recipes.full_name: Brazilian Feijoada (Black Bean and Meat Stew)
recipes.description: Black bean and meat stew - Brazil's national dinner dish
ingredients: 150g carne seca (dried salted beef), soaked and shredded
200g fresh orange slices or orange juice
instructions: Drain soaked beans; rinse
In large heavy pot or clay pot, combine soaked beans with 3 liters fresh water
Bring to boil; reduce heat to low simmer
In separate skillet, heat oil; sauté onion and garlic until soft
Add beef brisket, pork, sausage, carne seca; brown on all sides
Add cooked meat mixture to simmering beans
Add bay leaves, salt, pepper
Simmer gently uncovered for 4-5 hours, stirring occasionally
Add water if needed to maintain stew consistency
Beans should be very tender and broth dark and thick
Meanwhile, sauté collard greens in oil with garlic until wilted
Serve feijoada in bowls with rice on side, collard greens, farofa, orange slices, hot sauce
recipes.fun_fact: Believed to originate in slave quarters, transformed into national dish

recipes.name: Moqueca
recipes.description: Brazilian coconut seafood stew - coastal flavors in a pot
ingredients: 400g white fish fillets, cut into chunks
1 tablespoon palm oil (dendê) or vegetable oil
instructions: Heat palm oil in large pot over medium heat
Add sliced red onion and bell peppers, cook 3 minutes until slightly softened
Add minced garlic and diced tomatoes, cook 2 minutes
Add fish stock and bring to simmer
Add fish chunks, simmer gently 5 minutes
Add shrimp and crab meat if using, simmer 3 minutes
Pour in coconut milk, stir gently
Simmer 5 more minutes (do not boil or seafood will toughen)
Season with salt, pepper, and lime juice
Fold in fresh cilantro
Add malagueta peppers for heat if desired
Serve hot in wide bowls over white rice
Serve with hot sauce and lime wedges
tips: Palm oil (dendê) is essential for authentic flavor and color
recipes.fun_fact: Moqueca is Brazil's national seafood dish, with regional variations from different states
alternatives: Use coconut cream for richer version

recipes.name: Nasi Katok
recipes.description: Brunei's beloved everyday meal of fragrant rice paired with crispy fried chicken and fiery sambal, wrapped in brown paper for a quick and satisfying bite.
instructions: Cook jasmine rice in a rice cooker with a pinch of salt.
Season chicken drumsticks with turmeric, chili powder, and salt.
Coat chicken in flour and deep-fry in hot oil until golden brown and cooked through, about 12 minutes.
Serve a mound of rice topped with fried chicken and sambal belacan on the side.

recipes.name: Kuih Mor
recipes.description: Traditional Bruneian glutinous rice cakes filled with molten palm sugar and coated in grated coconut, a sweet morning treat enjoyed with tea.
instructions: Mix glutinous rice flour with coconut milk and a pinch of salt to form a smooth dough.
Melt palm sugar with a little water to make a thick syrup, then let it cool.
Take small portions of dough, flatten, and fill with palm sugar syrup. Seal into balls.
Wrap each ball in a piece of banana leaf and steam for 25 minutes until cooked through.
Serve warm, rolled in freshly grated coconut.

recipes.name: Kuih Malaya
recipes.description: Pandan-green crepes filled with sweet coconut — a beloved Malay kuih found at every Brunei morning market.
ingredients: Batter: 1 cup flour, 1 egg, 200ml coconut milk, pandan extract, pinch salt, green food coloring (optional)
Filling: grated coconut, palm sugar (gula melaka), pandan leaf
instructions: Make thin pancake batter with coconut milk, egg, flour, pandan
Cook filling: toast grated coconut with palm sugar and pandan until sticky
Make thin crepes from batter
Spread coconut filling on each crepe
Roll up tightly
Slice into rounds to serve

recipes.name: Ambuyat
recipes.description: The national dish of Brunei, a starchy sago-based preparation twirled on bamboo forks and dipped into tangy, savory shrimp paste sauce.
ingredients: Assorted side dishes: grilled fish, steamed vegetables
instructions: Bring water to a rolling boil in a pot.
Gradually add sago starch while stirring vigorously with a fork or chopsticks until the mixture forms a translucent, sticky mass.
Prepare the cacah dipping sauce by mixing shrimp paste with tamarind, sugar, and chilies.
Serve ambuyat in the pot with the cacah sauce and side dishes arranged around it.
Use a bamboo fork (candas) to twirl the ambuyat and dip into the sauce.

recipes.name: Soto Brunei
recipes.description: A comforting Bruneian-style chicken soup with aromatic spices, rice vermicelli, and fresh garnishes, often enjoyed as a midday meal.
ingredients: Bean sprouts, fried shallots, lime wedges for garnish
Salt and white pepper to taste
instructions: Simmer chicken thighs in chicken stock with lemongrass, galangal, and turmeric for 35 minutes until tender.
Remove chicken, shred the meat, and return broth to a simmer.
Saute shallots and garlic until fragrant, then add to the broth. Season with salt and pepper.
Cook rice vermicelli according to package directions and divide among bowls.
Ladle hot broth over noodles, top with shredded chicken, bean sprouts, fried shallots, and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Nasi Katok
recipes.description: Brunei's national cheap meal — rice, fried chicken, sambal. Sold wrapped in paper for 1 BND at stalls across the country.
instructions: Steam rice
Fry chicken piece until golden and cooked through
Make sambal: pound chili, shrimp paste, lime juice
Serve rice with chicken and sambal

recipes.name: Rendang Daging
recipes.description: A rich, slow-cooked beef rendang with layers of spice and toasted coconut, deeply flavored and dry in the Bruneian style.
instructions: Combine all blended ingredients in a large pot and cook over medium heat until fragrant, about 5 minutes.
Add beef cubes and stir to coat with the spice paste.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a gentle boil. Add lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaf.
Reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, for about 90 minutes.
Add coconut cream and kerisik, continue cooking until the sauce is thick and dark, coating the meat.
Season with salt and sugar. Serve with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Udang Sambal Serai
recipes.description: Succulent prawns wok-fried in a spicy lemongrass and chili sambal, a beloved Bruneian seafood dish with bold, aromatic flavors.
instructions: Heat oil in a wok and saute shallots, garlic, and lemongrass until fragrant.
Add the blended chili paste and cook until the oil separates from the paste.
Toss in the prawns and stir-fry until they turn pink, about 4 minutes.
Add tamarind juice, sugar, and salt. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve immediately with steamed rice.

recipes.name: Soto Brunei
recipes.description: Brunei's soul-warming chicken soup — fragrant with galangal and turmeric, loaded with toppings. A Ramadan staple.
instructions: Simmer chicken with lemongrass, galangal, turmeric until tender
Remove chicken, shred meat
Strain broth, return to pot
Add shredded chicken back
To serve: place vermicelli and bean sprouts in bowl
Ladle hot broth and chicken over
Top with egg halves, fried shallots, lime, sambal

recipes.name: Cucur Udang
recipes.description: Crispy Bruneian shrimp fritters packed with bean sprouts and spring onions, a popular teatime snack sold at roadside stalls.
instructions: Mix both flours with turmeric, chili flakes, and salt. Add water to make a thick batter.
Fold in shrimp, bean sprouts, and spring onions.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Drop spoonfuls of batter into the hot oil.
Fry until golden and crispy on all sides, about 3 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve with sweet chili sauce.

recipes.name: Cucur Udang
recipes.description: Crispy prawn fritters — a teatime favorite across Brunei, always served with dipping sauce.
instructions: Mix flours with turmeric, salt, and water to thick batter
Fold in prawns, chili, bean sprouts, spring onion
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden and crispy
Serve with sweet chili sauce

recipes.name: Ambuyat
recipes.description: Brunei's national dish — a translucent, stretchy sago starch eaten communally with a special bamboo fork and dipped in pungent cacah sauce. The bizarre texture and twirling technique have made it viral, and the fermented durian dipping sauce divides every food creator who tries it.
ingredients: Dipping sauces: cacah (fermented durian/shrimp paste), tempoyak, sambal
Side dishes: grilled fish, vegetables, fried tofu
instructions: Bring water to boil
Pour boiling water into sago starch gradually, stirring with chopstick or fork
Keep stirring — it transforms into a translucent, stretchy, gluey mass
It's ready when it's completely translucent and sticky
Use a bamboo fork (candas) — twirl a ball of ambuyat around the prongs
Dip the ball into cacah sauce and eat in one go — don't chew, swallow
The texture is the challenge — it's sticky, stretchy, and unfamiliar to outsiders
This is Brunei's national dish, eaten communally from a shared pot

recipes.name: Kuih Lapis
recipes.description: A beautiful multicolored steamed layer cake with a soft, chewy texture, a staple at Bruneian celebrations and festive gatherings.
ingredients: Food coloring (red, green, or pandan extract)
instructions: Dissolve sugar in water over low heat, then let cool. Mix in coconut milk and salt.
Combine rice flour and tapioca starch. Gradually add the coconut sugar mixture, stirring until smooth.
Divide batter into portions and color each differently.
Grease a square tray and steam the first colored layer for 5 minutes until set.
Add the next colored layer on top and steam again. Repeat until all layers are used.
Let cool completely, then cut into diamond shapes to serve.

recipes.name: Kuih Lapis
recipes.description: Layer cake of Malay royalty — 20 thin grilled layers alternating pandan and vanilla. A labor of love served at Hari Raya.
ingredients: Spice mix: cinnamon, cardamom, clove, nutmeg
instructions: Cream butter and sugar
Add egg yolks one at a time
Fold in flour and tapioca starch alternately with coconut milk
Divide batter: leave half plain (vanilla), color half with pandan
Grease a pan, pour thin layer of one batter
Grill/broil until set and lightly browned
Add layer of other batter, grill again
Repeat for 18-20 alternating layers
Cool completely before cutting — it should slice into distinct striped layers

recipes.name: Teh Tarik
recipes.description: Pulled tea made by pouring sweetened black tea between cups to create a creamy froth, a beloved daily drink throughout Brunei.
instructions: Brew black tea in boiling water for 5 minutes, then strain.
Add condensed milk and evaporated milk to the hot tea.
Pour the tea back and forth between two cups from a height to create a frothy top.
Repeat the pulling motion several times until well mixed and frothy.
Serve hot in glasses.

recipes.name: Tuak
recipes.description: Traditional palm wine made from naturally fermented coconut sap, historically enjoyed by Brunei's indigenous communities during celebrations.
ingredients: Bark strips from the raru tree (or substitute with a cinnamon stick for flavor)
instructions: Collect fresh coconut palm sap from the cut flower stalks of the coconut palm.
Add raru bark strips to the sap in a jar for a subtle woody flavor.
Allow the sap to naturally ferment for 1 to 3 days at room temperature.
Strain and serve at room temperature or slightly chilled.
Consume within a few days as it continues to ferment and will become more sour.

recipes.name: Teh Tarik
recipes.description: Tea pulled between two vessels to create thick froth — the art is in the pour. Every kopitiam in Brunei makes it.
ingredients: Strong black tea (2 tea bags or loose)
instructions: Brew very strong tea
Mix with condensed milk in a mug
'Pull' the tea: pour from one vessel to another at arm's length, repeatedly
This creates a thick foam and cools the tea
Serve immediately — the foam should sit on top

recipes.name: Banitsa
recipes.description: Bulgaria's iconic flaky filo pastry filled with tangy white cheese and eggs, coiled into a golden spiral and enjoyed warm for breakfast.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180C (350F).
Mix crumbled sirene with eggs, yogurt, and baking soda in a bowl.
Brush each filo sheet with melted butter, spread a line of filling along one edge, and roll into a log.
Coil the logs into a round baking dish, spiraling from the center outward.
Brush the top generously with remaining melted butter.
Bake for 30-35 minutes until golden and flaky. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Mekitsi
recipes.description: Puffy fried dough rounds made with yogurt, served warm with powdered sugar or salty white cheese, a classic Bulgarian street breakfast.
ingredients: Powdered sugar or sirene cheese for serving
instructions: Mix flour, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Add yogurt and egg, stirring until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 170C (340F).
With floured hands, pull off pieces of dough, flatten into discs, and fry until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain on paper towels and serve dusted with powdered sugar or topped with crumbled sirene.

recipes.name: Mekitsi
recipes.description: Puffy yogurt-based fried dough — THE Bulgarian breakfast, made with the country's legendary yogurt. Sweet or savory, your choice.
ingredients: Powdered sugar or sirene cheese to serve
instructions: Mix yogurt, egg, baking soda
Add flour to form soft sticky dough
With wet hands, shape into flat rounds
Fry in oil until puffed and golden on both sides
Serve with powdered sugar or crumbled sirene cheese

recipes.name: Banitsa
recipes.description: The spiral filo cheese pie that went viral — the coiling technique creates a dramatic spiral when cut. On New Year's Eve, Bulgarians hide fortune papers and a coin inside. The crunch of the filo and the tang of the sirene cheese make it addictive.
ingredients: Filling: 500g sirene (Bulgarian white cheese), 4 eggs, 200ml yogurt
instructions: Mix crumbled sirene with eggs and yogurt
Brush each filo sheet with butter and oil
Spread filling along one edge
Roll into a log, then coil the log into a spiral in a round pan
Continue adding coiled logs to the spiral
Brush top with remaining butter
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 min until deeply golden and flaky
On New Year's Eve, fortunes written on paper are hidden inside — whoever finds one gets a lucky year

recipes.name: Shopska Salata
recipes.description: The quintessential Bulgarian salad with ripe tomatoes, cucumbers, and roasted peppers topped with a snowy blanket of grated white cheese.
instructions: Combine tomatoes, cucumbers, roasted peppers, and onion in a large bowl.
Drizzle with sunflower oil and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and toss gently.
Transfer to a serving plate and top generously with grated sirene cheese.
Garnish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Bob Chorba
recipes.description: A hearty Bulgarian white bean soup seasoned with paprika and spearmint, a warming staple of the national cuisine.
ingredients: 2 cups dried white beans, soaked overnight
instructions: Drain soaked beans, cover with fresh water, and boil for 10 minutes. Drain again.
In a large pot, heat oil and saute onion and carrots until soft.
Add tomato paste, paprika, and grated tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add beans and 6 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook for 45-50 minutes until beans are tender. Season with salt, pepper, and dried spearmint.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Kavarma
recipes.description: Slow-baked meat stew topped with a cracked egg — served bubbling in traditional Bulgarian clay pots (gyuveche).
instructions: Brown meat in oil
Sauté onions, peppers, mushrooms
Add tomatoes, paprika, cumin
Transfer to clay pot, add a little water
Bake covered at 180°C for 45-60 min
Crack egg on top, return to oven 5 min until egg sets
Serve in the clay pot

recipes.name: Kavarma
recipes.description: A traditional Bulgarian clay-pot stew of slow-cooked pork with peppers and tomatoes, finished with baked eggs on top.
instructions: Heat oil in an oven-safe pot and brown pork cubes on all sides.
Add onions and bell peppers, cooking until softened.
Stir in garlic, paprika, and pepper. Add tomatoes and white wine.
Cover and bake at 180C (350F) for 45 minutes until pork is tender.
Make 4 wells in the stew and crack an egg into each. Return to oven for 8 minutes until eggs are set.
Garnish with parsley and serve in the pot.

recipes.name: Sarmi
recipes.description: Bulgarian stuffed vine leaves filled with seasoned pork, beef, and rice, slowly simmered in tomato juice and served with cool yogurt.
instructions: Rinse vine leaves in cold water and pat dry.
Mix ground meats with rice, diced onions, paprika, savory, salt, and pepper.
Place a spoonful of filling on each vine leaf and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Arrange rolls seam-side down in a large pot, layering tightly.
Pour tomato juice and 1 cup water over the rolls. Drizzle with oil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 90 minutes until rice is cooked through.
Serve warm with a dollop of plain yogurt.

recipes.name: Sarmi
recipes.description: Stuffed sauerkraut rolls with smoked meat — the winter celebration dish. Every Bulgarian grandmother guards her recipe.
ingredients: Filling: 400g minced pork and beef, 1 cup rice, 1 onion, paprika, cumin, salt
instructions: Separate sauerkraut leaves carefully
Mix filling: raw mince with rice, diced onion, paprika, cumin, salt
Place filling on each leaf, roll tightly, tuck ends
Layer rolls in pot with smoked ribs between layers
Cover with tomato sauce diluted with water
Simmer on low 90 min or bake covered at 175°C for 2 hours
The sauerkraut gives a tangy depth you can't get from fresh cabbage

recipes.name: Printsesa
recipes.description: A beloved Bulgarian fried cheese sandwich coated in egg batter, crispy on the outside with melted kashkaval cheese inside.
instructions: Place a slice of kashkaval cheese between two slices of bread and press edges to seal.
Dip the sandwich in flour, then in beaten egg, coating all sides.
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides, about 2 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels, cut in half, and serve warm.

recipes.name: Lyutenitsa
recipes.description: Roasted pepper and tomato relish — every family makes kilos in September. Spread on bread with sirene cheese for the perfect snack.
instructions: Roast peppers and eggplants until charred, peel
Peel and chop tomatoes
Blend everything coarsely — keep some texture
Simmer in large pot 45-60 min, stirring often
Add garlic, sugar, vinegar, salt to taste
Cook until thick
Jar hot for preserving, or refrigerate

recipes.name: Garash Torta
recipes.description: An elegant Bulgarian chocolate-walnut torte with layers of crunchy walnut meringue and rich dark chocolate ganache, a Sofia classic since the 1800s.
instructions: Beat egg whites with salt to stiff peaks, gradually adding sugar.
Fold ground walnuts gently into the meringue.
Divide into 4 portions and bake each as a thin disc at 170C (340F) for 12 minutes.
Melt chocolate with cream and rum to make a ganache. Let cool slightly.
Layer the walnut meringue discs with ganache between each layer.
Coat the entire cake with remaining ganache and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving.

recipes.name: Garash Cake
recipes.description: Bulgaria's most famous cake — walnut meringue layers with chocolate cream, invented at the Garash café in Sofia in 1885.
instructions: Whip egg whites with half the sugar to stiff peaks
Fold in ground walnuts gently
Divide into 3-4 layers, bake each at 180°C for 10-12 min
Make chocolate cream: melt chocolate, mix with yolks and remaining sugar
Layer: walnut meringue, chocolate cream, repeat
Pour chocolate glaze over the top
Refrigerate overnight

recipes.name: Ayran
recipes.description: A refreshing cold yogurt drink whisked until frothy, the traditional Bulgarian accompaniment to grilled meats and heavy meals.
instructions: Combine yogurt, cold water, and salt in a pitcher.
Whisk vigorously or blend until frothy and smooth.
Serve cold in tall glasses, optionally with ice.

recipes.name: Rakia
recipes.description: Bulgaria's national spirit, a potent fruit brandy typically distilled from grapes or plums, always enjoyed slowly with meze appetizers.
ingredients: Shopska salata or roasted peppers for accompaniment
instructions: Pour rakia into small traditional glasses at room temperature.
Serve alongside a small plate of shopska salata or roasted peppers with sirene.
Sip slowly, alternating with bites of the salad.

imageCredit.author: The original uploader was Blue at Bulgarian Wikipedia.

recipes.name: Ayran
recipes.description: Cold salted yogurt drink — made with Bulgaria's famous yogurt (Lactobacillus bulgaricus). The essential summer drink.
instructions: Whisk yogurt until smooth
Add cold water gradually, whisking
Season with salt
Serve very cold

recipes.name: Bouillie de Mil
recipes.description: A smooth, warm millet porridge sweetened with sugar and enriched with milk, the standard breakfast across Burkina Faso's households.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh milk or powdered milk
instructions: Mix millet flour with 1 cup of cold water to form a smooth paste.
Bring remaining 3 cups of water to a boil in a pot.
Slowly pour the millet paste into the boiling water, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick and smooth.
Stir in sugar, milk, and vanilla. Serve warm in bowls.

recipes.name: Beignets Burkinabe
recipes.description: Golden fried dough balls with a hint of nutmeg, sold at every market and street corner in Ouagadougou as a beloved morning snack.
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, nutmeg, and salt in a bowl.
Add eggs and warm water, stirring until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Heat oil in a deep pot to 170C (340F).
Drop spoonfuls of dough into the hot oil and fry until golden brown and puffed, about 3 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, optionally dusted with extra sugar.

recipes.name: Kooko
recipes.description: Tangy millet porridge — Burkina's everyday breakfast drink, thinned enough to sip from a bowl. The tamarind gives it a distinctive sourness.
instructions: Mix millet flour with cold water to smooth paste
Bring more water to boil
Stir in millet paste gradually
Cook until thick, stirring constantly
Thin to drinkable consistency
Add tamarind juice, sugar, lemon
Serve warm or cool

recipes.name: Riz Gras
recipes.description: Burkina Faso's festive one-pot rice cooked in a rich tomato and meat sauce with vegetables, a celebration dish enjoyed across the country.
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot and brown the beef cubes on all sides.
Add onion and garlic, cooking until softened.
Stir in blended tomatoes, tomato paste, and Maggi cube. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add carrots, green beans, and water. Bring to a boil.
Add rice, stir, cover tightly, and reduce heat to low.
Cook for 25 minutes until rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid. Fluff and serve.

recipes.name: To with Sauce Gombo
recipes.description: The daily staple of Burkina Faso: firm millet dough served with a thick, slimy okra sauce enriched with smoked fish and soumbala.
ingredients: 2 cups millet flour or corn flour
instructions: Bring 3 cups of water to a boil. Gradually add millet flour, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon until it forms a thick, firm dough. Set aside.
Heat palm oil and saute onion until translucent.
Add tomatoes and soumbala, cooking for 5 minutes.
Add chopped okra and smoked fish. Add 1 cup of water and simmer for 15 minutes until okra is slimy and tender.
Season with salt. Serve the to in mounds with the okra sauce ladled over the top.

recipes.name: Riz Gras
recipes.description: One-pot tomato rice cooked in meat broth — the popular Burkinabè lunch. Simple, deeply flavorful, always feeds a crowd.
instructions: Brown meat, set aside
Sauté onion, garlic, add tomato paste and tomatoes
Add water, return meat, simmer 15 min
Add rice and vegetables
Cook until rice absorbs liquid and is tender
The tomato and meat juices flavor every grain

recipes.name: Poulet Bicyclette
recipes.description: The famous grilled free-range chicken of Burkina Faso, named after the bicycles used to transport them, served with onions and fried plantains.
ingredients: 1 whole free-range chicken, cut into pieces
Sliced tomatoes and onions for garnish
instructions: Marinate chicken pieces in mustard, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, paprika, salt, and pepper for at least 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet and sear chicken pieces on all sides until golden.
Add sliced onion rings, cover, and cook on medium-low heat for 35 minutes, turning occasionally.
Uncover and increase heat to crisp the skin for the last 5 minutes.
Serve with sliced tomatoes, raw onion rings, and fried plantains.

recipes.name: Ragout d'Igname
recipes.description: A hearty yam and meat stew in a rich tomato and palm oil sauce, a filling evening meal enjoyed throughout Burkina Faso.
instructions: Heat palm oil and brown the meat on all sides.
Add onion and garlic, cooking until fragrant.
Stir in blended tomatoes, tomato paste, and Maggi cube. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add yam cubes and enough water to just cover. Add the whole habanero.
Simmer for 20 minutes until yam is tender and sauce is thick.
Remove habanero before serving. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Sauce Baobab
recipes.description: Soup made from dried baobab leaves — a staple sauce in Burkina, thickened naturally by the leaves. Served over tô (millet paste).
instructions: Sauté onion in palm oil
Add tomato, cook until broken down
Add meat or fish with water
Stir in powdered baobab leaves — they thicken the sauce
Add dawadawa for deep umami
Simmer 25 min until thick and slimy-smooth
Serve over tô

recipes.name: Galettes de Niebe
recipes.description: Crispy fried black-eyed pea fritters, a protein-rich street snack found at markets across Burkina Faso.
ingredients: 2 cups black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and peeled
instructions: Blend soaked and peeled black-eyed peas with onion, habanero, and salt into a thick paste.
Beat the paste vigorously with a spoon until light and airy.
Heat oil in a deep pan. Drop spoonfuls of the paste into hot oil.
Fry until golden brown and crispy, about 4 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with spicy tomato sauce.

recipes.name: Brochettes
recipes.description: Charcoal-grilled meat skewers dusted with suya spice — sold at every roadside grill stand in Ouagadougou.
ingredients: Suya spice: ground peanuts, chili, ginger, garlic, paprika
instructions: Thread meat and onion onto skewers
Brush with oil, season with suya spice and salt
Grill over charcoal, turning frequently
Serve immediately with more suya spice for dipping

recipes.name: Brochettes de Bœuf
recipes.full_name: Brochettes de Bœuf (Street Grilled Beef Skewers)
recipes.description: Street-grilled beef skewers coated in a peanut-spice crust — Ouagadougou's night food. The Sahel version of suya, served with raw onion and mustard. West African street food videos featuring these smoky skewers consistently go viral for the charcoal grilling atmosphere.
ingredients: Suya spice: ground peanuts, cayenne, ginger, onion powder, paprika, salt
instructions: Cut beef into 2cm cubes
Make suya spice mix: toast and grind peanuts, mix with cayenne, ginger, onion powder, paprika, salt
Coat beef cubes generously in spice mix
Thread onto skewers
Grill over charcoal, turning frequently, until charred outside but juicy inside — 8-10 min
Serve with raw sliced onion and mustard on the side
In Ouagadougou, these are everywhere after dark — the charcoal smoke and spice aroma fill entire neighborhoods

recipes.name: Gonre
recipes.description: Sweet banana and peanut cakes lightly pan-fried, a simple and nourishing dessert made from two of Burkina Faso's abundant crops.
instructions: Peel bananas and mash them roughly in a bowl.
Mix in peanut flour, honey, cinnamon, and salt.
Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture into the skillet and flatten slightly.
Cook until golden brown on each side, about 3 minutes per side.
Serve warm as a sweet treat.

recipes.name: Dèguè
recipes.description: Chilled yogurt with tiny millet pearls — sweet, creamy, refreshing. Shared across West Africa but beloved in Burkina.
instructions: Steam millet couscous until tender
Cool completely
Mix with yogurt and sugar
Add vanilla or nutmeg
Serve cold

recipes.name: Bissap
recipes.description: A vibrant ruby-red hibiscus tea sweetened with sugar and brightened with lime, the most popular refreshing drink in Burkina Faso.
instructions: Bring water to a boil and add dried hibiscus flowers. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Strain the liquid into a pitcher, pressing the flowers to extract all flavor.
Stir in sugar while still warm until dissolved. Add vanilla and lime juice.
Refrigerate until cold. Serve over ice with fresh mint leaves.

recipes.name: Dolo
recipes.description: Traditional sorghum beer brewed by women in Burkina Faso, a mildly alcoholic, tangy drink central to social and ceremonial life.
instructions: Soak sorghum grain in water for 24 hours, then drain and spread on a damp cloth.
Keep the grain moist and covered for 3 days until it sprouts.
Sun-dry the sprouted grain, then grind it coarsely.
Mix the ground malt with water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 3 hours, adding water as needed.
Strain the liquid and let it cool. Allow to ferment naturally for 1-2 days.
Serve at room temperature in calabash cups.

recipes.name: Zoom Koom
recipes.description: Gingery millet drink — Burkina's refreshment of choice on hot days. Sold in plastic bags by street vendors.
instructions: Mix millet flour with cold water until smooth
Strain through cloth
Add ginger juice, sugar, lemon
Add pineapple juice if desired
Serve very cold

recipes.name: Igisafuriya
recipes.description: Hearty one-pot vegetable stew.
instructions: Peel and chop plantains and sweet potatoes
Boil beans until almost tender
Add vegetables, onion, tomatoes
Cook in palm oil until soft
Season with salt

recipes.name: Umutsima
recipes.description: Thick cassava porridge, Burundi's staple starch.
instructions: Boil water with salt
Gradually stir in cassava flour
Stir constantly for 15 min until thick
Serve warm with beans or greens

recipes.name: Igisafuriya
recipes.description: Beans and green bananas cooked together — an everyday Burundian breakfast that keeps you full until midday.
instructions: Sauté onion in palm oil
Add cooked beans and plantain slices
Add water to just cover
Simmer until plantains are tender and beans are creamy
Mash slightly to thicken
Season with salt

recipes.name: Beans with Plantains
recipes.description: The national dish — red beans with sweet plantains.
instructions: Cook beans until tender
Peel and slice plantains
Sauté onion in palm oil
Add plantains and beans, simmer 15 min
Season with salt

recipes.name: Isombe
recipes.description: Creamy cassava leaf stew enriched with peanut paste.
instructions: Pound cassava leaves, boil 30 min
Add peanut paste and palm oil
Add diced onion and tomatoes
Simmer until thick
Add dried fish if using
Serve with umutsima

recipes.name: Isombe
recipes.description: Cassava leaves pounded and cooked with peanut paste — Burundi's signature green stew, rich in protein and deeply savory.
instructions: Boil pounded cassava leaves for 30 min to remove bitterness
Drain, add fresh water
Add peanut paste, stir until dissolved
Add palm oil, onion, tomato, eggplant
Simmer until thick and creamy
Serve over rice, ugali, or boiled plantains

recipes.name: Mukeke
recipes.description: Freshwater fish from Lake Tanganyika — one of the deepest, oldest lakes on Earth — grilled over charcoal and served with ubugari. Burundi's lakeside fish restaurants have become viral destinations for African food tourism content.
ingredients: 4 whole mukeke fish (or tilapia/perch — freshwater fish)
Marinade: lemon juice, garlic, salt, chili flakes
instructions: Clean and score fish on both sides
Marinate in lemon juice, garlic, salt, and chili — 30 min
Baste with palm oil
Grill over charcoal — the skin should blister and char
Alternatively, wrap in banana leaves and grill for a smokier, steamed effect
Serve with ubugari (stiff cassava porridge) and a fresh tomato-onion salad
Lake Tanganyika's fish are some of the freshest in Africa — the lake is 20 minutes from Bujumbura's grills

recipes.name: Brochettes
recipes.description: Charcoal-grilled meat skewers — Burundi's street food staple.
instructions: Marinate meat with oil, lime, salt, pepper
Thread meat and vegetables onto skewers
Grill over charcoal until done
Serve with fries and salad

recipes.name: Tilapia with Ugali
recipes.description: Fried tilapia with thick cornmeal and fresh tomato sauce.
instructions: Season fish with lemon and salt
Fry until golden
Make ugali: boil water, stir in cornmeal until thick
Make tomato-onion sauce
Serve fish on ugali with sauce

recipes.name: Mukeke
recipes.description: Fresh fish from Lake Tanganyika in palm oil tomato sauce — Bujumbura's waterfront specialty.
instructions: Clean fish, score sides, marinate in lime and salt
Heat palm oil, sauté onion, garlic, tomato, chili
Place fish in sauce
Cook covered 10-15 min, turning once
The sauce should be thick and coat the fish
Serve with rice or ugali

recipes.name: Mandazi
recipes.description: Sweet, cardamom-scented fried dough triangles.
instructions: Mix dough, let rise 1 hour
Roll out, cut triangles
Deep fry until golden
Drain and serve

recipes.name: Agatoke
recipes.description: Fried ripe plantains — sweet, caramelized, served with every meal or as a snack. The riper the plantain, the sweeter.
instructions: Peel plantains, slice diagonally
Fry in hot oil until golden brown on both sides
Drain, sprinkle with salt
Serve hot

recipes.name: Boiled Sweet Potatoes with Honey
recipes.description: Simple, naturally sweet dessert.
instructions: Boil sweet potatoes until tender
Peel and slice
Drizzle with honey and melted butter
Dust with cinnamon

recipes.name: Ikivuguto
recipes.description: Fermented milk — Burundi's traditional dairy product, similar to thick yogurt. Sweetened with honey, it becomes a dessert.
instructions: Heat milk to warm (not boiling)
Add culture, stir
Cover, ferment at room temperature 24-48 hours
The milk thickens into tangy yogurt-like consistency
Sweeten with honey, mix with mashed banana if desired
Serve cold

recipes.name: Urwarwa
recipes.description: Traditional fermented banana wine.
instructions: Mash ripe bananas, extract juice
Mix with small amount of sorghum flour
Let ferment 3-5 days
Strain and serve

recipes.name: Ikivuguto
recipes.description: Cultured milk drink, tangy like buttermilk.
instructions: Warm milk slightly
Add starter culture
Let sit at room temp 1-2 days
Shake well before serving

recipes.name: Urwarwa
recipes.description: Banana beer — brewed for centuries in Burundi, drunk communally through long reed straws from a single gourd. A social ceremony as much as a drink.
instructions: Ripen bananas in a pit covered with leaves for days until very soft
Extract juice by squeezing through grass filter
Mix juice with roasted sorghum flour
Let ferment 1-3 days in a gourd
Strain — the beer is thick, slightly sour, mildly alcoholic
Serve communally from a shared gourd, sipped through long straws

recipes.name: Cuscuz de Milho
recipes.description: Steamed cornmeal cake — Cape Verdean breakfast staple.
instructions: Mix cornmeal with water and salt
Steam in couscous mold 20 min
Unmold, top with butter and sugar

recipes.name: Papaya with Lime
recipes.description: Fresh tropical breakfast.
instructions: Halve papaya, scoop seeds
Squeeze lime over flesh
Drizzle with honey

recipes.name: Canja de Galinha
recipes.description: Chicken rice soup — a morning restorative on the islands, especially after a night of grogue.
instructions: Simmer chicken in salted water with onion, garlic, carrot
When tender, remove chicken, shred meat
Return meat to broth, add rice
Cook until rice is very soft and broth is thick
Finish with lime juice and parsley

recipes.name: Cachupa Rica
recipes.description: Cabo Verde's national dish — a rich stew of corn, beans, and meats.
instructions: Cook corn and beans until nearly tender, ~90 min
Add pork and sausages
Add root vegetables and cabbage
Simmer until all is tender
Slice sausages on top
Season and serve

recipes.name: Atum com Molho Cru
recipes.full_name: Atum com Molho Cru (Tuna with Raw Sauce)
recipes.description: Fresh tuna with a tangy raw vegetable sauce.
instructions: Grill or sear tuna steaks
Mix tomatoes, onion, pepper, vinegar, oil, cilantro
Spoon raw sauce over tuna
Serve with rice

recipes.name: Caldo de Peixe com Banana Verde
recipes.full_name: Caldo de Peixe com Banana Verde
recipes.description: Fish broth with green banana and cassava — everyday island comfort on the windward islands.
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, tomato in oil
Add water, bring to boil
Add cassava first (takes longest)
Add green banana slices
Add fish last — it cooks fast
Season with salt, lime juice, cilantro
Serve in bowls with broth

recipes.name: Cachupa Rica
recipes.description: Cabo Verde's national dish in its full glory — the 'rica' version loaded with every meat available. A slow stew of hominy corn, beans, and whatever the family can afford. Viral food travel content from Cabo Verde always centers on cachupa — the communal pot that defines the islands.
ingredients: Dried beans (butter beans and kidney beans, soaked)
Manioc, sweet potato, green banana, squash
instructions: Soak corn and beans overnight
Boil corn and beans until nearly tender — 2+ hours
In stages, add pork ribs, beef, chorizo, linguiça
Add root vegetables: manioc, sweet potato, green banana, squash
Add cabbage in the last 20 minutes
Season with garlic, bay leaf, salt, pepper
Simmer until everything is tender and the broth thickens
Serve in deep bowls — every bowl is different, layered with different meats and vegetables
Leftovers are fried the next morning as cachupa guisada — the best hangover breakfast

recipes.name: Buzio
recipes.description: Tender conch stewed in tomato and wine.
instructions: Dice conch meat
Sauté onion, garlic, pepper
Add tomatoes and wine
Add conch, simmer 30 min
Garnish with cilantro
Serve with rice

recipes.name: Caldo de Peixe
recipes.description: Light fish broth with potatoes and plantain.
instructions: Simmer fish with vegetables 30 min
Remove fish, flake off bones
Return fish to broth
Add lime juice and cilantro
Serve in bowls

recipes.name: Xerém
recipes.description: Cracked corn stew — a humbler cousin of cachupa, eaten across Santiago island.
instructions: Cook cracked corn in water until soft, 30 min
Separately brown meat with onion and garlic
Combine corn with meat and beans
Simmer until thick and porridge-like
Season with bay leaf and salt

recipes.name: Pastéis de Atum
recipes.description: Crispy tuna-filled turnovers.
ingredients: Filling: 1 can tuna, onion, tomato, olives, egg
instructions: Make pastry dough, chill
Cook tuna filling with onion, tomato, olives, chopped egg
Fill dough circles, fold and seal
Deep fry until golden

recipes.name: Rissóis de Peixe
recipes.description: Crispy breaded fish turnovers — Portuguese pastry tradition alive in Cape Verdean celebrations.
ingredients: Filling: flaked fish, onion, parsley, tomato
instructions: Make dough by cooking flour in milk and butter until it forms a ball
Roll thin, cut rounds
Fill with seasoned fish
Fold, seal
Dip in egg, coat with breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden

recipes.name: Pudim de Queijo
recipes.description: Smooth cheese flan with caramel.
instructions: Blend cheese, eggs, sugar, milk, vanilla
Pour into caramel-lined mold
Bake in water bath at 160°C for 45 min
Chill and unmold
Dust with cinnamon

recipes.name: Doce de Papaia
recipes.description: Candied green papaya — the papaya trees grow everywhere on the islands, so this preserve is in every kitchen.
instructions: Cook grated papaya with sugar, water, and spices
Stir frequently until thick and translucent
Cool — it firms into a jam-like consistency
Serve as a dessert or with cheese

recipes.name: Grogue
recipes.description: Cape Verdean sugarcane spirit — the island's signature drink.
instructions: Press fresh sugarcane for juice
Ferment juice 5-7 days
Distill in copper pot still
Age in oak if desired

recipes.name: Pontche
recipes.description: Sweet lime and honey rum punch.
instructions: Mix grogue with honey and lime juice
Stir until honey dissolves
Serve over ice

recipes.name: Cambodian Rice Porridge
recipes.description: Cambodian rice porridge with toppings
instructions: Bring broth to boil
Add rice and ginger
Simmer 25-30 minutes
Add garlic
Season with fish sauce
Serve in bowl
Top with fried shallots and scallions
recipes.fun_fact: Rice porridge is Cambodian everyday breakfast

recipes.name: Amok
recipes.description: Cambodian steamed curry custard with fish
instructions: Mix coconut milk with curry paste
Add whisked eggs slowly
Add cut fish pieces
Add lime leaf, galangal, lemongrass
Pour into banana leaf bowls
Steam 25-30 minutes
Custard should be set but silky
Serve in banana leaf
recipes.fun_fact: Amok is Cambodian national dish

recipes.name: Samlor Somla
recipes.description: Cambodian sour soup with sour fruit
instructions: Heat broth with tamarind
Add onion and garlic
Add potatoes
Simmer 20 minutes
Add fish or meat
Simmer 15 minutes
Add sour fruit
Season with fish sauce and chili
Serve hot
recipes.fun_fact: Samlor Somla is traditional Cambodian soup

recipes.name: Nom Ansom
recipes.description: Cambodian sticky rice and banana cake
instructions: Mix sticky rice with coconut milk and salt
Spread thin layer in banana leaf
Layer banana slices
Sprinkle brown sugar
Add more rice layer
Wrap tightly
Steam 40 minutes
Serve warm or cold
recipes.fun_fact: Nom Ansom is popular Cambodian snack

recipes.name: Khmer Custard Tart
recipes.description: Cambodian creamy custard tart
instructions: Make tart dough
Line tart pan
Make custard: whisk eggs, milk, sugar, vanilla
Pour into shell
Bake at 350°F for 35-40 minutes
Custard should be set but jiggly in center
Cool completely
Top with caramelized sugar if desired
recipes.fun_fact: Custard tart shows French influence in Cambodian cooking

recipes.name: Sugar Cane Juice
recipes.description: Fresh Cambodian sugar cane juice
instructions: Extract juice from sugar cane
Squeeze through press or juicer
Add lime juice
Serve over ice
Refreshing street drink
recipes.fun_fact: Sugar cane juice is popular Cambodian street drink

recipes.name: Cambodian Beer
recipes.description: Light Cambodian lager beer
instructions: Serve ice-cold
Enjoy with meal
Popular social drink
recipes.fun_fact: Beer culture strong in Cambodia

recipes.name: Puff-Puff
recipes.description: Sweet, airy fried dough balls.
instructions: Mix dough, let rise 1 hour
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden
Drain and serve

recipes.name: Accra Banana
recipes.description: Sweet plantain fritters.
instructions: Mash plantains, mix with flour and sugar
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden brown
Serve warm

recipes.name: Beans and Puff-Puff
recipes.description: Beans in spicy palm oil sauce scooped up with puff-puff — a filling Cameroonian morning meal.
instructions: Sauté onion in palm oil
Add cooked beans, ground crayfish, pepper
Simmer until saucy
Serve alongside puff-puff for dipping

recipes.name: Ndolé
recipes.description: Cameroon's national dish — bitterleaf stew with peanuts and shrimp.
instructions: Wash bitterleaf multiple times to remove bitterness
Cook beef until tender
Add ground peanuts, palm oil, onion, garlic, ginger
Add bitterleaf, simmer 30 min
Add shrimp and crayfish, cook 10 more min
Serve with plantains or rice

recipes.name: Koki
recipes.description: Steamed bean pudding wrapped in leaves.
instructions: Blend beans to smooth paste
Mix with palm oil, onion, crayfish, seasoning
Wrap in spinach or banana leaves
Steam for 60 min
Unwrap and serve

recipes.name: Achu Soup with Yellow Soup
recipes.description: Pounded cocoyam in yellow palm oil soup — the iconic dish of Cameroon's Northwest region. The limestone gives the distinctive yellow color and slight alkaline taste.
ingredients: Yellow soup: palm oil, limestone paste (kanwa), spices
instructions: Boil cocoyam, pound into smooth, stretchy paste (achu)
Make yellow soup: heat palm oil, add dissolved limestone paste, stir until yellow and emulsified
Add cooked meat, smoked fish, spices
Shape achu into a ball in the soup bowl
Ladle yellow soup around it
Eat by pinching pieces of achu and dipping in the soup

recipes.name: Eru Soup
recipes.description: Thick, nutritious leaf soup.
instructions: Wash and shred eru leaves finely
Cook waterleaf until wilted
Add eru, smoked fish, cow skin, crayfish
Add palm oil, simmer 30 min
Season with salt
Serve with garri or fufu

recipes.name: Poulet DG
recipes.description: Director General's chicken — a celebratory Cameroonian dish.
instructions: Season and fry chicken until golden
Fry ripe plantain slices
Sauté onions, garlic, ginger, tomatoes, carrots, peppers
Add chicken back, simmer 15 min
Add fried plantains on top
Serve hot

recipes.name: Sanga
recipes.description: Corn and greens cooked in palm oil — a one-pot farmer's meal from Cameroon's grasslands.
instructions: Cook corn in water until tender
Add chopped greens
Add palm oil, crayfish, pepper
Simmer until thick and vegetables are cooked
Season with salt
Serve as main dish

recipes.name: Beignets
