instructions: Fry potatoes and onion in oil until soft
Beat eggs, season
Pour over potatoes, cook until set
Flip to cook other side
Serve in wedges

recipes.name: Café con Leche con Pan
recipes.description: The Cuban morning — strong sweet coffee with hot milk and buttered bread for dunking.
instructions: Brew very strong espresso
Heat milk until steaming
Pour equal parts espresso and hot milk into mug
Sweeten generously — Cubans like it sweet
Dunk buttered Cuban bread into the coffee

recipes.name: Cafecito
recipes.description: The Cuban coffee ritual — the secret is the espuma, a whipped sugar-and-espresso foam made from the first drops of coffee beaten with sugar until creamy. The whipping technique went viral and changed how people outside Cuba think about sweetened coffee. Every ventanita in Miami keeps the tradition alive.
ingredients: A small amount of the first drops of espresso
instructions: Begin brewing espresso in a moka pot
Immediately catch the first few drops of espresso in a cup with the sugar
Beat the sugar and initial espresso drops vigorously with a spoon — whip until it becomes a light brown, creamy paste (espuma/espumita)
This step is everything — the foam must be thick and pale
Pour the rest of the brewed coffee over the espuma
The foam rises to the top, creating a sweet, crema-like layer
Pour into small tacitas (demitasse cups)
This is not optional sweetness — the espuma IS the cafecito

recipes.name: Ropa Vieja
recipes.description: Cuba's national dish — slow-cooked shredded beef in tomato sauce.
instructions: Boil beef until tender, about 90 min
Shred beef with forks
Sauté peppers, onions, garlic in olive oil
Add tomato sauce, cumin, oregano, wine
Add shredded beef, simmer 30 min
Top with olives

recipes.name: Moros y Cristianos
recipes.full_name: Moros y Cristianos (Black Beans and Rice)
recipes.description: Black beans and rice cooked together — a Cuban essential.
instructions: Sauté onion, pepper, garlic in olive oil
Add cumin, oregano, bay leaf
Add beans with liquid
Add rice and water
Cook covered until rice is done

recipes.name: Sandwich Cubano
recipes.description: Pressed, flattened, and crispy — the iconic Cuban sandwich. The mustard and pickles cut through the rich pork.
instructions: Butter bread on both sides
Layer: mustard, ham, roast pork, Swiss cheese, pickles
Close sandwich
Press in sandwich press until flattened, crispy, and cheese melts
Cut diagonally

recipes.name: Lechón Asado
recipes.description: Slow-roasted mojo pork — the Cuban celebration centerpiece.
ingredients: 2 cups sour orange juice (or orange + lime)
instructions: Mash garlic with salt, cumin, oregano
Mix with sour orange juice
Score pork, rub marinade in
Marinate overnight
Roast at 160°C for 4 hours
Rest 20 min, serve

recipes.name: Picadillo
recipes.description: Sweet and savory ground beef hash.
instructions: Brown beef with onion, pepper, garlic
Add tomato sauce, cumin, oregano
Add olives, raisins, capers
Simmer 15 min
Serve over white rice

recipes.name: Vaca Frita
recipes.description: Twice-cooked beef — boiled, shredded, marinated, then fried crispy. The charred edges and lime are irresistible.
instructions: Boil flank steak until tender
Shred beef
Marinate in lime juice, garlic, salt for 30 min
Fry in single layer until crispy and browned
Fry onions until caramelized
Serve beef topped with onions, alongside rice and beans

recipes.name: Croquetas de Jamón
recipes.description: Crispy ham croquettes — ubiquitous Cuban snack.
instructions: Make thick béchamel with butter, flour, milk
Stir in ham and nutmeg
Chill until firm
Shape into cylinders
Dip in egg, coat in breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden

recipes.name: Tostones
recipes.description: Twice-fried green plantains — smashed flat and fried crispy. The mojo garlic-lime dipping sauce is non-negotiable.

Fry until lightly golden
Smash each piece flat
Fry again until golden and crispy
Salt immediately
Serve with mojo garlic sauce

recipes.name: Flan de Caramelo

instructions: Caramelize sugar in flan mold
Blend eggs, milks, vanilla
Pour into caramelized mold
Bake in water bath at 160°C for 60 min
Chill overnight, unmold

recipes.name: Arroz con Leche

Add milk, sugar, cinnamon stick, lime zest
Cook on low, stirring often, until thick and creamy
Add vanilla
Serve warm or cold, dusted with ground cinnamon

recipes.name: Guarapo

Add squeeze of lime
Serve over ice

recipes.name: Mojito

Add rum and ice
Top with soda water
Garnish with mint

recipes.name: Daiquirí

instructions: Combine rum, lime juice, simple syrup in shaker
Add ice, shake vigorously
Strain into chilled coupe glass

recipes.name: Halloumi and Eggs
recipes.description: Cypriot breakfast of fried halloumi and eggs.
instructions: Fry halloumi slices until golden
Fry eggs

recipes.name: Tahinopita

instructions: Make oil-based dough, rest
Roll out, spread tahini-sugar filling
Roll up, coil into pan

recipes.name: Flaouna
recipes.description: Aromatic cheese-filled pastry made for Easter — the mahlab and mastic in the dough give a distinctive flavor. Every Cypriot household bakes dozens.

Mix grated cheeses with eggs, semolina, raisins, mint
Shape dough into squares, fill generously
Fold corners over, leaving center open

recipes.name: Souvlaki with Pita

instructions: Marinate pork with oil, lemon, oregano, garlic
Thread on skewers
Grill over charcoal
Serve in pita with tzatziki, onions, tomatoes

recipes.name: Sheftalia

instructions: Mix meats with onion, parsley, cinnamon
Shape into sausages
Wrap in caul fat
Grill over charcoal until cooked through

recipes.name: Kolokasi
recipes.description: Cyprus's signature stew — taro root and pork in lemony sauce. Taro must be broken by hand so the starch thickens the broth naturally.

instructions: Brown pork and onion
Add tomato paste, celery, stock
Break kolokasi into chunks by hand (never cut)
Add to stew
Simmer 40 min until taro is tender and sauce thick
Finish with lemon juice

recipes.name: Kleftiko

Place with potatoes in roasting pan
Cover tightly with foil
Bake at 160°C for 4 hours
Lamb should fall off bone

recipes.name: Koupepia
recipes.description: Cypriot-style stuffed vine leaves with pork and mint.
instructions: Mix meat with rice, onions, herbs, spices
Fill vine leaves, roll tightly
Pack in pot seam-down
Add water, tomato paste, lemon juice
Simmer 60 min

recipes.name: Ofton Kleftiko
recipes.description: Stolen lamb — named for bandits who slow-cooked lamb in sealed underground pits to hide the smoke. Sealed cooking concentrates all the flavor.

Season with lemon juice, oregano, cinnamon, salt, pepper
Place lamb and potatoes in sealed vessel
Seal tightly — no steam should escape
Bake at 150°C for 4 hours
Do not open until serving — the lamb falls off the bone

recipes.name: Koupes

instructions: Soak bulgur, knead into shell
Make spiced meat filling
Shape bulgur around filling into torpedoes
Deep fry until crispy

recipes.name: Halloumi Grilled
recipes.description: Grilled halloumi — Cyprus's famous cheese that doesn't melt. The squeaky texture and salty char are addictive.
instructions: Brush halloumi with olive oil
Grill on high heat 2 min per side
Squeeze lemon over, sprinkle oregano and mint
Eat immediately while warm

recipes.name: Halloumi Fries
recipes.description: Halloumi fries — the Cypriot cheese that doesn't melt, cut into fry shapes and fried until golden outside and squeaky-molten inside. The cheese that 'breaks the rules' went viral globally, and halloumi fries are now on menus from London to Sydney. Cyprus lobbied for and won EU protected status for the cheese.
instructions: Cut halloumi into thick fry shapes
Dust lightly in flour — helps the exterior crisp
Fry in hot oil 2-3 min per side until golden, or air-fry at 200°C for 8 min
The outside should be crispy, the inside squeaky and molten
Squeeze lemon juice over immediately
Sprinkle fresh mint
Optional: drizzle honey for a sweet-salty contrast
Eat immediately — halloumi hardens as it cools

recipes.name: Loukoumades
recipes.description: Puffy dough balls drizzled with honey — a Cypriot favorite.
instructions: Make batter, rise 1 hour
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until golden
Drizzle with honey
Top with cinnamon and walnuts

recipes.name: Galaktoboureko
recipes.description: Crispy phyllo pie filled with semolina custard and drenched in syrup — Cypriot-Greek dessert at its most indulgent.
ingredients: Custard: 1L milk, 150g semolina, 200g sugar, 4 eggs, vanilla, butter
Syrup: 300g sugar, 200ml water, lemon juice, cinnamon stick
instructions: Make custard: cook milk, semolina, sugar until thick, cool, beat in eggs
Layer phyllo in pan, brushing each with butter
Pour in custard, top with more buttered phyllo
Score top, bake at 180°C for 35-40 min
Make syrup: boil sugar, water, lemon, cinnamon
Pour cool syrup over hot pie
Let soak before serving

recipes.name: Cypriot Coffee
recipes.description: Strong, thick coffee brewed in a briki.
instructions: Add coffee, sugar, water to briki
Heat slowly, stirring
When foam rises, pour into cups
Serve with glass of water

recipes.name: Zivania
recipes.description: Potent grape pomace spirit — Cyprus's national drink.
instructions: Collect grape pomace after pressing
Distill in copper pot still
Distill twice for purity
Serve as aperitif or digestif

recipes.name: Commandaria
recipes.description: The oldest named wine in the world — produced in Cyprus since 800 BC. Made from sun-dried grapes.
ingredients: Commandaria wine (from sun-dried Xynisteri and Mavro grapes)
instructions: Serve at room temperature or slightly chilled in small glasses
Sip slowly — it's rich, amber, and honeyed

recipes.name: Rohlik s Máslem
recipes.full_name: Rohlik s Máslem (Bread Roll with Butter)
recipes.description: The everyday Czech breakfast — crescent rolls from the bakery with butter, ham, and cheese. Simple, fast, and always good.
instructions: Split rohlíky
Spread with butter
Layer ham and cheese
Add tomato and cucumber slices
Eat with coffee

recipes.name: Lívance
recipes.description: Small, thick yeast pancakes — softer and puffier than Western pancakes. Served with plum jam and sour cream.
instructions: Mix flour, milk, eggs, sugar, yeast, salt
Let batter rise 20 min
Fry small thick pancakes in butter until golden on both sides
Stack on plate
Top with plum jam and sour cream

recipes.name: Sázené Vejce s Uzeninou
recipes.full_name: Sázené Vejce s Uzeninou (Baked Eggs with Smoked Meat)
recipes.description: Eggs fried over smoked meat — a hearty Czech breakfast, especially on weekends.
instructions: Fry sliced smoked meat in butter
Crack eggs over the meat
Cook until eggs are set
Serve in the pan with bread for dipping

recipes.name: Svíčková na Smetaně
recipes.full_name: Svíčková na Smetaně (Marinated Beef in Cream Sauce)
recipes.description: The Czech national dish — beef braised then served in a tangy cream-vegetable sauce with bread dumplings and cranberries.
instructions: Lard beef, marinate overnight with sliced vegetables, vinegar, and spices
Brown beef on all sides in butter
Add vegetables, roast until browned
Add marinade and water, braise covered 2-2.5 hours until tender
Remove beef, blend sauce with vegetables until smooth
Strain, add cream, adjust with lemon juice and sugar
Slice beef, pour cream sauce over
Serve with bread dumplings and cranberry sauce

recipes.name: Vepřo-knedlo-zelo
recipes.description: The holy Czech trinity — roast pork with crackling, bread dumplings, and sauerkraut.
instructions: Season pork with caraway, garlic, salt
Roast at 180°C for 90 min, basting frequently
Make sauerkraut: simmer with onion, caraway, pinch of sugar
Slice pork
Serve with bread dumplings and sauerkraut

recipes.name: Kulajda
recipes.description: Creamy mushroom and dill soup from South Bohemia — the dill and vinegar tang sets it apart from any other mushroom soup.
instructions: Sauté mushrooms in butter
Add diced potatoes and water, simmer until potatoes are tender
Add cream, bring back to simmer
Add generous chopped dill
Season with vinegar, salt, pepper
Poach an egg for each serving
Ladle soup into bowls with a poached egg on top

recipes.name: Smažený Sýr
recipes.description: Deep-fried cheese — a Czech institution found on every pub menu. The double breading keeps the cheese from escaping.
instructions: Coat cheese: flour, egg, breadcrumbs, egg again, breadcrumbs again (double-coat)
Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides
Serve immediately with tartar sauce and potatoes or fries

recipes.name: Guláš
recipes.description: Czech guláš — thicker than Hungarian gulyás, more onion and caraway, always served over bread dumplings.
instructions: Brown beef in batches
Slowly cook onions until deeply golden — 15 min, essential
Add paprika off heat, stir
Add tomato paste, garlic, caraway, marjoram
Add water to cover, simmer low 2 hours until beef falls apart
Sauce should be thick from dissolved onions, not flour
Serve over bread dumplings

recipes.name: Pečená Kachna
recipes.description: Roast duck with cabbage and dumplings — the Sunday and holiday centerpiece. The rendered duck fat is saved for cooking.
instructions: Season duck with caraway, marjoram, salt
Prick skin all over to render fat
Roast at 160°C for 2 hours, basting with rendered fat
Raise heat to 200°C for final 20 min to crisp skin
Rest 15 min, carve
Serve with braised cabbage and dumplings

recipes.name: Chlebíčky

instructions: Spread each bread slice with potato salad
Arrange decorative toppings
Garnish with parsley
Arrange on a platter

recipes.name: Utopenci
recipes.description: Pickled sausages — 'drowned men' in vinegar and onions. The classic Czech beer snack, found in every pub.
instructions: Slice sausages lengthwise
Layer in jar with onion rings, spices
Mix vinegar, oil, sugar, salt into brine
Pour over sausages
Seal, refrigerate at least 3 days
Serve cold with bread and beer

recipes.name: Trdelník
recipes.description: The chimney cake that took over Prague's tourist streets — dough wrapped around a cylinder, rolled in cinnamon-walnut-sugar, baked until caramelized. The hollow center gets stuffed with ice cream for Instagram. The most viral pastry debate in food tourism: tourists love it, some Czechs say it's actually Hungarian/Slovak.
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 7g yeast, 250ml warm milk, 60g sugar, 60g butter, 2 egg yolks, salt
Optional fillings: ice cream, Nutella, whipped cream
instructions: Make sweet yeast dough, let rise 1 hour
Roll dough into long strips
Wrap strips around a wooden or metal cylinder (trdelník roller)
Roll the wrapped cylinder in sugar-walnut-cinnamon mix
Bake over heat (traditionally charcoal, or in oven at 200°C) rotating until golden and caramelized
Slide off the cylinder — the hollow center is for filling
The caramelized sugar shell should be crispy and slightly charred
Fill with ice cream, Nutella, or eat plain
Prague tourists have made this the most photographed pastry in Europe — locals debate whether it's actually traditional

recipes.name: Trdelník
recipes.description: Spiral pastry baked on a cylinder — crispy, sugary, warm from the oven. Found at every Christmas market in Prague.
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 200ml warm milk, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 80g sugar, 80g butter, salt
instructions: Make enriched yeast dough, rise 1 hour
Roll into long strips
Wrap strips around a wooden cylinder, spiraling
Brush with butter
Roast over coals or bake at 200°C, rotating, until golden
Roll in cinnamon-sugar-walnut mixture while hot

recipes.name: Koláče
recipes.description: Round filled pastries — the Czech koláč. The three-filling plate (tvaroh, poppy, plum) is traditional.
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 200ml milk, 7g yeast, 2 eggs, 100g sugar, 100g butter

instructions: Make enriched dough, rise 1 hour
Shape rounds, press indentation in center

Rise 20 min
Bake at 190°C for 15-18 min

recipes.name: Czech Pilsner
recipes.description: The Czechs drink more beer per capita than any nation on Earth. Pilsner was invented in Plzeň in 1842.
instructions: The beer must be draft (čepované)
Pour slowly at an angle, creating a thick foam head
The foam should be 2-3 fingers thick — it protects the beer
Drink slowly

recipes.name: Becherovka and Tonic

Pour Becherovka
Top with tonic water
Garnish with lemon

recipes.name: Koláče

instructions: Make yeast dough
Let rise 1 hour
Shape into small buns

Make indent in center of each

Make streusel topping
Sprinkle on buns
Bake at 375°F for 20-25 minutes
Serve warm

recipes.name: Czech Schnitzel

instructions: Pound pork thin

Set up breading: flour, egg, breadcrumbs
Coat each cutlet
Heat oil to 350°F

Drain on paper towels
Serve with lemon

recipes.name: Czech Goulash

instructions: Brown beef in batches
Sauté onions
Add paprika, cook 1 minute
Add tomato paste
Add broth, bay leaf, caraway
Return beef
Simmer 45 minutes
Add vegetables
Simmer 30 more minutes
Season with salt and pepper
recipes.fun_fact: Goulash is Czech national dish shared with Hungary

recipes.name: Trdelník
recipes.description: Czech spiral pastry with sugar and cinnamon
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, 1 packet yeast, 3/4 cup milk, 1/4 cup sugar, 2 tbsp oil
instructions: Make yeast dough
Let rise 1 hour
Roll thin
Brush with oil

Roll tightly into spiral

Slide off cone

recipes.name: Medovina
recipes.description: Czech layered honey cake
ingredients: Cake: 1 cup honey, 1 cup sugar, 3 eggs, 3 cups flour, 1 tsp baking soda
instructions: Make honey cake batter
Bake in thin layers
Cool completely
Assemble layers with filling
Make frosting
Cover cake with frosting
Decorate with patterns
Let dry before serving

recipes.name: Czech Fruit Juice
recipes.description: Fresh Czech fruit juice
instructions: Blend fresh fruit with water

Add sugar to taste
Chill
Serve over ice
recipes.fun_fact: Fresh juice is popular in Czech Republic

recipes.name: Czech Beer
recipes.description: Czech Pilsner or Lager
instructions: Serve ice-cold in proper glass
Pour with head
Enjoy the craftsmanship
Pair with food
recipes.fun_fact: Czech Republic produces world's best beers and has strong beer culture

recipes.name: Fufu with Peanut Sauce
recipes.description: Cassava fufu — the starchy foundation of Congolese meals. The pounding and stirring technique determines the texture: it should be smooth, elastic, and slightly stretchy.
ingredients: Peanut sauce: 1 cup peanut paste, 2 tomatoes, 1 onion, garlic, palm oil, salt, chili pepper
instructions: Bring water to boil
Add cassava flour gradually, stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon
Stir constantly for 10-15 min — the fufu should pull away from the sides and form a smooth, elastic mass
Shape into a dome on a plate using a wet spoon
Make sauce: sauté onion and garlic in palm oil, add tomato, cook until soft
Stir in peanut paste diluted with water, add chili
Simmer 15 min until thick and oily on top
Serve fufu with peanut sauce alongside — tear pieces of fufu and dip

recipes.name: Vitumbula
recipes.description: Sweet banana fritters — sold by women at every Kinshasa market at dawn. The riper the bananas, the sweeter and more fragrant the fritters.
instructions: Mash ripe bananas to smooth paste
Mix with flour, sugar, salt, cinnamon
The batter should be thick enough to hold its shape on a spoon
Heat oil to 175°C
Drop spoonfuls of batter into hot oil
Fry until deeply golden on all sides, turning once
Drain on paper — they should be crispy outside, soft banana inside
Eat warm from the fryer

recipes.name: Loso na Madesu
recipes.description: Rice and beans cooked together — the combination is more than the sum of its parts. The bean starch gives the rice a creamy, pink-tinged quality.
instructions: Sauté onion and garlic in palm oil
Add cooked beans, mash some for creaminess
Add rice and water
Cook until rice is tender and has absorbed the bean liquid
The rice should be slightly pink from the beans and palm oil
Serve with fried ripe plantain

recipes.name: Moambe Chicken
recipes.description: DRC's national dish — chicken braised in rich, oily palm nut cream. The moambe (palm nut pulp) gives a distinctive flavor found only in Central African cooking. Often called the 'butter of Africa.'
instructions: Season chicken with salt, brown in palm oil on all sides
Remove chicken, sauté onions and garlic until soft
Add tomatoes, cook 5 min until broken down
Return chicken, add palm nut cream and 1 cup water
Bring to gentle simmer — do not boil hard or the cream separates
Cook covered 30 min
Add okra, cook 10 more min
The sauce should be thick, oily, and orange-red
Serve over rice or with fufu

recipes.name: Pondu
recipes.description: The everyday dish of the DRC — cassava leaves pounded for hours and slow-cooked with palm oil and smoked fish. Every Congolese person has eaten more pondu than anything else in their life.
ingredients: 1kg cassava leaves (pounded smooth — this takes 30+ min by hand)
instructions: Pound cassava leaves in mortar until very smooth (or use pre-ground frozen)
Boil pounded leaves in water for 30 min — this removes bitterness
Drain, add fresh water
Add palm oil, onion, garlic, chili
Add smoked fish (flaked)
Simmer 20 min until thick and dark green
The oil should float on top when done
Serve with fufu — scoop fufu, dip into pondu

recipes.name: Soso ya Mbika
recipes.full_name: Soso ya Mbika (Chicken in Pumpkin Seed Sauce)
recipes.description: Chicken in ground pumpkin seed sauce — the seeds give a rich, nutty, slightly earthy sauce unlike anything made with peanuts. A celebration dish in the Bas-Congo region.
ingredients: 2 cups pumpkin seeds (shelled, ground to paste)
instructions: Brown chicken pieces in palm oil
Sauté onions and tomato
Grind pumpkin seeds to a smooth paste — this is the sauce base
Dissolve pumpkin seed paste in warm water
Add to the pot with chicken
Simmer 30 min — the sauce thickens and turns pale green-grey
Season with chili and salt
Serve over rice or with fufu

recipes.name: Liboke
recipes.description: Fish steamed in banana leaf parcels — a Congo River tradition. The wrapping technique traps all the juices, and the unwrapping at the table is a moment of shared anticipation.
instructions: Clean fish, score sides, marinate in lemon, salt, garlic, ginger
Lay banana leaves over heat briefly to soften
Place fish on leaves, top with tomato, onion, pepper, pili-pili
Add a splash of palm oil
Wrap tightly into parcels, tie with banana leaf strips or string
Grill over charcoal or steam 25-30 min
The banana leaf steams the fish and infuses it with a subtle green flavor
Unwrap at the table — the aroma when opened is the first course

recipes.name: Madesu
recipes.description: Stewed red beans — cheap, filling, eaten almost daily. The palm oil and smoked fish transform simple beans into something deeply savory. The backbone of Congolese home cooking.
ingredients: Fufu, rice, or chikwangue to serve
instructions: Cook soaked beans until just tender, 40 min
Sauté onions and garlic in palm oil
Add tomato paste, cook until it darkens
Add beans with their cooking liquid
Add smoked fish or dried shrimp for depth
Simmer 20 min until beans are very soft and sauce is thick
Season with chili and salt
Serve with fufu, rice, or chikwangue

recipes.name: Sombe
recipes.description: Like pondu but richer — cassava leaves with peanut paste, smoked fish, and dried shrimp. Triple the protein, triple the umami. A feast-day version of everyday pondu.
instructions: Boil pounded cassava leaves 30 min to remove bitterness
Drain, add fresh water and palm oil
Add smoked fish, dried shrimp, onions, garlic
Add peanut paste dissolved in warm water
Simmer 20 min until thick, rich, and dark green
The palm oil should be visible on the surface — this means it's done
Season with chili and salt
Serve with fufu

recipes.name: Kwanga
recipes.description: Fermented cassava sticks wrapped in banana leaves — the slight sourness from fermentation is characteristic and intentional. Served alongside almost every Congolese meal.
ingredients: Cassava roots (peeled, soaked 3-4 days until fermented)
instructions: Soak peeled cassava in water 3-4 days until soft and slightly sour
Drain, pound or press into smooth paste
Shape into cylindrical sticks
Wrap tightly in banana leaves
Steam or boil 30 min until firm
Cool — the sticks become dense and slightly chewy
Slice and serve alongside stews and sauces

recipes.name: Mikate
recipes.description: Congolese doughnuts with mashed banana in the batter — the banana makes them moist and adds natural sweetness. Sold by the dozen at every street corner in Kinshasa.
instructions: Mash banana, mix with flour, sugar, yeast, salt, warm water
Beat batter until smooth and elastic
Cover, let rise 1 hour until bubbly
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until deeply golden brown all over
Drain — they should be light and airy inside
Eat warm, plain or dusted with sugar

recipes.name: Mikate
recipes.description: Kinshasa's morning doughnut — fluffy fried balls with mashed banana in the batter for sweetness. The street vendors' rapid-fire frying technique and the mountain-pile presentations have gone viral as symbols of Congolese street food culture.
instructions: Mix flour, sugar, salt, nutmeg, yeast
Add mashed banana and warm water — batter should be thick but spoonable
Cover and let rise 1-2 hours until very bubbly
Heat oil to 170°C
Drop spoonfuls into oil — they puff into irregular golden balls
Fry until deep golden on all sides — 3-4 min total
Drain on paper
The banana gives them a slight sweetness and chewiness inside
In Kinshasa, mikate vendors appear at every intersection by 6am

recipes.name: Grilled Pineapple
recipes.description: Charcoal-grilled pineapple — the sugar caramelizes over the fire, creating sticky, smoky edges. Sold as street dessert across Kinshasa.
ingredients: 1 ripe pineapple (peeled, cored, sliced into rings)
instructions: Slice pineapple into thick rings
Sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon
Grill over charcoal until caramelized and marked, 3-4 min per side
Squeeze lime juice over
Drizzle with honey if desired
Serve warm — the caramelization intensifies the sweetness

recipes.name: Beignets de Banane Plantain
recipes.description: Fried ripe plantain fritters — the plantains must be almost black for maximum sweetness. The caramelized edges are the best part.
instructions: Mash overripe plantains until smooth — they must be very ripe (black skin) for sweetness
Mix with flour, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil
Fry until dark golden — the natural sugar caramelizes
Drain and eat immediately
The exterior should be crispy-caramelized, the inside soft and sweet

recipes.name: Tangawisi
recipes.description: Fiery ginger-lemon drink — Kinshasa's favorite refreshment. The ginger should burn your throat slightly. Believed to ward off illness and boost energy.
instructions: Grate ginger, squeeze through cloth to extract juice
Mix ginger juice with lemon juice and sugar
Add cold water, stir until sugar dissolves
Adjust sweetness and ginger intensity to taste — Congolese drink it very strong
Add mint if desired
Serve over ice, very cold

recipes.name: Kasiksi
recipes.description: Traditional corn beer.
instructions: Cook corn flour into porridge
Let cool, add sugar
Ferment 3-5 days
Strain and serve

recipes.name: Lotoko
recipes.description: Artisanal corn or cassava spirit — distilled in villages across the DRC. Raw, potent, and central to every celebration. Each distiller's product tastes different.
ingredients: Distillation equipment (traditional: pot with condensation tube)
instructions: Ferment corn or cassava mash for 5-7 days
Transfer to distillation pot
Heat slowly — the vapor rises and condenses through a tube cooled with water
Collect the distillate — clear, strong, rough
The first and last portions are discarded (heads and tails)
The middle cut is lotoko — strong and fiery
Dilute if desired, or drink straight

recipes.name: Rundstykker med Ost og Marmelade
recipes.full_name: Rundstykker med Ost og Marmelade (Breakfast Rolls)
recipes.description: The Danish breakfast table — an assortment of rolls with butter, cheese, jam, and leverpostej. Each half gets its own topping. Coffee is essential, always strong.
ingredients: 4 rundstykker (Danish breakfast rolls, crusty with poppy or sesame seeds)
instructions: Split rundstykker in half
Butter each half generously
One half: top with cheese slices and tomato
Other half: spread with marmelade
Or: spread with leverpostej and cucumber
Serve with strong filter coffee

recipes.name: Æbleskiver
recipes.description: Round pancake puffs cooked in a special cast-iron pan with half-sphere molds — a December tradition. Turning them with a knitting needle takes practice, but the reward is light, pillowy spheres.
instructions: Mix flour, egg yolks, buttermilk, sugar, baking powder, soda, cardamom
Whip egg whites to stiff peaks, fold in gently
Heat æbleskive pan, add butter to each round well
Fill each well two-thirds full
Cook until bottom is set and golden, use a knitting needle or chopstick to turn each ball 90 degrees
Continue turning until they form perfect golden spheres
Dust with powdered sugar, serve with raspberry jam

recipes.name: Havregrød
recipes.description: Everyday Danish porridge — the cold milk moat around the hot oatmeal is essential. A smørklat (butter lump) melts in the center.
instructions: Bring water or milk to boil with salt
Add oats, reduce heat
Stir 5-8 min until thick and creamy
Serve in bowl with a pat of butter, brown sugar
Pour a ring of cold milk around the edges — the contrast of hot porridge and cold milk is the point

recipes.name: Smørrebrød: Stjerneskud
recipes.description: The most extravagant smørrebrød — two preparations of plaice, shrimp, asparagus, caviar, and remoulade piled high on dark rye. Named 'shooting star' for its exuberance.
ingredients: 1 piece steamed or poached plaice fillet
instructions: Butter the rugbrød, place lettuce leaf
Lay fried plaice fillet on one side
Lay steamed plaice fillet overlapping
Add a mound of shrimp
Arrange white asparagus spears
Add a spoonful of caviar
Dollop remoulade
Garnish with dill and lemon — the smørrebrød must be so loaded it's impossible to pick up
Eat with knife and fork, never your hands

recipes.name: Smørrebrød: Dyrlægens Natmad
recipes.description: The most famous named smørrebrød — supposedly invented when a veterinarian came home late and piled everything from the fridge onto one slice. Every smørrebrødsrestaurant in Copenhagen serves it.
ingredients: 2 slices salt beef (saltmadder or corned beef)
instructions: Butter rye bread generously
Spread thick layer of leverpostej
Lay salt beef slices on top
Add a spoonful of meat aspic
Top with raw onion rings and watercress
The combination is specifically: pâté, salt beef, aspic, onion — changing it makes it a different smørrebrød

recipes.name: Frikadeller
recipes.description: Denmark's defining meatball — flat-oval, fried in butter, juicy inside. The sparkling water trick makes them impossibly light. Served with red cabbage and potatoes on every family dinner table.
instructions: Mix ground meat with grated onion, egg, flour, milk, salt, white pepper, allspice
The mixture should be soft and loose — the milk or sparkling water makes them light
Shape into slightly flattened oval patties with wet hands
Fry in mixture of butter and oil on medium heat — 4-5 min per side until deeply golden
Do not press them down — they should be juicy inside
Serve with boiled potatoes, brown gravy, and pickled red cabbage

recipes.name: Smørrebrød
recipes.description: Denmark's edible art form — open-faced rye bread sandwiches built in precise architectural layers. The presentation videos and the 'you eat it with a fork' revelation went viral globally. A proper Danish lunch involves multiple smørrebrød eaten in strict order: fish, then meat, then cheese.
ingredients: Classic toppings — pick one per piece: 1) Pickled herring, raw onion rings, capers, curry sauce 2) Roast beef, remoulade, crispy onions, horseradish 3) Smoked salmon, cream cheese, dill, lemon 4) Egg and shrimp, mayo, dill, lemon
Garnish: fresh herbs, microgreens, edible flowers
instructions: Butter rye bread generously — the butter is structural, not decorative
Build toppings in layers — architecture matters
The bottom layer is the protein, the middle is sauce/spread, the top is garnish
Each smørrebrød is eaten with knife and fork, never picked up
The order matters at a traditional lunch: herring first, then meat, then cheese
Make it beautiful — Danish smørrebrød is edible art, and the presentation IS the tradition
A proper frokost (lunch) has at least three different smørrebrød

recipes.name: Flæskesteg
recipes.description: Christmas Eve dinner for 90% of Danes — the crackling (svær) must shatter when you bite it. The rind is scored obsessively tight and salted aggressively. A Danish Christmas without flæskesteg is not Christmas.
ingredients: 3kg pork loin (bone-in, with rind scored in tight parallel lines)
Rødkål (braised red cabbage): 1 red cabbage, butter, sugar, vinegar, redcurrant jelly
Brunede Kartofler (caramelized potatoes): small potatoes, sugar, butter
instructions: Score the rind in very tight parallel lines (every 5mm) — a sharp Stanley knife works better than a kitchen knife
Rub coarse salt deep into every cut
Insert bay leaves and cloves between the cuts
Pour boiling water over the rind — this opens the cuts and starts the crackling
Roast at 180°C for 2 hours, adding water to the pan to prevent burning
Raise to 220°C for the last 20 min — the rind puffs and crackles
If any patches don't crackle, blast with a kitchen torch
Rest 20 min before carving — cut between the crackling lines
Serve with rødkål and brunede kartofler

recipes.name: Stegt Flæsk med Persillesovs
recipes.full_name: Stegt Flæsk med Persillesovs (Fried Pork Belly with Parsley Sauce)
recipes.description: Voted Denmark's national dish in 2014 — crispy fried pork belly slices swimming in thick parsley sauce over boiled potatoes. Simple, heavy, and exactly what Danes want.
ingredients: Parsley sauce: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp flour, 500ml milk, large bunch parsley (finely chopped), salt, pepper, nutmeg
instructions: Fry pork belly slices slowly until the rind is crispy and the meat is golden — 5-6 min per side on medium heat
Make parsley sauce: melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 2 min, add milk gradually, simmer until thick
Add finely chopped parsley — it should be visibly very green, packed with parsley
Season with salt, pepper, nutmeg
Serve crispy pork on boiled potatoes, drench in parsley sauce

recipes.name: Kogt Torsk
recipes.full_name: Kogt Torsk (Poached Cod with Mustard Sauce)
recipes.description: Old-school Danish feast-day fish — mild poached cod with punchy mustard sauce and horseradish. Still served at many Danish homes on Christmas Eve before the pork comes out.
ingredients: Mustard sauce: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp flour, 500ml fish poaching liquid, 2 tbsp strong Danish mustard, 1 egg yolk
instructions: Salt cod generously, rest 30 min
Bring water with a splash of vinegar to gentle simmer
Poach cod 8-10 min — it should flake easily but stay moist
Make mustard sauce: melt butter, whisk flour, add poaching liquid, stir until thick, add mustard, finish with egg yolk
Serve cod on boiled potatoes with mustard sauce, grated horseradish, chopped hard-boiled egg, and melted butter

recipes.name: Pølse fra Pølsevogn
recipes.full_name: Pølse fra Pølsevogn (Hot Dog from a Cart)
recipes.description: The pølsevogn (sausage cart) is a Copenhagen institution — a bright red sausage in a bun buried under remoulade, mustard, ketchup, and mountains of fried onions. Tourist and Dane alike queue in the rain.
instructions: Boil or grill the rød pølse
Warm the bun
Place sausage in bun
Squiggle lines of ketchup, mustard, and remoulade
Pile on crispy fried onions and raw diced onions
Add sliced pickles along the side
Everything goes on top — the more toppings, the more Danish

recipes.name: Rugbrødschips
recipes.description: Crispy rye bread chips — a use for stale rugbrød. The dense, sour rye makes deeply flavored chips.
instructions: Slice rye bread paper-thin
Brush with olive oil
Sprinkle with salt and herbs
Bake at 180°C for 12-15 min until crispy
Cool — they crisp further as they cool

recipes.name: Rødgrød med Fløde
recipes.full_name: Rødgrød med Fløde (Red Berry Pudding with Cream)
recipes.description: The name is a tongue-twister foreigners use to test their Danish: rødgrød med fløde. The dessert itself is simple — stewed red berries thickened with potato starch, drowned in cold cream.
ingredients: 500g mixed red berries (strawberries, raspberries, redcurrants, rhubarb)
Cold heavy cream to pour over
instructions: Cook berries with sugar until they release juice and soften
Mix potato starch with cold water, stir into berries
Cook until thickened to a loose pudding consistency — not stiff, not runny
Pour into serving bowls
Chill until cool
Pour cold cream generously over the top

recipes.name: Drømmekage
recipes.description: Dream cake — a simple sponge topped with a caramelized coconut-brown sugar crust that goes bubbly and golden under the broiler. From the town of Brovst in North Jutland.
ingredients: Cake: 200g flour, 200g sugar, 3 eggs, 100ml milk, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp vanilla
Topping: 100g butter, 200g shredded coconut, 150g brown sugar, 3 tbsp milk
instructions: Beat eggs and sugar until fluffy
Fold in flour, baking powder, milk, vanilla
Pour into greased pan, bake at 180°C for 25 min
Make topping: melt butter, mix with coconut, brown sugar, milk
Spread topping over hot cake
Broil 3-5 min until golden and caramelized — watch carefully, it burns fast
Cool slightly before cutting

recipes.name: Kanelsnegle
recipes.description: The original Danish pastry — a cardamom-scented cinnamon roll that predates every American bakery version. The difference is the cardamom in the dough, which lifts it from 'just a cinnamon roll' to something more complex. Copenhagen bakery videos showing the rolling technique are viral staples.
ingredients: Dough: 500g flour, 80g sugar, 7g yeast, 250ml warm milk, 1 egg, 80g butter, cardamom, salt
Filling: 100g soft butter, 100g brown sugar, 2 tbsp cinnamon
instructions: Make dough with cardamom — this is what makes Danish pastry Danish, not just cinnamon
Let rise 1 hour
Roll out large rectangle, spread with butter-sugar-cinnamon filling
Roll into a tight log
Cut into 3cm slices
Place in muffin tins or on baking sheet — let rise again 30 min
Bake at 190°C for 15-18 min until golden and caramelized at edges
Glaze while warm
The cardamom in the dough is non-negotiable — without it, it's just a cinnamon roll

recipes.name: Gløgg
recipes.description: Danish mulled wine — heavier than Swedish glögg, with port and aquavit. The boozy raisins and almonds at the bottom of the mug are half the fun. A December constant.
instructions: Put raisins and almonds into serving mugs
Heat wine with sugar, port, and all spices — do not boil
Simmer 10 min until fragrant
Add aquavit off heat
Ladle into mugs, making sure each gets raisins and almonds
The raisins and almonds at the bottom are part of the experience — eat them with a spoon

recipes.name: Kaffe
recipes.description: Denmark drinks more coffee per capita than Italy. Filter-brewed, medium-roast, always with cream. The vehicle for hygge — no cozy moment exists without it.
instructions: Brew strong filter coffee — Danes drink more coffee per capita than almost anywhere
Serve in a proper cup, not a mug
Add a splash of cream
Drink throughout the day, especially during hygge

recipes.name: Smørrebrød
recipes.description: Danish open sandwich with various toppings
ingredients: Various toppings: cheese, ham, herring, hard-boiled egg
instructions: Slice dark rye bread
Butter generously
Top with main ingredient
Arrange garnishes attractively
Serve immediately
Eat with knife and fork
recipes.fun_fact: Smørrebrød is Denmark's iconic lunch and breakfast item

recipes.name: Danish Meatballs
recipes.description: Danish small meatballs in sauce
instructions: Soak breadcrumbs in milk
Mix with meat, egg, onion, salt, pepper, nutmeg
Form into small balls
Brown in butter
Make sauce: whisk flour into drippings
Add broth, simmer 10 minutes
Add cream
Add meatballs back
Simmer 10 more minutes
recipes.fun_fact: Danish meatballs are served at every celebration

recipes.name: Flødeboller
recipes.description: Danish chocolate-covered cream cake
instructions: Make almond base: crush almonds with sugar and egg white
Form into small cakes
Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes
Cool completely
Make whipped cream filling
Top each cake with cream
Melt chocolate
Dip entire cake in chocolate
Set on baking paper
Refrigerate until set
recipes.fun_fact: Flødeboller is Denmark's favorite treat and comfort food

recipes.name: Danish Pastry
recipes.description: Buttery laminated Danish pastry
ingredients: Dough: 3 cups flour, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp yeast, 3/4 cup milk
instructions: Make dough, let rise
Laminate with butter layers
Fold and turn multiple times
Chill between folds
Shape into croissants or twists
Let proof
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 400°F for 20-25 minutes
Serve warm or at room temperature
recipes.fun_fact: Danish pastry is world-famous and is eaten throughout the world

recipes.name: Æbleskiver
recipes.description: Danish spherical pancakes filled with jam
instructions: Make batter from flour, sugar, baking powder, eggs, milk
Heat æbleskiver pan (special pan with round molds)
Add butter to each mold
Pour batter halfway
Add apple slice or jam
Pour more batter
Bake until golden on outside
Use needle to turn while baking
Cook until spheres are done
Dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon
recipes.fun_fact: Æbleskiver are traditional Danish dessert and street food

recipes.name: Gløgg
recipes.description: Danish spiced drink
instructions: Heat cider and juice
Add spices
Simmer 15 minutes
Strain if desired
Pour into cups
Add orange slice
Serve hot
recipes.fun_fact: Gløgg is traditional Danish Christmas drink

recipes.name: Danish Beer
recipes.description: Danish lager beer
instructions: Serve ice-cold
Pour with head
Enjoy
Cheers
recipes.fun_fact: Denmark has strong beer tradition and many breweries

recipes.name: Laxoox
recipes.description: Spongy, one-sided pancake covered in tiny holes — the fermented batter creates the characteristic perforations. Eaten at every meal in Djibouti, rolled around stews or dipped in honey.
ingredients: 2 cups flour (or mix of wheat and cornmeal)
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, sugar, salt with warm water to thin, pourable batter
Cover, ferment 2-4 hours or overnight — the batter should be bubbly and slightly sour
Heat a flat pan, pour batter in a spiral from outside to center
Cook on one side only — the top gets hundreds of tiny holes as steam escapes
The bottom should be golden, the top spongy and perforated
Roll or fold, serve with tea, honey, or stews

recipes.name: Foul Medames
recipes.description: Slow-cooked fava beans mashed with cumin, tomato, and olive oil — the same dish eaten across the Horn of Africa and Middle East, connecting Djibouti to both worlds.
instructions: Soak fava beans overnight, cook until very soft — 60 min or more
Mash roughly, leaving some beans whole for texture
Sauté onion and garlic in oil, add cumin and chili
Mix into beans
Add tomato, drizzle olive oil and lemon juice
Top with hard-boiled egg
Serve with laxoox for scooping

recipes.name: Muufo iyo Suqaar
recipes.full_name: Muufo iyo Suqaar (Flatbread with Sautéed Meat)
recipes.description: Thick corn flatbread with spiced sautéed meat — the muufo is dense and chewy, perfect for scooping up the saucy, spiced meat cubes. A hearty Djiboutian breakfast.
ingredients: Muufo: corn flour, wheat flour, water, salt
Suqaar: 400g beef or goat (diced small), onion, green pepper, tomato, garlic, cumin, coriander, chili, oil, salt, lime
instructions: Make muufo: mix flours with water and salt, shape into thick disc, cook on flat griddle until firm and slightly charred on both sides
Make suqaar: heat oil, brown diced meat quickly
Add onion, pepper, garlic, cook until softened
Add tomato, cumin, coriander, chili
Cook until meat is tender and sauce coats the pieces
Squeeze lime over
Tear muufo into pieces, scoop up suqaar

recipes.name: Laxoox
recipes.description: Djibouti's spongy, crater-covered breakfast crepe — fermented batter poured on a hot griddle, cooked on one side only. The hundreds of tiny holes form naturally as the fermentation creates steam. Laxoox (also called canjeero) is viral for its hypnotic bubble-forming process on the griddle.
ingredients: 2 cups flour (or mix of regular and whole wheat)
1 cup fermented batter (flour + water left overnight)
instructions: Mix fermented batter with flour, water, salt, touch of sugar — consistency of thin pancake batter
The fermentation gives it a tangy flavor and the signature bubbles
Pour onto hot, greased griddle or non-stick pan
Cook on one side only — do not flip
The surface develops hundreds of tiny holes as steam escapes from the fermented batter
The bottom is golden, the top is spongy and crater-covered
Stack and serve with butter and honey drizzled on top
Eat by tearing and dipping — this is breakfast from the Horn of Africa to the Gulf

recipes.name: Skoudehkaris
recipes.description: Djibouti's national dish — fragrant lamb and rice.
instructions: Brown lamb with onions and garlic
Add spices and tomatoes
Add rice and water
Cook covered until rice absorbs liquid

recipes.name: Maraq
recipes.description: Warming spiced meat and vegetable soup.
instructions: Simmer meat until tender
Add diced vegetables
Season with spices
Cook until vegetables are soft
Garnish with cilantro

recipes.name: Cambulo
recipes.description: Sweet-savory red bean rice — the butter, sesame oil, and sugar combination seems unusual but is beloved in Djibouti. Eaten during Ramadan and celebrations.
instructions: Cook rice normally
Mix hot rice with cooked beans
Add generous butter or ghee
Drizzle sesame oil
Sweeten with sugar — yes, it's sweet, savory, and oily at the same time
Serve as a main dish

recipes.name: Fah-Fah
recipes.description: Hearty goat soup — Djibouti's comfort food.
instructions: Boil goat meat with onions 45 min
Add tomatoes, chili, spices
Simmer 15 more min
Garnish with cilantro
Serve with canjeero

recipes.name: Sambuusa
recipes.description: Crispy fried triangular pastries filled with spiced meat — the Djiboutian version of samosa. Every household has their own spice blend. Essential during Ramadan iftar.
ingredients: Pastry: 2 cups flour, oil, water, salt
Filling: 300g ground beef or lamb, onion (finely diced), garlic, chili flakes, cumin, coriander, salt
instructions: Make thin pastry: mix flour, oil, water, salt, knead until smooth
Roll very thin, cut into strips
Make filling: cook ground meat with onion, garlic, spices until dry
Place filling on strip, fold into triangle shape, sealing as you go
Each fold creates a neat triangular pocket
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve hot with lime — they're best eaten immediately

recipes.name: Bariis Iskukaris
recipes.description: Djibouti's celebration rice — spiced with xawaash (the Somali-Djiboutian spice blend), layered over slow-cooked lamb. Served on a communal platter, eaten together.
ingredients: Xawaash spice mix: cumin, coriander, turmeric, cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, black pepper
instructions: Brown meat in oil with one sliced onion
Add garlic, tomatoes, xawaash spice mix
Add water, simmer 25 min until meat is tender
Fry second onion until golden
Add raisins, carrot, potato to the meat
Layer soaked rice on top
Add enough broth to cover rice by 1cm
Cook covered on low 20 min until rice absorbs all liquid
The rice should be fluffy and each grain separate, perfumed with the spice mix
Serve on a large communal platter, meat underneath rice

recipes.name: Bajiya
recipes.description: Crunchy lentil fritters.
instructions: Grind lentils coarsely
Mix with onion, chili, cumin
Fry spoonfuls until golden

recipes.name: Nafaqo
recipes.description: Crispy breaded potato balls with a spiced meat center — popular street food, especially during Ramadan evenings.
ingredients: Filling: 200g ground beef, onion, garlic, cumin, chili, salt
instructions: Mash potatoes smooth
Cook filling: brown meat with onion, garlic, spices until dry
Take a ball of potato, flatten in palm, place filling in center
Close potato around filling, shaping into smooth ball
Dip in beaten egg, roll in breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden all over
Cut open to reveal the surprise meat center

recipes.name: Halwo
recipes.description: Jewel-toned, aromatic cornstarch halva.
instructions: Dissolve cornstarch in water
Make sugar syrup
Cook cornstarch mixture, add butter and sugar syrup
Stir until thick and translucent
Add spices, set in mold

recipes.name: Bur Muusbaar
recipes.description: Date balls rolled in sesame — a sweet snack that stores well in the heat. Dates are central to Djiboutian food culture, especially during Ramadan.
instructions: Mash dates with a little ghee until sticky
Mix in ground peanuts and cardamom
Shape into small balls
Roll in toasted sesame seeds
Let firm up at room temperature

recipes.name: Shaah
recipes.description: Aromatic spiced milk tea.
instructions: Boil tea with spices 5 min
Add milk and sugar
Strain and serve hot

recipes.name: Qishr
recipes.description: Tea brewed from coffee cherry husks.
instructions: Boil coffee husks with spices 10 min
Strain, sweeten
Serve hot

recipes.name: Bakes
recipes.description: Puffy fried dough — Caribbean morning staple.
instructions: Mix dough, rest 10 min
Flatten pieces
Deep fry until golden

recipes.name: Cocoa Tea with Bread
recipes.description: Rich cocoa drink from local cocoa sticks.
instructions: Grate cocoa stick into boiling water
Add milk, sugar, spices
Simmer 5 min, strain
Serve with buttered bread

recipes.name: Saltfish Souse
recipes.description: Salt cod 'souse' — cured fish dressed with lime, onion, and fiery Scotch bonnet. A bright, acidic morning dish that wakes you up faster than coffee.
instructions: Boil salt cod 5 min, drain, flake into pieces
Mix with sliced onion, cucumber, Scotch bonnet
Dress generously with lime juice and olive oil
Add parsley, black pepper
Let marinate 10 min
Serve with sliced avocado and bakes (fried dough)

recipes.name: Mountain Chicken
recipes.description: Dominica's national dish — not poultry, but the legs of the giant crapaud frog, fried and served with Creole sauce. Named 'mountain chicken' because of its taste. Now critically endangered, the dish lives on in cultural memory and with chicken substitutes.
ingredients: 4 crapaud (giant dodo frog) legs — or substitute chicken thighs if crapaud is unavailable
Seasoning: lime juice, garlic, thyme, scallion, parsley, Scotch bonnet pepper
Creole sauce: tomato, onion, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, lime
instructions: Clean frog legs, season heavily with lime, garlic, thyme, scallion, Scotch bonnet
Marinate overnight in the fridge
Dredge in seasoned flour
Fry in hot oil until golden and crispy — the meat inside should be white and tender
Make Creole sauce: sauté onion, garlic, add tomato, thyme, Scotch bonnet, lime
Serve fried legs with Creole sauce
Note: crapaud is now endangered — this dish is increasingly made with chicken as a cultural preservation

recipes.name: Callaloo Soup
recipes.description: Thick green soup of dasheen leaves, coconut milk, crab, and dumplings — Dominica's soul food. The salted pigtail gives deep umami, and the whole Scotch bonnet gives aroma without lethal heat (unless someone breaks it).
instructions: Boil soaked salted pigtail until tender, 30 min
Shred dasheen leaves, add to pot with coconut milk
Add okra, onion, garlic, thyme, whole Scotch bonnet (don't burst it unless you want extreme heat)
Simmer 25 min until dasheen leaves break down into thick green soup
Add crab pieces
Make small flour dumplings, drop into soup
Cook 10 more min
The soup should be thick, green, and rich with coconut
Remove Scotch bonnet before serving

recipes.name: Provisions Plate
recipes.description: A plate of boiled root vegetables — dasheen, yam, green banana, breadfruit — with salt fish and avocado. The foundation of Dominican cooking, simple and sustaining.
instructions: Peel and chop root vegetables into large chunks
Boil in salted water until each is tender — dasheen takes longest, banana the least
Drain, arrange on plate
Serve with butter, flaked salt fish, sliced avocado
Drizzle coconut milk over the provisions

recipes.name: Mountain Chicken
recipes.description: Dominica's most famous and controversial dish — giant frog legs so meaty they're called 'mountain chicken.' Now critically endangered from chytrid fungus, this dish documents a culinary tradition that made Dominica unique. The 'why is it called chicken?' reveal went viral on food travel channels.
ingredients: 8 crapaud legs (giant ditch frog — Dominica's 'mountain chicken')
Seasoning: lime juice, garlic, thyme, green seasoning (cilantro, chive, celery, parsley, pepper)
Creole sauce: tomatoes, onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme
instructions: Note: crapaud is now critically endangered — this recipe documents a cultural tradition
Clean and season frog legs with lime juice, garlic, thyme, green seasoning
Marinate at least 1 hour
Dredge in seasoned flour
Fry until golden and crispy — the meat is white, tender, tastes like chicken
Make Creole sauce: sauté onion, garlic, add tomatoes, Scotch bonnet, thyme, simmer
Serve fried legs with Creole sauce, rice, and provisions (root vegetables)
Dominica is the only place this was a national dish — the name 'mountain chicken' refers to the taste and the fact that the frogs live in the mountains

recipes.name: Creole Fish
recipes.description: Fried fish in spicy Creole tomato sauce — the way fish is eaten across Dominica. The fish is seasoned with local 'green seasoning' (herbs blended into a paste), fried crispy, then smothered in sauce.
ingredients: 4 fresh fish fillets or whole snapper
Seasoning: garlic, thyme, scallion, parsley, salt, black pepper
Creole sauce: 2 onions (sliced), 3 tomatoes, garlic, thyme, Scotch bonnet, green pepper, lime juice, oil
instructions: Clean fish, score sides if whole, marinate in lime, garlic, thyme, scallion, salt
Let sit at least 30 min
Dredge in flour, fry until golden and crispy on both sides
Make Creole sauce: sauté onions and garlic in oil until soft
Add sliced green pepper, tomatoes, thyme, Scotch bonnet
Cook until sauce is thick and fragrant
Pour sauce over fried fish
Squeeze fresh lime over everything
Serve with provisions (boiled root vegetables) or rice

imageCredit.author: Photo by Victor Monsour of Monsour's Photography

recipes.name: Titiwi Accras
recipes.description: Crispy fritters made with tiny river fish.
ingredients: 1 cup titiwi (tiny fish) or salt cod
instructions: Mix fish with batter ingredients
Drop spoonfuls in hot oil
Fry until golden and crispy

recipes.name: Goat Water
recipes.description: Slow-cooked goat stew with dumplings — Dominica's answer to comfort food. The bones give the broth incredible body. The splash of rum near the end is the secret.
instructions: Season goat with garlic, thyme, salt, pepper
Brown in oil
Add onion, cloves, bay leaf, Scotch bonnet
Add water to cover, bring to simmer
Cook low 60-90 min until goat is very tender
Add breadfruit if using
Make small flour dumplings, add to stew
Add a splash of rum
Simmer 15 more min
The stew should be thick, rich, and deeply flavored from the bones

recipes.name: Cassava Farine
recipes.description: Toasted cassava granules — Dominica's traditional Kalinago food.
instructions: Grate cassava, squeeze out liquid
Toast in dry pan, stirring constantly
Add butter and salt
Cook until golden granules form

recipes.name: Accra and Floats
recipes.description: Salt cod fritters paired with plain fried bread — Caribbean street food eaten in Dominica at any hour, especially Saturday mornings.
ingredients: Accra: salt cod (soaked, flaked), flour, baking powder, onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme, oil for frying
Floats: flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, butter, water, oil for frying
instructions: Accra: mix flaked salt cod with flour, baking powder, onion, garlic, Scotch bonnet, thyme into thick batter
Drop spoonfuls into hot oil, fry until golden
Floats: make simple dough, shape into rounds, fry until puffy and golden
Serve accra and floats together — the salty cod fritters and plain fried bread complement each other

recipes.name: Banana Bread
recipes.description: Moist banana bread with island nutmeg.
instructions: Mash bananas, cream butter and sugar
Add eggs and vanilla
Fold in flour, baking soda, nutmeg
Bake at 175°C for 60 min

recipes.name: Coconut Fudge
recipes.description: Dense coconut fudge — made with freshly grated coconut from the trees that grow everywhere. A simple sweet sold in paper bags at every village shop.
instructions: Cook sugar and water to soft ball stage
Add grated coconut, lime zest, vanilla, salt
Stir constantly until mixture thickens and pulls from the sides of the pot
Pour onto greased tray
Score into squares while warm
Let cool and harden
Break into pieces

recipes.name: Sea Moss Drink
recipes.description: Creamy, nutritious sea moss smoothie.
instructions: Soak sea moss overnight, wash
Boil until dissolved
Blend with milk, sugar, spices
Chill and serve

recipes.name: Rum Punch
recipes.description: Classic Caribbean rum punch.
instructions: Mix rum, lime, syrup, bitters
Serve over ice
Grate nutmeg on top

recipes.name: Mangú
recipes.description: Mashed green plantain with 'los tres golpes' (the three hits): fried salami, fried egg, and pickled red onion. THE Dominican breakfast — eaten every single morning by millions. The pickled onion on top is non-negotiable.
instructions: Peel green plantains, cut into chunks, boil in salted water until very tender — 20 min
Drain, reserving some cooking water
Mash plantains with butter, adding cooking water for smoothness — it should be creamy, not gluey
Make los tres golpes (the three hits) to go with it:
Fry salami until crispy on both sides
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Pickle onions: sauté sliced red onion in oil with vinegar until soft and tangy
Plate mangú topped with pickled onion, fried salami, and fried egg alongside
Some add fried cheese for the fourth 'hit'

recipes.name: Avena
recipes.description: Creamy oat beverage with cinnamon and lime.
instructions: Cook oats in milk with cinnamon and lime zest
Add sugar and vanilla
Blend until smooth
Serve warm or cold

recipes.name: Yaroa
recipes.description: Loaded fries — a late-night Dominican street creation. Fries buried under seasoned meat, ketchup, mayo, and melted cheese. Eaten at 2am from a food cart after a night out.
instructions: Fry thick-cut potatoes until golden and crispy
Cook seasoned meat (ground beef with sofrito)
Layer in a takeaway container: fries on bottom, meat on top
Drizzle heavily with ketchup and mayonnaise
Cover with mozzarella cheese
Put under broiler until cheese melts
Eat with a fork — it's a beautiful mess

recipes.name: Mangú con Los Tres Golpes
recipes.description: The Dominican Republic's national breakfast — mashed green plantain with 'the three strikes': fried egg, fried salami, and fried cheese, topped with tangy pickled red onions. Mangú videos showing the cold-water mashing technique are viral Dominican food content, and the dish is a point of fierce national pride.
ingredients: Los tres golpes: fried eggs, fried Dominican salami, fried white cheese
Pickled red onions (cebolla curtida): red onion, lime juice, vinegar, oregano, olive oil
instructions: Boil plantains until very tender
Mash with butter, cooking water, and a splash of milk — must be smooth but thick
The key: add cold water to hot plantain while mashing — this is the Dominican technique for silky texture
Fry eggs sunny-side up
Fry sliced Dominican salami until crispy and curled
Fry thick slices of queso blanco until golden
Make cebolla curtida: slice red onion, soak in lime juice and vinegar with oregano and olive oil
Plate mangú in center, arrange the three strikes around it: eggs, salami, cheese
Top mangú with pickled onions
This is THE Dominican breakfast — 'los tres golpes' means 'the three strikes'

recipes.name: La Bandera
recipes.description: The Flag — rice, beans, and meat, the daily lunch of every Dominican. Named because the red beans, white rice, and meat represent the flag's colors. It is eaten so universally that 'lunch' and 'la bandera' are practically synonyms.
ingredients: White rice (2 cups, cooked fluffy — each grain separate)
Red kidney beans: cooked with sofrito (onion, garlic, pepper, cilantro, oregano), tomato sauce, cumin
Carne guisada (stewed chicken or beef): seasoned with sazón, adobo, oregano, braised in tomato
instructions: Cook rice: rinse until water runs clear, cook with oil and salt — every grain must be separate, never sticky
Make beans: sauté sofrito (onion, garlic, pepper, cilantro), add cooked beans, tomato sauce, cumin, simmer until thick and creamy
Make meat: season chicken or beef with sazón, adobo, oregano, brown, then braise in tomato sauce until tender
Fry tostones or sweet plantain
Plate: rice takes half the plate, beans go over the rice, meat alongside, salad on the side, plantain on the edge
The rice must be white and fluffy — Dominican identity is partly rice identity

recipes.name: Sancocho
recipes.description: Seven-meat stew with root vegetables — the Dominican gathering dish. Making sancocho is a family event: everyone helps, everyone eats. The broth is thick, the meats varied, and the bowl is bottomless. A national ritual more than a recipe.
instructions: In a massive pot, brown seasoned meat pieces (traditionally seven meats: chicken, pork, goat, beef, longaniza, smoked pork, beef ribs)
Add water, bring to simmer
Add root vegetables in order of cooking time: yuca and yam first, then potato, then green plantain, then corn
Add sofrito: sautéed onion, garlic, pepper, cilantro, recao (culantro)
Add sour orange juice or lime juice — the acid is essential
Simmer until everything is tender and broth is thick from the dissolved starches
The broth should be cloudy and substantial — not a clear soup
Serve in large bowls with white rice on the side and avocado
Made for Christmas, New Year's, or whenever the whole family gathers

recipes.name: Chivo Guisado
recipes.description: Slow-braised goat — the sour orange marinade tenderizes the meat and adds a citrus depth. A weekend and celebration dish, especially in the Cibao region.
ingredients: Sour orange juice (or lime + orange juice)
instructions: Marinate goat in sour orange, garlic, oregano, sazón for 2+ hours
Brown goat pieces in oil
Add onion, pepper, garlic, cook until soft
Add tomato paste, wine, olives, capers
Add water to partially cover
Braise low and slow, 90 min, until goat is fall-off-bone tender
The sauce should reduce to thick, dark gravy
Serve with white rice and tostones

recipes.name: Mofongo
recipes.description: Fried plantain mashed with garlic and pork cracklings in a wooden mortar — Puerto Rican in origin but deeply Dominican. The pilón pounding is rhythmic and practiced. Served in a dome with broth pooling around it.
ingredients: Garlic (6+ cloves, mashed into paste with olive oil and salt)
Broth: chicken or shrimp broth to pour over
instructions: Peel plantains, slice into thick rounds
Fry in oil until golden but not too crispy — they'll be mashed
While hot, place fried plantain in a pilón (wooden mortar)
Add mashed garlic-oil paste and crushed chicharrón
Pound with pestle — the motion is fold and press, not smash
The mofongo should be chunky-smooth, not puréed — texture matters
Shape into a dome in a bowl
Pour hot chicken or shrimp broth around the base
Serve with stewed shrimp, chicken, or pork on top

recipes.name: Pescado con Coco
recipes.description: Fish simmered in coconut milk.
instructions: Season fish with lime and salt
Sauté vegetables
Add coconut milk, simmer
Add fish, cook gently 15 min
Garnish with cilantro

recipes.name: Pollo al Horno Dominicano
recipes.full_name: Pollo al Horno Dominicano (Dominican Baked Chicken)
recipes.description: Dominican roast chicken — what makes it Dominican is the aggressive seasoning: sazón, adobo, sour orange, and oregano. Every Dominican can identify this chicken by smell alone.
ingredients: Marinade: sour orange juice, garlic, oregano, sazón, adobo, cumin, black pepper, olive oil
instructions: Season chicken aggressively with all spices and sour orange — really rub it in
Marinate overnight if possible — at minimum 2 hours
Place in roasting pan with onion, pepper, potatoes
Roast at 190°C for 55-60 min, basting with pan juices
The skin should be golden, crispy, and deeply seasoned
The adobo and sazón create a flavor profile that is distinctly Dominican
Serve with rice, beans, and ensalada verde

recipes.name: Empanadas de Yuca
recipes.description: Crispy yuca-dough empanadas — the cassava shell shatters into crispy shards when you bite through to the seasoned beef filling. Served with ketchup, which foreigners question and Dominicans defend fiercely.
ingredients: Dough: 1kg yuca (cassava, boiled and mashed), 2 tbsp butter, salt, achiote oil (for color)
Filling: seasoned ground beef with sofrito, olives, capers, hard-boiled egg
Ketchup to serve (yes, ketchup — this is Dominican tradition)
instructions: Boil yuca until very soft, drain, mash until completely smooth — no lumps or they'll crack when frying
Mix with butter, salt, and achiote oil for golden color
Flatten a ball of dough in your palm
Place filling in center: seasoned beef, a piece of olive, a slice of hard-boiled egg
Close and seal edges — the yuca dough is more fragile than wheat, handle gently
Deep fry until golden and crispy — the yuca shell should shatter when bitten
Serve with ketchup — this is the authentic Dominican way

recipes.name: Chimichurri Burger
recipes.description: Not to be confused with Argentine chimichurri sauce — this is the Dominican street burger. Loaded with cabbage slaw and sauces in a soft pan de agua bun. The late-night fuel of Santo Domingo.
ingredients: Cabbage slaw (shredded cabbage, tomato, onion, lime)
instructions: Season patties with sazón, garlic, oregano
Grill or fry until cooked through
Toast the pan de agua bun
Layer: bun, ketchup, mayo, patty, cabbage slaw
Smash it all together
Serve with fries or tostones on the side

recipes.name: Habichuelas con Dulce
recipes.description: Sweet bean cream — a Lenten dessert of puréed red beans with coconut milk, spices, and sweet potato. Sounds impossible, tastes like a rich, creamy pudding. Served cold during Holy Week to the whole neighborhood. Dominicans bring it door to door.
ingredients: 2 cups red kidney beans (cooked very soft)
Whole milk cookies (galletas de leche) to serve
instructions: Blend cooked beans until very smooth
Strain through a fine sieve — the dessert must be silky, no bean skins
Heat bean purée with evaporated milk, coconut milk, cinnamon, cloves
Add diced sweet potato, cook until tender
Add sugar, butter, raisins, vanilla
Simmer until thick and creamy — it should coat a spoon
Chill — it's served cold during Lent and Easter
Pour into glasses or bowls, top with milk cookies for dipping
The cookies get soft as they soak up the bean cream

recipes.name: Bizcocho Dominicano
recipes.description: The Dominican birthday cake — yellow cake with pineapple filling and dramatic meringue frosting. Every birthday, every quinceañera, every celebration. The meringue is piled sky-high.
ingredients: Cake: butter, sugar, eggs, flour, baking powder, milk, vanilla, pineapple juice
Meringue frosting: egg whites, sugar, cream of tartar
Pineapple filling: crushed pineapple, sugar, cornstarch
instructions: Cream butter and sugar, add eggs one at a time
Add flour alternately with milk and pineapple juice
Bake in layers at 175°C for 25-30 min
Make pineapple filling: cook crushed pineapple with sugar and cornstarch until thick
Make meringue: whip egg whites with sugar and cream of tartar until stiff and glossy
Assemble: cake layer, pineapple filling, repeat, frost with meringue
The meringue should be dramatically swirled and tall
Torch or broil meringue peaks until golden

recipes.name: Morir Soñando
recipes.description: Creamy orange-milk drink — do not let it curdle.
instructions: Mix cold milk with sugar and vanilla
Slowly add cold orange juice while stirring
Serve immediately over ice

recipes.name: Mamajuana
recipes.description: Dominican herbal liqueur — rum, red wine, and honey infused with bark and roots. Every Dominican household has a bottle, constantly refilled. Believed to be an aphrodisiac and general cure-all. The bark lasts for years.
ingredients: Bark and herbs: cat's claw bark, timacle bark, bohuco root, star anise, cinnamon sticks, cloves (pre-packaged mamajuana bark mix)
instructions: Fill bottle with bark and herbs — these are sold as pre-packaged mixes across the DR
First soak: fill with cheap red wine, let sit 1-2 days, then discard the wine (this 'cures' the bark)
Second fill: add equal parts dark rum, red wine, and honey
Let infuse for at least a week — longer is better
Strain and drink in small glasses
The same bark can be re-used for years — just top off with more rum, wine, and honey
Each family's bottle tastes different and is never empty for long

recipes.name: Tapai
recipes.description: Mildly sweet fermented cassava — traditional Timorese breakfast.
instructions: Serve tapai in bowl
Top with coconut milk and sugar

recipes.name: Katupa
recipes.description: Compressed rice cakes wrapped in coconut leaves.
instructions: Weave coconut leaves into pouches
Fill with washed rice
Boil 60 min until rice is compact
Unwrap and slice
Serve with curry or coconut

recipes.name: Katupa
recipes.description: Rice cooked inside woven coconut leaf pouches — the leaves imprint a diamond pattern onto the compressed rice. The intricate weaving technique has gone viral as an example of Southeast Asian edible craft. A festive food in East Timor, especially for celebrations and ceremonies.
instructions: Weave coconut leaves into small diamond-shaped pouches — this is the art
Fill each pouch about half with rice — it swells as it cooks
Boil pouches in salted coconut milk-water for 1 hour
The rice compresses inside the leaf, becoming a dense, fragrant cake
Unwrap the leaf — the rice has a diamond pattern imprinted from the weaving
Serve with any stew or curry, or just with sambal
The weaving technique is passed down through generations — it takes practice to learn the fold

recipes.name: Ikan Pepes
recipes.full_name: Ikan Pepes (Spiced Fish in Banana Leaf)
recipes.description: Fish steamed in banana leaf with aromatic spice paste.
instructions: Blend spice paste
Coat fish with paste
Wrap in banana leaves
Grill or steam 30 min

recipes.name: Batar Da'an
recipes.full_name: Batar Da'an (Corn and Mung Bean Stew)
recipes.description: Thick corn and bean stew — a Timorese staple.
instructions: Cook corn and mung beans
Add pumpkin and cassava leaves
Add coconut milk, simmer until thick

recipes.name: Batar Da'an
recipes.full_name: Batar Da'an (Corn and Mung Bean Stew)
recipes.description: East Timor's traditional staple — corn and mung beans simmered with pumpkin and coconut milk into a thick, nourishing stew. Corn, not rice, is the ancestral grain of Timor-Leste. The hearty simplicity and the beautiful golden color from the pumpkin have earned attention from food travel creators.
instructions: Boil soaked corn until starting to soften — 30 min
Add mung beans, continue cooking
Add pumpkin cubes and coconut milk
Simmer until everything is tender and the stew thickens
Add greens in the last 5 minutes
Season with garlic, onion, salt
This is Timor-Leste's staple — corn, not rice, is the traditional grain
The thick, hearty consistency makes it both a soup and a main course

recipes.name: Tukir
recipes.description: Slow-braised pork with tamarind and turmeric.
instructions: Cut pork into chunks
Brown with shallots and garlic
Add turmeric, tamarind, chili, water
Braise 45 min until tender

recipes.name: Caril
recipes.description: Timorese-Portuguese fusion curry.
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, ginger, spices
Add chicken, brown
Add coconut milk and potatoes
Simmer 30 min

recipes.name: Ikan Saboko
recipes.description: Fresh fish stuffed with chili sambal, wrapped in banana leaves, and grilled over beach-side charcoal — East Timor's coastal cooking at its purest. The banana-leaf unwrap reveal and the beachside setting have made Dili's grilled fish a viral food-travel destination scene.
ingredients: 4 whole fresh fish (snapper, mackerel, or tuna)
Sambal: red chilies, garlic, shallots, lime juice, salt
instructions: Score fish on both sides
Make sambal: pound chilies, garlic, shallots, add lime juice and salt
Stuff fish cavities with sambal
Wrap in banana leaves
Grill over charcoal until leaves are charred and fish is cooked through — 10-15 min
Unwrap at the table — the banana leaf steams the fish while the charcoal smokes it
Serve with rice, extra sambal, and lime
The beach-side grilling scene in Dili is the viral image of Timorese food

recipes.name: Ai-Kaka
recipes.description: Crispy fried cassava sticks.
instructions: Peel and slice cassava
Boil until just tender
Deep fry until golden
Serve with chili sauce

recipes.name: Pastel de Nata Timorense
recipes.full_name: Pastel de Nata Timorense (Timorese Egg Tart)
recipes.description: East Timor's take on the Portuguese egg tart — with coconut milk replacing regular milk, a tropical twist on the Lisbon classic. Portugal's colonial legacy lives on in Dili's bakeries. The coconut-custard version has gained attention as a unique fusion in the global pastel de nata trend.
ingredients: Filling: egg yolks, sugar, coconut milk (Timorese twist), vanilla, cinnamon
Powdered sugar and cinnamon for dusting
instructions: Line muffin tins with puff pastry
Make custard: whisk yolks, sugar, coconut milk, vanilla
Pour into pastry shells — don't overfill
Bake at 220°C until pastry is crispy and custard has charred spots on top
Dust with cinnamon and powdered sugar
The Portuguese legacy meets tropical coconut — East Timor's colonial fusion in a pastry
The charred custard spots are the sign of a proper pastel

recipes.name: Bibinka
recipes.description: Dense, sweet coconut rice cake.
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, eggs
Pour into greased pan
Bake at 175°C for 40 min
Cut into squares

recipes.name: Bibinka
recipes.description: A coconut-milk rice cake baked on banana leaves — East Timor's version of a dessert found across Southeast Asia and the Pacific. The banana leaf lining gives it a subtle grassy aroma that elevates the simple coconut-rice base. A staple of Timorese celebrations.
instructions: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, eggs into a smooth batter
Line baking pan with banana leaves
Pour batter in
Bake at 175°C for 35-40 min until set and golden on top
The banana leaf infuses a subtle green, grassy flavor
Cut into squares and serve warm or at room temperature
A celebratory cake found across Southeast Asia but with Timorese variations

recipes.name: Tua Mutin
recipes.description: Sweet, mildly alcoholic palm sap.
instructions: Collect sap from palm tree
Serve fresh same day

recipes.name: Ai-Café
recipes.description: Strong, rich Timorese coffee — world-renowned single origin.
instructions: Boil water, add coffee grounds
Simmer 3 min
Strain into cup
Add sugar

recipes.name: Bolón de Verde
recipes.description: Ecuador's breakfast powerhouse — a giant ball of mashed green plantain stuffed with cheese and pork cracklings, fried until golden. The cheese-pull when you break it open went viral. Guayaquil wakes up on bolón de verde the way other cities wake up on toast.
instructions: Boil or roast green plantains until tender
Mash while still hot — must be smooth and sticky
Mix in crumbled cheese and chicharrón pieces
Shape into large balls — bigger than a baseball
Fry in oil until golden crust forms, or serve as-is (boiled version)
The outside should be crispy, the inside gooey with melted cheese and pork
Serve with a fried egg on top and coffee
This is Ecuador's most important breakfast — coastal Guayaquil runs on bolón

recipes.name: Tigrillo
recipes.description: Smashed green plantain scrambled with eggs and melted cheese — a hearty Ecuadorian breakfast from the gold-mining town of Zaruma. The one-pan technique and the melted-cheese-through-plantain texture make tigrillo a viral Latin American breakfast discovery.
instructions: Boil plantains until tender, mash roughly — keep some chunks
Melt butter, add mashed plantain
Scramble eggs into the plantain, stir together
Add crumbled cheese — it melts through
Season with salt, top with cilantro
Serve with hot sauce and coffee
This is Zaruma's gift to Ecuador — a gold mining town that created the perfect morning fuel

recipes.name: Encebollado
recipes.description: Ecuador's national soup and world-famous hangover cure — fresh tuna and cassava in a tomato-cumin broth buried under tangy pickled red onions. The most debated dish in Ecuador (every city claims the best version), and the dramatic onion-pile presentation makes it a viral food landmark.
ingredients: Red onion (sliced into rings, pickled in lime juice)
instructions: Boil yuca until tender but not falling apart
Cook tuna in broth with tomatoes, garlic, cumin
Do not overcook the tuna — it should be tender, not dry
Quick-pickle red onion rings in lime juice and salt
Ladle soup into bowls — yuca and tuna in broth
Top with a mountain of pickled onions
Serve with plantain chips on the side and extra lime
This is Ecuador's hangover cure and national soup — the debate between coast and highlands about the best version is eternal

recipes.name: Seco de Chivo
recipes.description: Ecuador's celebratory goat stew — braised in naranjilla juice and beer with a shocking amount of cilantro that turns the sauce bright green. The vivid color and fall-apart meat have made seco de chivo a viral Ecuadorian food landmark. Reserved for weekends and celebrations.
ingredients: Naranjilla juice (or orange-lime mix as substitute)
Rice, fried plantain, avocado for serving
instructions: Marinate goat in naranjilla juice and beer overnight
Blend a massive amount of cilantro into a green paste — this is the base color
Sauté onion, garlic, add tomatoes, green pepper, cumin, achiote
Add goat and marinade, bring to simmer
Add cilantro paste — the stew turns bright green
Slow-cook 2+ hours until goat is fall-apart tender
Serve with yellow rice, fried ripe plantain, avocado, and salad
The green color from the cilantro is striking and unusual

recipes.name: Hornado
recipes.description: Ecuador's market-day centerpiece — whole pig roasted until the skin shatters like glass, served with potato patties and hominy corn. The skin-cracking moment and the market stall carving spectacle are the most filmed food scenes in Ecuador's highlands.
ingredients: 1 whole suckling pig or large pork leg
Marinade: chicha (fermented corn drink) or beer, garlic, cumin, achiote, salt
instructions: Score the skin deeply all over
Marinate in chicha/beer with garlic, cumin, achiote, salt — overnight
Roast in wood-fired oven low and slow for 6+ hours
Baste repeatedly — the skin must become crackly and golden while meat stays moist
The skin should shatter when you tap it — crispy like glass
Carve at the market stall, serve with llapingachos, mote, curtido, and agrio
In Ecuadorian markets, whole hornado sits on display — customers point at which cut they want
The skin-cracking moment is the most viral Ecuadorian food video

recipes.name: Ceviche de Camarón Ecuatoriano
recipes.description: Ecuador's ceviche controversy — cooked shrimp in a tomato-citrus sauce (not raw like Peru's), topped with popcorn and plantain chips.
