ingredients: Grape molasses (pekmez -- for the sesame coating glaze)
instructions: Simit is the Turkish sesame bread ring -- the street food of Istanbul
Found everywhere: on carts pushed by simitci (simit sellers), at bakeries, at every corner
The dough is ring-shaped and dipped in diluted grape molasses (pekmez) before rolling in sesame seeds
The molasses gives the crust its characteristic deep golden color and slight sweetness
Baked until the sesame is toasty and the crust is crunchy
Eaten for breakfast with white cheese (beyaz peynir) and tea (cay)
The simitci with his tray on his head is the image of Istanbul street life

recipes.name: Gozleme
recipes.description: Turkish filled flatbread -- thin dough rolled on a sac (concave griddle), filled with spinach and white cheese (or ground beef), folded and cooked in butter until golden. Traditionally made by women at Turkish markets. The sac griddle and the stretching sound are the market experience.
ingredients: Yufka or thin flatbread (or homemade dough rolled thin)
Spinach and white cheese filling OR ground beef and onion
instructions: Gozleme is the Turkish stuffed flatbread -- traditionally made by women on a sac (concave griddle)
A thin dough is rolled out, filled on one half, folded, and cooked on the sac
The most popular filling: spinach and beyaz peynir (white cheese)
Or ground beef with onion and peppers
Cooked in butter until golden and crispy
Sold at Turkish markets and roadside stalls -- the sac is visible
The sound of the dough being stretched on the sac is the sound of Turkish markets

recipes.name: Turkish Breakfast Spread
recipes.description: Turkish breakfast spread -- kahvalti (under coffee) is a spread of beyaz peynir (white brine cheese), olives, tomatoes, cucumber, honey with kaymak (clotted cream), jams, pan-fried sucuk (spiced sausage), and boiled eggs. A leisurely weekend event in Turkey. Mezze-style approach to the first meal.
instructions: Turkish breakfast (kahvalti) is a spread -- not a single dish
Kahvalti literally means under (before) coffee -- the word suggests it predates the first coffee
A mezze-style approach to breakfast: many small components
The spread: white cheese, olives, tomatoes, cucumber, honey with kaymak, jams, butter, eggs, and sucuk
Sucuk: the Turkish spiced dry sausage -- pan-fried until the fat renders and it sizzles
Kaymak: Turkish clotted cream, thicker than cream -- eaten with honey
Eaten slowly on weekends: kahvalti is a leisurely event in Turkey

recipes.name: Doner Kebab
recipes.description: Turkish rotating spit-roasted lamb or beef -- meat stacked in a cone on a vertical rotating spit, outer layer sliced as it cooks. Invented in Bursa in the 19th century. Eaten in flatbread with tomato, onion, and sumac. Traveled to Germany with Turkish workers in the 1960s; the Berlin doner is now Germany's most eaten fast food.
ingredients: Lamb or beef (sliced thin, layered and compressed onto a vertical spit)
Marinade: yoghurt, olive oil, onion juice, spices (cumin, paprika, oregano, black pepper)
Tomato, onion, parsley, sumac (for the doner sandwich)
instructions: Doner kebab is Turkey's most internationally known food
Doner means rotating in Turkish -- the meat rotates on a vertical spit
The meat is layered in a cone shape, compressing as it rotates
The outer layer cooks while the inside stays raw -- sliced off continuously as needed
Invented in Bursa, Turkey in the 19th century (Iskender Efendi often credited)
Eaten in a flatbread wrap (the street version) or on a plate with rice and vegetables
The doner traveled to Germany with Turkish gastarbeiter (guest workers) in the 1960s
The German doner kebab is now Berlin's most popular fast food and a cultural institution

recipes.name: Mercimek Corbasi
recipes.description: Turkish red lentil soup -- red lentils cooked until completely smooth, finished with a sizzling drizzle of butter with paprika and dried mint. Lemon at the table. Eaten as a starter at virtually every Turkish meal. The butter drizzle sizzle is the signature finishing moment.
ingredients: Butter (for the finishing drizzle with dried mint)
instructions: Mercimek corbasi is the Turkish red lentil soup -- ubiquitous across Turkey
Simple but deeply satisfying
The lentils cook down completely until smooth
Finished with a drizzle of butter sizzled with paprika and dried mint
The butter-paprika drizzle sizzles when it hits the soup
Lemon squeezed at the table
Eaten as a starter at virtually every Turkish meal

recipes.name: Lahmacun
recipes.description: Turkish thin flatbread with minced lamb -- lahmacun (from Arabic lahm bi-ajeen: meat on dough), paper-thin dough topped with finely spiced lamb-onion-tomato paste, baked in a very hot oven. No cheese. Rolled up with parsley and sumac to eat. Also exists in Lebanon and Syria.
ingredients: Onion, tomato, peppers (all very finely chopped)
Parsley, onion, sumac (rolled inside as toppings)
instructions: Lahmacun is the Turkish thin flatbread with a spiced meat topping -- often called Turkish pizza overseas
But it predates modern pizza and is fundamentally different: very thin, no cheese
The dough is rolled paper-thin
The meat topping is finely minced with onion, tomato, herbs, and spices
Baked quickly in a very hot oven
Served with parsley, lemon, and sumac
Rolled up with the herbs inside to eat -- a wrap
Lahm bi-ajeen in Arabic (meat on dough) -- it also exists in Lebanon and Syria

imageCredit.author: No machine-readable author provided. Rainer Zenz assumed (based on copyright claims).

recipes.name: Iskender Kebab
recipes.description: Bursa-origin doner on soggy bread -- doner slices on torn pide bread, hot tomato sauce poured over, then sizzling brown butter poured over at the table. Cold yoghurt on the side. Named after Iskender Efendi (credited with inventing doner). A sit-down restaurant dish, not street food.
ingredients: Pide bread (torn into pieces -- the base)
Brown butter (poured hot over at serving)
instructions: Iskender kebab is a specific dish from Bursa -- named after Iskender Efendi, who is credited with inventing doner
Slices of doner meat placed on torn pide bread
Hot tomato sauce poured over
Then hot brown butter poured over -- it sizzles when it hits the tomato sauce and meat
Cold yoghurt on the side as contrast
The combination of hot butter, hot tomato sauce, meat, soggy bread, and cold yoghurt
Iskender kebab is not a street food -- it is a sit-down restaurant dish

recipes.name: Kofte
recipes.description: Turkish spiced meatballs -- ground lamb and beef with grated onion, parsley, cumin, and paprika, shaped and grilled, fried, or baked. Dozens of regional variations: Inegol (pressed, no breadcrumbs), Izmir (baked with potato and tomato), Adana (skewered, spicy). Kofte variations map Turkey's regional identity.
instructions: Kofte are the Turkish spiced meatballs or patties -- eaten across all of Turkey
Many regional variations: Inegol kofte (no breadcrumbs, distinct shape), Izmir kofte (baked with tomato and potato), Adana kofte (on a skewer, spicy)
The basic recipe: ground meat (lamb and beef) with onion, herbs, and spices
Shaped and grilled, pan-fried, or baked
Eaten with bread, rice, or salad
Turkish kofte variations are a map of regional identity

recipes.name: Kuru Fasulye
recipes.description: Turkish white bean stew -- white beans slow-cooked in a tomato-onion base until very soft. Kuru fasulye (dry beans) is the Turkish national comfort food: the dish of the lokanta (canteen restaurant) and military service. Eaten over rice pilav. Simple, profound, deeply beloved.
ingredients: Lamb or beef (optional -- often just the beans)
instructions: Kuru fasulye is the Turkish national comfort food -- simple and profound
White beans cooked in a tomato-onion base until very soft
Often with lamb or beef but the vegetarian version is equally revered
Eaten over pilav (rice) or with bread
The dish of the traditional Turkish lokanta (canteen-style restaurant)
Associated with military service -- every Turkish man who did military service ate kuru fasulye
Voted among the most beloved Turkish dishes in national polls

recipes.name: Manti
recipes.description: Turkish tiny dumplings -- small pasta parcels filled with spiced lamb, boiled and served on a bed of garlic yoghurt with brown butter sizzled with dried mint and paprika. The traditional benchmark: 40 manti on one spoon (grandmother skill test). Central Asian origin: related to Mongolian and Chinese dumplings.
ingredients: Thin pasta dough (very thin -- the traditional manti are very small)
Ground lamb or beef, onion, parsley
Brown butter with dried mint and paprika
instructions: Manti are the Turkish dumplings -- the filling is tiny, the labor is immense
Traditional manti: very small, each the size of a small coin
The skill: 40 manti fitting on a single spoon is the Turkish grandmother benchmark
Filled with spiced ground meat
Boiled and served with a generous pool of garlic yoghurt
Drizzled with brown butter sizzled with dried mint and paprika
The combination: hot dumplings + cold garlic yoghurt + hot butter drizzle
Central Asian origin: related to Mongolian buuz, Chinese baozi, Korean mandu

recipes.name: Imam Bayildi
recipes.full_name: Imam Bayildi (Stuffed Eggplant in Olive Oil)
recipes.description: Turkish stuffed eggplant in olive oil -- eggplant fried, then stuffed with onion, tomato, and garlic, slow-cooked in generous olive oil until silky. Imam bayildi: the imam fainted (from pleasure, or from the olive oil). A zeytinyagli dish (olive oil vegetable): eaten at room temperature, the olive oil the flavor medium.
instructions: Imam bayildi means the imam fainted -- the name is the story
The story: the imam fainted from pleasure (or from the amount of olive oil used)
Eggplants are fried in olive oil, then stuffed with onion-tomato-garlic mixture
Slow-cooked until very soft and the olive oil is absorbed
Eaten at room temperature -- an olive oil vegetable dish (zeytinyagli)
Zeytinyagli dishes: Turkish vegetable dishes cooked in generous olive oil, eaten cold or room temperature
The olive oil is the flavor medium -- it absorbs all the aromatics

recipes.name: Adana Kebab
recipes.description: Turkish Adana spicy lamb kebab -- ground fatty lamb pressed onto wide flat metal skewers, chargrilled. Adana (southern Turkey, the spicier region): much spicier than Urfa kebab (the milder Sanliurfa version). The Adana-Urfa comparison is a regional identity matter. Served with flatbread and sumac-onion salad.
ingredients: Ground lamb (fatty -- from the tail fat)
Red chilli (Turkish biber -- fresh and dried, quite spicy)
Wide flat skewers (the kebab is hand-pressed onto the skewer)
instructions: Adana kebab is from the city of Adana in southern Turkey -- the spiciest region
Ground fatty lamb pressed onto wide flat metal skewers
Cooked over charcoal -- the fat drips and the flame chars the meat
Much spicier than Urfa kebab (the milder version from Sanliurfa)
The Adana-Urfa debate is a regional identity matter
Served with flatbread, grilled peppers, and sumac-onion salad

recipes.name: Pilav
recipes.description: Turkish butter-fried rice -- baldo rice sauteed in generous butter before stock is added, each grain separate and buttery. Sehriyeli pilav: with orzo toasted until golden-red before the rice goes in, the toasted pasta adding crunch and nuttiness. The foundation of Turkish cooking; every meal has pilav.
ingredients: Baldo or baldo-type rice (or orzo pasta for arpa sehriyeli pilav)
Chicken or vegetable stock (for cooking the rice in)
instructions: Turkish pilav is the foundation of Turkish cooking -- every meal has pilav
Made with butter, not oil -- this is the Turkish distinction
The rice is sauteed in butter first (the fried rice method)
Then hot stock added -- absorbed completely
The result: each grain separate, buttery, fragrant
Sehriyeli pilav: with orzo (small pasta) toasted in butter first -- the orzo turns golden-red, then the rice added
The toasted orzo gives crunch and a nutty contrast to the soft rice

recipes.name: Borek
recipes.description: Turkish filled pastry -- yufka (Turkish thin pastry) filled with spinach and white cheese, ground beef, or potato, shaped into rolls (sigara boregi), coils, or trays. The Ottoman pastry heritage that spread across the Balkans and Middle East. Su boregi: the yufka briefly boiled before layering.
ingredients: Spinach and white cheese filling OR ground beef OR potato
Egg and oil or milk (for brushing)
instructions: Borek is the Turkish filled pastry -- the Ottoman pastry heritage
Yufka: the Turkish thin pastry, different from Greek phyllo (thicker, more doughy)
Many shapes: roll (sigara boregi -- cigarette), coil (su boregi), tray (tepsi boregi)
The most common fillings: spinach-white cheese, ground beef-onion, or potato
The Ottoman pastry tradition spread across the Balkans, Middle East, and North Africa
Su boregi (water borek): the yufka is briefly boiled before layering -- softer than regular borek

recipes.name: Ayran
recipes.description: Turkish salted yoghurt drink -- yoghurt diluted with cold water and salted. Drunk with every Turkish meal. The frothy top from whisking is the quality signal. Savory, not sweet. Drunk with kebabs, kofte, and bread. Turkey's most consumed drink after water.
instructions: Ayran is the Turkish yoghurt drink -- drunk at every meal and available everywhere
Yoghurt diluted with cold water and salted
The salt is essential -- this is a savory drink, not sweet
Drunk with kebabs, kofte, bread, and all Turkish meals
Available in every supermarket, fast food restaurant, and kebab shop
The frothy top from whisking: the quality signal
Turkey exports ayran globally -- Ayran is the most consumed drink in Turkey after water

recipes.name: Midye Dolma
recipes.description: Istanbul street food stuffed mussels -- large mussels filled with spiced rice (pine nuts, currants, allspice, cinnamon), steamed. Sold by waterfront vendors at Besiktas and Eminonu. The vendor opens the shell, you squeeze lemon, eat from the shell, buy by the piece. The taste of Istanbul street eating.
ingredients: Spiced rice filling: short-grain rice, onion, pine nuts, currants, allspice, cinnamon, mint
instructions: Midye dolma are the Istanbul street food stuffed mussels
Large mussels stuffed with spiced rice (with pine nuts, currants, and warm spices)
The rice filling is the same style as Turkish dolma (stuffed vegetables)
Sold by midyeci vendors on the Istanbul waterfront -- especially Besiktas and Eminonu
Eaten in hand: the vendor opens the shell, you squeeze lemon, you eat from the shell
Bought by the tray -- you pay per mussel

recipes.name: Simil and Beyaz Peynir
recipes.full_name: Simil and Beyaz Peynir (Simit with White Cheese)
recipes.description: Turkish classic breakfast combination -- simit (sesame bread ring), beyaz peynir (white brine cheese: milder and creamier than Greek feta), and cay (black tea in a small glass). Eaten by millions every morning. The fundamental Turkish working breakfast: crunchy-salty-sweet-hot.
ingredients: Beyaz peynir (Turkish white brine cheese -- similar to feta but milder)
instructions: Simit with beyaz peynir and cay is the Turkish working-class breakfast
The combination is so fundamental it is almost a cultural institution
Simit: crunchy, sesame-fragrant, slightly sweet from the pekmez glaze
Beyaz peynir: creamy, mild, briny -- a creamy white cheese in brine
Turkish cay (tea): small glass, strongly brewed black tea
This combination is eaten by millions every morning at the waterside, in parks, on commutes

recipes.name: Baklava
recipes.description: Turkish pistachio baklava -- dozens of paper-thin filo layers brushed with clarified butter, filled with Gaziantep pistachios (the bright green Turkish variety with GI protection), baked golden, cool syrup poured over hot. Gaziantep baklava has a protected designation. The pinnacle of Ottoman pastry craft.
ingredients: Clarified butter (generously -- brushed on every layer)
Pistachios (Antep/Gaziantep pistachios -- the green Turkish pistachio)
Sugar syrup (cool, poured over hot baklava)
instructions: Turkish baklava is the pinnacle of Ottoman pastry art
The Gaziantep (Antep) pistachio: the bright green Turkish pistachio -- the best for baklava
Gaziantep has a protected geographical indication for its baklava
The technique: dozens of layers of paper-thin filo, each brushed with clarified butter
Cut before baking into diamond or square pieces
Baked golden, then cool syrup poured over hot baklava (or hot over cold -- the opposite creates a different texture)
The cool-over-hot rule: the temperature difference drives syrup absorption
Karakoy Gulluoglu and Hafiz Mustafa in Istanbul: the famous baklava houses

recipes.name: Lokum
recipes.description: Turkish confectionery -- lokum (Turkish delight) created in Istanbul around 1777, attributed to Haci Bekir (whose shop still exists). Sugar and cornstarch cooked and stirred for hours into a gel, flavored with rosewater, mastic, or pistachio, cut and coated in icing sugar. European travelers spread it globally as an Ottoman luxury.
instructions: Lokum (Turkish delight) was created in Istanbul in the late 18th century
Often attributed to Haci Bekir, a confectioner who came to Istanbul from Kastamonu around 1777
Haci Bekir's shop still exists in Istanbul (Eminonu)
Sugar and water cooked to a specific temperature, cornstarch added, stirred for hours
The long stirring creates the gel texture
Flavored with rosewater (the classic), mastic (resin from Chios mastic tree), or pistachio
European travellers in the Ottoman Empire discovered it and brought it back -- it became an exotic luxury in Victorian England

recipes.name: Sutlac
recipes.description: Turkish rice pudding -- sutlac, a thin creamy pudding served cold in earthenware pots. Firin sutlac: the oven version, the top browned under a hot grill into a caramelized crust. The burned top and cold creamy interior contrast is the signature experience.
instructions: Sutlac is the Turkish rice pudding -- served cold in earthenware pots
A very thin, creamy pudding -- more liquid than Western rice pudding
The firin sutlac (oven rice pudding) version: the top is browned under a very hot oven or grill
The burned top is the signature: browned, slightly caramelized
Eaten cold with the contrast of the warm (or cooled) burned top and cold creamy pudding

recipes.name: Cay
recipes.description: Turkish Black Sea tea -- cay brewed in a double pot (caydanlik: concentrated tea on top, hot water below for dilution), served in small tulip-shaped glasses. Turkey has the world's highest per-capita tea consumption. Rize province grows the tea. Ataturk promoted tea post-WWI to replace imported coffee.
ingredients: Turkish black tea (Rize tea -- grown on the Black Sea coast)
instructions: Cay (pronounced chai) is the Turkish national drink -- consumed more per person than almost any other nation
Turkey has the highest per-capita tea consumption in the world
Grown on the Black Sea coast (Rize province) -- a relatively recent crop (1930s)
Before Rize tea, Turks drank coffee; Ataturk promoted tea after WWI to reduce dependency on imported coffee
Made in a double pot (caydanlik): water in the bottom, concentrated tea in the top
The tea is poured from the top pot (strong) and diluted with hot water from the bottom
Each person chooses their strength: koyu (dark) or acik (light)
Served in small tulip-shaped glasses with two sugar cubes

recipes.name: Raki
recipes.description: Turkish anise spirit -- raki (Lion's Milk: aslan sutu), grape-based spirit double-distilled with anise. Clear until water is added: the louche turns it milky white (anise oils suspending in dilution). Drunk slowly at a meze table over hours. Yeni Raki is the most known brand.
ingredients: Cold water (to dilute -- essential: turns white)
Ice (optional -- purists say ice first, then water)
instructions: Raki is the Turkish national spirit -- the Lion's Milk (aslan sutu)
Distilled from grapes and anise -- clear until water is added
The louche: the water turns the clear spirit milky white -- from the anise oils
This is why it is called the Lion's Milk -- the white cloudy appearance
Drunk very slowly at the raki table -- a meal in itself
The meze table: raki is drunk alongside many small dishes over hours
Yeni Raki is the most famous brand -- also Tekirdağ
The culture: drinking raki is an event, not just a drink

imageCredit.author: The original uploader was Blue at Bulgarian Wikipedia.

recipes.name: Salep
recipes.description: Turkish Ottoman winter orchid drink -- salep powder (ground wild orchid tuber, Orchis genus) mixed with hot milk and sugar into a thick, warming, slightly viscous drink. Cinnamon on top. Over-harvesting has made real salep rare and expensive; most commercial salep uses cornstarch. Traditionally sold by winter street vendors in Istanbul.
ingredients: Salep powder (ground dried orchid tuber -- Orchis mascula and related species)
instructions: Salep is the Ottoman winter drink -- made from ground orchid tuber
The orchid tuber (from wild orchids of the Orchis genus) ground to a powder
Mixed with hot milk and sugar -- it thickens into a warming, slightly slimy drink
The characteristic texture: thicker than milk, slightly gel-like from the orchid starch
Traditionally sold by salep vendors in winter in Istanbul
The over-harvesting of wild orchids has made real salep rare and expensive
Much commercial salep now uses cornstarch substitutes
Cinnamon dusted on top is essential

recipes.name: Menemen
recipes.full_name: Menemen (Scrambled Eggs with Peppers and Tomatoes)
recipes.description: A Turkish breakfast specialty from the town of Menemen, combining soft vegetables with scrambled eggs for a simple yet satisfying meal traditionally served family-style
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat
Dice onions and peppers, add to oil and sauté for 5 minutes until softened
Add diced tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes
Gently crack eggs into pan and slowly scramble with the vegetable mixture
Cook for 4-5 minutes until eggs are just set
Add cheese if desired, season with salt and pepper
Serve hot in the same skillet with crusty bread
tips: Menemen should be cooked slowly to keep eggs creamy. The dish is traditionally served in the skillet for family-style sharing
recipes.fun_fact: Menemen originated in the town of Menemen in Northern Izmir where it is believed to have been invented and remains a beloved traditional Turkish breakfast
alternatives: Use red peppers instead of green
Include kaşar cheese instead of feta
Add fresh herbs like parsley or dill

recipes.name: Simit
recipes.description: A beloved Turkish street food - a golden sesame-crusted bread with a tender, fluffy interior, sitting between a bagel and soft pretzel
instructions: Mix flour, yeast, salt, and sugar in a bowl
Add warm water and oil, knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic
Cover and let rise for 1-1.5 hours until doubled
Divide dough into 8 portions and shape into balls
Roll each into a thin rope about 12 inches long
Bring ends together to form ring and seal
Mix grape molasses with water for syrup
Pour sesame seeds into shallow bowl
Dip each simit ring into syrup, then roll in sesame seeds
Place on oiled baking sheet and let rise 15-20 minutes
Bake at 400°F for 15-18 minutes, turning every 3-4 minutes
Cool on wire rack and serve with cheese, olives, and Turkish tea
tips: Rotating simits while baking ensures even browning. Grape molasses creates authentic flavor
recipes.fun_fact: Turkish simit may have been invented around 1500s during Ottoman Empire. Today it remains a beloved street food, often eaten for breakfast with fresh vegetables and cheese
alternatives: Dip in zaatar instead of sesame

recipes.name: Döner Kebab
recipes.description: Turkish rotisserie meat sandwich with thin-sliced cooked meat, vegetables and yogurt sauce in pita. Modern döner developed in Istanbul in 19th century
instructions: Mix ground meat with fat, onion, garlic and spices
In vertical rotisserie (or bake at 400°F for 45 min), cook meat until outer layer browns and crisps
Slice thinly from outside
Serve in pita with vegetables and yogurt sauce
Squeeze lemon over filling
tips: If no vertical rotisserie, shape mixture into loaf on baking sheet and bake until golden, slicing as it cooks
recipes.fun_fact: Modern döner kebab developed in Istanbul in 19th century, revolutionized by vertical rotisserie cooking. One of most popular lunch sandwiches worldwide

recipes.name: Karniyarik
recipes.description: Turkish dinner specialty - halved eggplants stuffed with spiced ground meat
instructions: Peel eggplants in stripes and soak in salted water 20 minutes
Pat dry and fry in olive oil until lightly browned on all sides
Cut lengthwise slit down center of each eggplant, careful not to cut through
Brown meat with onion, add garlic, fry 1 minute
Add peppers, tomatoes, tomato paste, spices; cook 10 minutes
Stuff eggplant slit with meat mixture
Arrange in baking dish and bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes
tips: The striped peeling technique helps eggplant cook more evenly
recipes.fun_fact: Name means 'split belly' in Turkish, referring to the slit where meat is stuffed

recipes.name: Lamb Pide
recipes.description: Turkish savory meat-filled pastry - street food and dinner staple
ingredients: For dough: 500g flour, 250ml warm water, 7g salt, 7g instant yeast, 2 tablespoons oil

For filling: 400g ground lamb, 1 onion finely diced, 3 cloves garlic minced, 1 red bell pepper diced, 2 tomatoes diced, 2 tablespoons tomato paste, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon allspice, 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, salt and pepper
Egg wash: 1 egg beaten with 1 tablespoon water
instructions: Make dough: mix flour and salt in large bowl
Dissolve yeast in warm water, let sit 5 minutes
Add yeast mixture and oil to flour
Knead 10 minutes until smooth and elastic
Cover and let rise 1 hour until doubled
Meanwhile, make filling: brown ground lamb with onion and garlic
Add bell pepper, tomatoes, tomato paste, spices
Cook 10 minutes until reduced, season with salt and pepper
Let cool
Divide dough into 6 portions
Roll each portion into oval shape
Place 2-3 tablespoons filling in center of each oval
Fold long sides up and pinch together at top (traditional pide shape)
Place on oiled baking sheets
Cover and let rise 20 minutes
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 425°F (220°C) for 25-30 minutes until golden brown
Serve hot
tips: Pide are best eaten fresh and hot. Filling must cool before filling dough
recipes.fun_fact: Pide are called 'Turkish pizza' and are eaten throughout Turkey at street stalls and restaurants
alternatives: Make vegetarian with spinach and feta

recipes.name: Çörek
recipes.description: Round bread baked in a clay oven.
instructions: Make dough, rise 1 hour
Shape into flat rounds
Bake in tandoor or oven at 230°C

recipes.name: Gatyk
recipes.description: Rich homemade yogurt.
instructions: Serve thick yogurt with sugar or honey

recipes.name: Chorek
recipes.description: Turkmen round tandoor flatbread -- chorek, leavened dough baked by sticking to the hot inner clay wall of the tamdyr (tandoor). Slightly charred, smoky. Bread is sacred in Turkmen culture; wasting it is disrespectful. Breaking chorek together is the hospitality ritual.
instructions: Chorek is the Turkmen round flatbread -- baked in a tandoor (tamdyr)
Similar to Uzbek non and Tajik non but with Turkmen character
Baked by sticking to the hot inner wall of the clay oven
The outside: slightly charred, smoky from the tandoor
A sacred food: bread should not be wasted in Turkmen culture
Breaking bread together is a hospitality ritual

recipes.name: Salam
recipes.description: Turkmen simple bread in warm milk -- day-old chorek torn into warm milk. Eaten salted or sweetened. A frugal staple from necessity that became a nostalgic comfort food. The Turkmen imperative to never waste bread: even old bread is eaten.
instructions: Salam is the simple Turkmen breakfast of bread torn into warm milk
Day-old bread softened in warm milk
Eaten savory (salted) or sweet (sugared)
A poverty-era staple that has become a nostalgic comfort food
Simple, warming, and deeply Turkmen in its frugality -- bread must be used

recipes.name: Turkmen Plov
recipes.description: Central Asian lamb pilaf — Turkmen style.
instructions: Fry onion and lamb
Add carrots and cumin
Add rice and water
Cook covered, add garlic head on top

recipes.name: Çorba
recipes.description: Clear lamb soup with vegetables.
instructions: Simmer lamb 30 min
Add vegetables
Cook 15 more min

recipes.name: Shurpa
recipes.description: Turkmen lamb and vegetable soup -- bone-in lamb simmered for a long time (marrow enriching the broth) with whole potatoes, carrots, and turnips. The most common Turkmen lunch. Eaten with fresh bread at home and at chai khane (teahouses).
instructions: Shurpa is the Central Asian lamb and vegetable soup -- the most common lunch in Turkmenistan
A simple, hearty broth with whole vegetables and bone-in lamb
The lamb is cooked for a long time -- the marrow enriches the broth
The vegetables are added whole or in large pieces -- they cook in the lamb broth
Served with fresh bread
Eaten at home and at teahouses (chai khane)

recipes.name: Gutap
recipes.description: Turkmen stuffed flatbread -- gutap, unleavened dough folded around a pumpkin-onion filling (or fresh greens), cooked on a griddle. The pumpkin filling sweetens as it cooks. A snack, bread substitute, or light main.
ingredients: Filling: pumpkin and onion OR greens and spring onion
instructions: Gutap are the Turkmen stuffed flatbreads -- similar to Tajik sambusa but pan-cooked
A thin unleavened dough
Stuffed with pumpkin and onion (the most popular) or fresh greens
Folded into a half-moon shape and cooked on a griddle
Eaten as a snack, bread substitute, or main
The pumpkin filling sweetens slightly as it cooks

recipes.name: Dovga
recipes.description: Turkmen yoghurt soup -- dovga, yoghurt stabilized with egg and heated with rice and generous fresh herbs (dill, coriander, spring onion). The soup stays tangy and silky from the egg stabilization. Served warm or cold. Related to Azerbaijani and Persian yoghurt soups.
ingredients: Rice (cooked or added raw to cook in the soup)
Fresh herbs: dill, coriander, spring onion
instructions: Dovga is the Turkmen yoghurt soup -- similar to Azerbaijani and Persian yoghurt soups
Yoghurt stabilized with egg (so it does not curdle when heated)
Rice and herbs cooked in the yoghurt
The result: a thick, tangy, herby soup
Served warm or cold
The herb quantity: very generous -- it should be green
A cooling summer soup

recipes.name: Manti
recipes.description: Large steamed lamb dumplings.

recipes.name: Pulaka

recipes.description: British boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat -- Scotch egg, breaded and fried (or baked). Claimed by Fortnum & Mason (1738). Not actually Scottish. The yolk debate (runny vs hard) divides the nation. Pub snack, picnic food, petrol station staple.
instructions: The Scotch egg is a boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat, breaded, and fried
Invented in London by Fortnum & Mason in 1738 (they claim)
Despite the name, it is not Scottish
Eaten cold at picnics or hot from the fryer
The yolk debate: slightly runny yolk or fully hard-boiled -- divides the nation
A pub snack, picnic food, and petrol station staple

recipes.name: Sunday Roast
recipes.description: The British Sunday roast — beef, Yorkshires, roast potatoes, and gravy.
instructions: Roast beef 2 hours
Roast potatoes in dripping
Make Yorkshire pudding batter, bake in hot fat
Make gravy from drippings
Serve together with horseradish

recipes.name: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.description: Lamb mince under golden mashed potato — the comfort classic.
instructions: Brown lamb with onion, carrots, peas
Add tomato paste, Worcestershire, broth
Pour into dish, top with mashed potato
Sprinkle cheese
Bake at 200°C until golden

recipes.name: Sunday Roast
recipes.description: British weekly ritual -- the Sunday Roast, a roasted meat joint with crispy roast potatoes, Yorkshire pudding (not a dessert -- risen batter baked in hot fat), gravy from pan drippings, and vegetables. Each meat has its condiment: beef/horseradish, lamb/mint, pork/apple. The anchor of British family life.
ingredients: Roasting joint: beef (with Yorkshire pudding), lamb (with mint sauce), chicken, or pork (with apple sauce)
Roast potatoes (par-boiled then roasted in goose fat or oil until crispy)
Yorkshire pudding (batter: eggs, flour, milk -- baked in hot fat)
Vegetables: carrots, peas, green beans, cabbage
instructions: The Sunday Roast is the British weekly ritual -- the anchor of family life
A roasted joint of meat with all the trimmings
Yorkshire pudding: a crispy, risen batter pudding baked in hot fat -- NOT a dessert despite the name
Roast potatoes: the make-or-break element -- must be crispy outside, fluffy inside
Gravy: made from the meat pan drippings -- instant gravy is sacrilege
Each meat has its condiment: beef with horseradish, lamb with mint sauce, pork with apple sauce
Eaten after the pub on Sunday -- a tradition dating back centuries
The Sunday Roast is so important it was nominated as a UNESCO cultural heritage candidate

recipes.name: Shepherd's Pie
recipes.description: British baked meat pie -- Shepherd's pie (MUST be lamb; beef = cottage pie, and mixing them up is a faux pas). Seasoned lamb mince with vegetables topped with mashed potato and baked golden. Worcestershire sauce for depth. Warming comfort food.
ingredients: Lamb mince (shepherd's pie uses lamb; cottage pie uses beef)
Mashed potato topping (butter and milk, piped or forked on top)
instructions: Shepherd's pie is the British baked meat-and-potato pie -- a distinction matters:
Shepherd's pie = lamb (shepherds tend sheep)
Cottage pie = beef
Mixing them up is a British faux pas
Seasoned lamb mince with vegetables, topped with creamy mashed potato, baked until golden
Worcestershire sauce: the essential British flavoring -- fermented anchovy and vinegar
A comfort food -- warming, filling, and cheap to make

recipes.name: Fish and Chips
recipes.description: Iconic British takeaway -- fish and chips, beer-battered cod or haddock with thick-cut chips, mushy peas, and malt vinegar. Traditionally newspaper-wrapped. Chippies in every town. Friday night fish and chips -- linked to Catholic fish Friday tradition.
ingredients: White fish: cod or haddock fillet
Beer batter: flour, beer, baking powder, salt
instructions: Fish and chips is the iconic British takeaway -- the national dish argument always includes it
The batter: beer batter gives a light, crispy coating
The chips: thick-cut, not thin fries -- soft inside, crispy edges
Mushy peas: a love-or-hate side -- marrowfat peas boiled into a bright green mush
Traditionally wrapped in newspaper (now illegal for food hygiene)
Malt vinegar and salt: the only proper seasoning
Chip shops (chippies) are found in every British town
Friday night fish and chips -- a British tradition linked to Catholic fish Fridays

recipes.name: Scotch Egg
recipes.description: Hard-boiled egg wrapped in sausage meat, crumbed and fried.
instructions: Wrap eggs in sausage meat
Coat in flour, egg, breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden
Serve with mustard

recipes.name: Sausage Roll
recipes.description: British puff pastry classic -- sausage roll, seasoned pork in flaky puff pastry. Greggs sells more than any other item. Football match, picnic, and Christmas party staple. The vegan version (Greggs, 2019) became a cultural moment.
ingredients: Pork sausage meat (seasoned with sage, pepper, nutmeg)
instructions: The sausage roll is the British pastry staple -- pork in puff pastry
Sausage meat wrapped in puff pastry and baked until golden and flaky
Greggs (the bakery chain) sells more sausage rolls than any other item
A football match, picnic, and Christmas party staple
The vegan sausage roll (Greggs launched it in 2019) became a cultural moment

recipes.name: Cheese and Pickle Sandwich
recipes.description: The most British sandwich -- cheese and pickle, strong cheddar with Branston pickle on buttered bread. Found in every supermarket meal deal. The meal deal (sandwich + drink + snack for a set price) is a British institution.
instructions: The cheese and pickle sandwich is the most British sandwich that exists
Cheddar cheese and Branston pickle between two slices of buttered bread
Found in every supermarket meal deal across Britain
The "meal deal" (sandwich + drink + snack for a set price) is a British institution
Simple, satisfying, and deeply nostalgic

recipes.name: Crumpet
recipes.description: British teatime spongy bread -- crumpets, yeasted batter cooked in rings on a griddle. The holes on top absorb melted butter (they are a butter delivery mechanism). Toasted crispy outside, spongy inside. Eaten with butter, Marmite, honey, or jam.
instructions: Crumpets are the British teatime bread -- spongy, holey, and toasted
A yeasted batter cooked on a griddle in metal rings
The bubbles rise through the batter creating the characteristic holes on top
Toasted until crispy on the outside, spongy inside
The holes: designed to absorb melted butter -- a delivery mechanism for butter
Eaten with butter alone, or with Marmite, honey, or jam

recipes.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
recipes.description: Dense date sponge drenched in toffee sauce.
ingredients: Toffee sauce: butter, cream, brown sugar
instructions: Soak dates in hot water
Make sponge batter with dates
Bake at 175°C 35 min
Make toffee sauce
Pour sauce over warm pudding
Serve with ice cream

recipes.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
recipes.description: British pub dessert classic -- sticky toffee pudding, moist date sponge cake drenched in toffee sauce (butter, cream, brown sugar). Invented at Sharrow Bay Hotel, Lake District (1960s). Appears on almost every pub menu in Britain. Served with custard or ice cream.
ingredients: Toffee sauce: butter, double cream, dark brown sugar
instructions: Sticky toffee pudding is the British dessert -- a moist date sponge drenched in toffee sauce
The dates are soaked in hot water with baking soda -- they dissolve into the batter
The result is a deeply moist, dark, and dense sponge cake
The toffee sauce: butter, cream, and dark brown sugar -- poured over generously
Served with custard, cream, or vanilla ice cream
Invented at the Sharrow Bay Hotel in the Lake District (1960s)
The pub dessert menu staple -- it appears on almost every pub menu in Britain

recipes.name: Victoria Sponge
recipes.description: Classic British layer cake -- Victoria sponge, named after Queen Victoria. Two light sponge rounds sandwiched with jam and cream, dusted with icing sugar. The benchmark of home baking, judged at every village fete. The Great British Bake Off made it a national obsession.
ingredients: Butter, caster sugar (equal weight to eggs)
instructions: The Victoria sponge is the classic British layer cake -- named after Queen Victoria
Two rounds of light sponge cake sandwiched with jam and cream
The all-in-one sponge method: butter and sugar creamed, eggs added, flour folded in
The top is simply dusted with icing sugar -- no frosting, no fuss
Queen Victoria reportedly took a slice with her afternoon tea
The benchmark of home baking -- judged at every village fete baking competition
The Great British Bake Off has made it a national obsession

recipes.name: Proper Cup of Tea
recipes.description: Strong tea with milk — the UK runs on this.
instructions: Boil water, warm teapot
Add tea, pour boiling water
Steep 4 min
Add milk
Debate whether milk goes first

recipes.name: Pimm's Cup
recipes.description: The quintessential British summer drink.
instructions: Fill glass with ice
Add Pimm's and lemonade
Garnish with fruit, cucumber, and mint

recipes.name: Pimm's Cup
recipes.description: Quintessential British summer drink -- Pimm's Cup, gin-based herbal liqueur mixed with sparkling lemonade, cucumber, strawberries, mint, and orange. The drink of Wimbledon, Henley Regatta, and every garden party. Cucumber is essential. Pimm's means summer has arrived.
instructions: Pimm's is the quintessential British summer drink
Pimm's No. 1: a gin-based liqueur with herbs and spices -- the recipe is secret
Mixed with sparkling lemonade and served in a tall jug with fruit and cucumber
The drink of Wimbledon, Henley Regatta, and every garden party
British lemonade is carbonated (not still like American lemonade)
The cucumber is essential -- it provides the refreshing crispness
Drinking Pimm's means summer has arrived

recipes.name: Khubz

Roll thin

Until golden and puffed

recipes.name: Mandi

Create spice bed with onions and spices
Layer rice

Cover tightly
Slow cook at 300°F for 60+ minutes
Fluff rice
Serve with meat

recipes.name: Zarbiyan

instructions: Brown meat with onion and garlic

Rice should be tender
Fluff and serve
recipes.fun_fact: Zarbiyan is everyday UAE meal

recipes.name: Luqaimat

instructions: Mix flour and baking powder
Add water and egg
Form into balls
Heat oil to 350°F
Fry until golden
Drain on paper towels
Coat with honey
Sprinkle saffron threads

recipes.name: Umm Ali

instructions: Toast bread cubes in oven

Layer bread, coconut, nuts, raisins in baking dish

recipes.name: Qahwa

Crush cardamom

recipes.name: Traditional Tea
recipes.description: UAE tea culture focuses on non-alcoholic beverages
instructions: Heat water
Add black tea and spices

Serve hot or cold
recipes.fun_fact: UAE tea culture is central to social gatherings

recipes.name: Mate
recipes.description: Uruguayan national identity drink -- yerba mate (Ilex paraguariensis) steeped in a gourd with a bombilla (filtered metal straw). Hot water, never boiling (burns the yerba). Carried everywhere with a thermos. Uruguay has the world's highest per-capita consumption. Shared in a circle: the cebador prepares, each person drinks and returns.
ingredients: Yerba mate (dried leaves and stems of Ilex paraguariensis)
Bombilla (metal straw with a filter at the bottom)
instructions: Mate is not just a drink in Uruguay -- it is the national identity
Uruguay has the highest per-capita mate consumption in the world -- higher than Argentina or Paraguay
Carried everywhere: Uruguayans walk with a thermos under one arm and a mate gourd in hand
The water must be hot but NOT boiling -- boiling water burns the yerba and makes it bitter
Drunk continuously throughout the day -- it is a constant companion, not a single serving
In social settings, one person (the cebador) prepares and passes the mate around the circle
Each person drinks the full gourd through the bombilla and returns it for refilling
Sharing mate is an act of friendship and trust

recipes.name: Bizcocho
recipes.description: Uruguayan flaky pastries -- bizcochos, puff-pastry-like, made with butter or beef fat (grasa). Savory (salty) or sweet (sugared). Bought at the panaderia every morning. Eaten with mate: the Uruguayan morning ritual.
instructions: Bizcochos are the Uruguayan pastry eaten with mate
A flaky, buttery pastry -- like a cross between a croissant and puff pastry
The savory version: flaky, salty, made with beef fat (grasa)
The sweet version: dusted with sugar
Bought at the panaderia (bakery) every morning
Bizcochos with mate: the Uruguayan morning ritual

recipes.name: Tortas Fritas
recipes.full_name: Tortas Fritas (Fried Bread on Rainy Days)
recipes.description: Uruguayan rainy-day fried bread -- tortas fritas, simple dough discs fried until puffed and golden, dusted with sugar. The tradition: tortas fritas are made ONLY on rainy days. The association is deeply ingrained in Uruguayan culture. Eaten with mate.
instructions: Tortas fritas are the Uruguayan fried bread -- but only made on rainy days
The tradition: when it rains, you make tortas fritas -- the association is deeply ingrained
Simple fried dough -- flattened discs fried until puffed and golden
Dusted with sugar
Eaten with mate
The rainy day tradition is taken seriously -- asking for tortas fritas on a sunny day is odd

recipes.name: Medialunas
recipes.description: Uruguayan half-moon croissants -- medialunas, smaller than French, two types: de manteca (buttery) and de grasa (beef fat, savory). Glazed with simple syrup after baking. The Rioplatense cafe culture centers on medialunas and cafe con leche.
ingredients: Flour, yeast, butter, eggs, sugar, milk
instructions: Medialunas are Uruguayan croissants -- half moons
Two types: de manteca (buttery, croissant-like) and de grasa (made with beef fat, savory)
Smaller than French croissants
Glazed with simple syrup after baking -- shiny and slightly sticky
Eaten at cafes with coffee or mate
The Rioplatense cafe culture (shared with Buenos Aires) centers on medialunas and cafe con leche

recipes.name: Asado
recipes.description: Uruguayan grilled beef ritual -- asado, an afternoon-long social event. Beef seasoned only with coarse salt, grilled over wood on a parrilla. Chorizos and morcilla first, then beef cuts (tira de asado, vacio, entrana). Chimichurri on the side. Uruguay has more cattle per capita than almost any country. The Sunday family gathering.
ingredients: Beef: tira de asado (cross-cut short ribs), vacio (flank), entrana (skirt steak), chorizo (sausage), morcilla (blood sausage)
Wood or charcoal (lena -- wood is preferred for flavor)
Chimichurri (parsley, garlic, oregano, red pepper, olive oil, vinegar)
instructions: Asado is the Uruguayan (and Argentine) ritual of grilled beef
Uruguay has more cattle per capita than almost any country on earth
The asado is not just cooking -- it is a social event, an afternoon-long ritual
The asador (the person who grills) controls the fire, the timing, and the order of meats
The parrilla (grill) uses wood or charcoal -- gas is unacceptable for asado purists
The meat is seasoned only with coarse salt -- nothing else
The order: chorizos and morcilla first (appetizer), then the beef cuts
Chimichurri on the side -- the Argentine-Uruguayan herb sauce
The asado is the Sunday family gathering -- every week, rain or shine

recipes.name: Chivito
recipes.description: Uruguayan national steak sandwich -- chivito, a thin beef steak with ham, bacon, mozzarella, fried egg, lettuce, tomato, olives, and mayo in a firm roll. Named "little goat" though it never contained goat (invented when a restaurant ran out of goat). Invented in Punta del Este, 1940s. Served with fries.
ingredients: Bread roll (a firm roll that can hold the weight)
instructions: The chivito is Uruguay's national sandwich -- and it is enormous
A thin steak with ham, bacon, mozzarella, fried egg, lettuce, tomato, olives, and mayo
All stacked in a bread roll -- the roll must be firm enough to hold everything
Invented in Punta del Este in the 1940s -- a customer asked for goat (chivito) but the restaurant didn't have any, so they improvised with steak
Named chivito (little goat) even though it has never contained goat
Served with fries on the side
The Uruguayan answer to a burger -- but much more loaded

recipes.name: Empanadas
recipes.description: Uruguayan baked meat pastries -- empanadas, ground beef with onion, cumin, olives, and hard-boiled egg in a flour pastry. The repulgue (edge crimp) is each cook's signature. Typically baked (not fried). Eaten before asado or as a quick lunch.
ingredients: Filling: ground beef (carne) with onion, bell pepper, cumin, paprika, olives, hard-boiled egg
Or: ham and cheese, or spinach and cheese
instructions: Uruguayan empanadas are baked (not fried like Argentine empanadas, usually)
The meat filling: ground beef with onion, cumin, olives, and hard-boiled egg
The repulgue (edge crimp): each region and each cook has their own style
Eaten as a lunch, snack, or appetizer before asado
Sold at every bakery and supermarket

recipes.name: Milanesa
recipes.description: Uruguayan breaded cutlet -- milanesa, thin beef or chicken pounded, breaded, and fried (Italian Milanese heritage via River Plate immigration). Eaten with lemon. Milanesa a la napolitana: topped with tomato sauce, ham, and melted mozzarella. Every Uruguayan eats milanesa weekly.
ingredients: Milanesa a la napolitana: tomato sauce, ham, and mozzarella melted on top
instructions: Milanesa is the Rioplatense breaded cutlet -- from the Italian Milanese tradition
Italian immigrants brought the cotoletta alla milanese to the River Plate
Pounded thin, breaded, and fried in oil
Eaten with lemon squeezed on top
Milanesa a la napolitana: with tomato sauce, ham, and melted cheese on top -- a hybrid
Milanesa a caballo: with fried eggs on top (a caballo = on horseback)
Every Uruguayan eats milanesa weekly -- it is the everyday comfort food

recipes.name: Guiso de Lentejas
recipes.description: Uruguayan hearty lentil stew -- lentils with chorizo colorado (cured red sausage for smoky depth), potato, carrot, and tomato. A winter comfort food. Spanish and Italian immigrant influence on Rioplatense home cooking.
instructions: Guiso de lentejas is the Uruguayan homestyle lentil stew
A hearty one-pot stew with lentils, vegetables, and chorizo
The chorizo colorado (red-cured sausage) gives it a smoky-spiced depth
A winter comfort food
Spanish and Italian immigrant influence on Rioplatense home cooking

recipes.name: Parrillada
recipes.description: Uruguayan mixed grill platter -- curated selection of beef cuts, fresh chorizo, morcilla (blood sausage), molleja (sweetbreads: crispy outside, creamy inside), and provoleta (provolone grilled on the parrilla until bubbly). The Rioplatense nose-to-tail tradition. Served at parrilla restaurants.

Morcilla (blood sausage with rice or onion filling)

Includes a selection of beef cuts, offal (sweetbreads, kidneys), sausages, and provoleta
Provoleta: a disc of provolone cheese grilled directly on the parrilla until bubbly and charred underneath
Sweetbreads (molleja): prized in River Plate cuisine -- crispy outside, creamy inside
The Rioplatense tradition of eating all parts of the animal -- nose to tail

recipes.name: Pascualina
recipes.description: Uruguayan Italian-heritage spinach pie -- pascualina, puff pastry shell filled with spinach and ricotta, whole hard-boiled eggs embedded (cross-section visible when sliced). From Genoese torta pasqualina (Easter tradition). Genoese immigrants brought it to the River Plate. Now year-round.

Hard-boiled eggs (whole, embedded in the filling)
instructions: Pascualina is the Uruguayan spinach pie -- Italian heritage (torta pasqualina from Genoa)
A deep pie with spinach and ricotta, whole hard-boiled eggs nested inside
When sliced, each slice reveals a cross-section of the embedded egg

Genoese immigrants (many came to the River Plate) brought the tradition
Now eaten year-round as a main course or lunch

recipes.name: Buseca
recipes.description: Uruguayan Italian-heritage tripe stew -- buseca, tripe slow-cooked with white beans, chorizo colorado, and vegetables. From Milanese busecca. Rich and hearty, eaten on cold winter nights.
instructions: Buseca is the Uruguayan tripe stew -- Italian heritage (busecca from Milan)
Tripe slow-cooked with white beans, chorizo, and vegetables
A rich, hearty winter stew
Eaten at home on cold nights
The Milanese Italian community brought the tradition

recipes.name: Tallarines con Tuco
recipes.full_name: Tallarines con Tuco (Pasta with Meat Sauce)
recipes.description: Uruguayan Italian-heritage pasta -- tallarines (flat noodles) with tuco (slow-cooked meat and tomato sauce, from Italian sugo). Generous parmesan. Tuco is the Rioplatense word for a slow-cooked meat and tomato sauce
From the Italian sugo/tuco
Italian immigration to Uruguay was massive -- shaping the cuisine fundamentally
Between 1860-1920, hundreds of thousands of Italians (mostly from Genoa, Calabria, Naples) settled in Montevideo
This is everyday home cooking -- not fancy, but foundational

recipes.name: Faina
recipes.description: Uruguayan chickpea flatbread -- faina (from Genoese farinata), chickpea flour baked thin and crispy. In Uruguay: eaten ON TOP of pizza -- a slice of faina placed on a pizza slice. The pizza-faina combination is uniquely Rioplatense. Sold at every Montevideo pizzeria.

Thin, slightly crispy on top, creamy inside
In Uruguay: faina is eaten ON TOP of pizza -- a slice of faina placed on a slice of pizza
The pizza-faina combination is uniquely Rioplatense -- nowhere else combines them
Sold at every pizzeria in Montevideo

recipes.name: Alfajor
recipes.description: Uruguayan dulce de leche sandwich cookies -- alfajores, two soft shortbread cookies with dulce de leche (slow-caramelized milk) between, coated in chocolate or powdered sugar. From Spanish (Arab origin al-hasu), adapted in South America. Portezuelo is the Uruguayan brand. National snack.

instructions: Alfajores are the River Plate cookie sandwich -- dulce de leche between two soft cookies
Dulce de leche: milk and sugar cooked slowly until caramelized -- the Rioplatense sweet staple
Alfajor brands (Portezuelo in Uruguay) are national pride
Chocolate-coated or dusted in powdered sugar or coconut
Eaten as a snack, dessert, or with mate and coffee
The alfajor came from Spain (Arab origin al-hasu) and was adapted in South America

recipes.name: Chorizo al Pan

instructions: Choripan is the River Plate grilled sausage sandwich
A fresh chorizo grilled on the parrilla, placed in a crusty roll
Chimichurri or salsa criolla on top
The appetizer before asado -- or a stand-alone street food

recipes.name: Tarta de Jamon y Queso

Baked until golden

recipes.name: Martin Fierro
recipes.description: Uruguayan cheese and quince paste pairing -- Martin Fierro, named after the gaucho epic poem (1872). A slice of semi-hard cheese with a slice of dulce de membrillo (quince paste). Sweet-savory-tart. The gaucho tradition: simple food of the pampa.

Dulce de membrillo (quince paste -- firm, dark, sweet-tart)

A slice of cheese placed on a slice of quince paste

recipes.name: Dulce de Leche
recipes.description: Rioplatense caramelized milk -- dulce de leche, whole milk and sugar slow-cooked for 1-2 hours until Maillard-browned to deep amber. Thick, spreadable, intensely sweet. recipes.name: Chaja

instructions: Chaja is the signature Uruguayan cake -- from the city of Paysandu

Layers of sponge cake, dulce de leche, whipped cream, crushed meringue, and peaches
Light, airy, and indulgent

recipes.name: Postre Chaja -- Flan con Dulce
